160.e: Gempolishers, potters, weaponsmiths, weavers, makers of adornments with peacock feathers, sawyers, makers of artificial ornaments, perforators of shells and ornaments, ivoryworkers, whitewashers, purveyors of fragrant essences, renowned goldsmiths, blanketcleaners, hotbath attendants, physicians, vintners, incense merchants, washermen, tailors, headmen of villages and hamlets, actors along with their wives, fishermen -- all followed Bharata.

160.sa: मणिकाराश्च ये केचित्कुम्भकाराश्च शोभनाः। सूत्रकर्मकृतश्चैव ये च शस्त्रोपजीविनः।2.83.12।। मयूरकाः क्राकचिका रोचका वेधकास्तथा। दन्तकारा स्सुधाकारा स्तथा गन्धोपजीविनः।।2.83.13।। सुवर्णकाराः प्रख्यातास्तथा कम्बलधावकाः। स्नापकोष्णोदका वैद्याधूपकाश्शौण्डिकास्तथा।।2.83.14।। रजकास्तुन्नवायाश्च ग्रामघोषमहत्तराः। शैलूषाश्च सह स्त्रीभिर्ययुः कैवर्तकास्तथा।।2.83.15।।
160.e: Gempolishers, potters, weaponsmiths, weavers, makers of adornments with peacock feathers, sawyers, makers of artificial ornaments, perforators of shells and ornaments, ivoryworkers, whitewashers, purveyors of fragrant essences, renowned goldsmiths, blanketcleaners, hotbath attendants, physicians, vintners, incense merchants, washermen, tailors, headmen of villages and hamlets, actors along with their wives, fishermen -- all followed Bharata.

160.sa: मणिकाराश्च ये केचित्कुम्भकाराश्च शोभनाः। सूत्रकर्मकृतश्चैव ये च शस्त्रोपजीविनः।2.83.12।। मयूरकाः क्राकचिका रोचका वेधकास्तथा। दन्तकारा स्सुधाकारा स्तथा गन्धोपजीविनः।।2.83.13।। सुवर्णकाराः प्रख्यातास्तथा कम्बलधावकाः। स्नापकोष्णोदका वैद्याधूपकाश्शौण्डिकास्तथा।।2.83.14।। रजकास्तुन्नवायाश्च ग्रामघोषमहत्तराः। शैलूषाश्च सह स्त्रीभिर्ययुः कैवर्तकास्तथा।।2.83.15।।
160.e: Gempolishers, potters, weaponsmiths, weavers, makers of adornments with peacock feathers, sawyers, makers of artificial ornaments, perforators of shells and ornaments, ivoryworkers, whitewashers, purveyors of fragrant essences, renowned goldsmiths, blanketcleaners, hotbath attendants, physicians, vintners, incense merchants, washermen, tailors, headmen of villages and hamlets, actors along with their wives, fishermen -- all followed Bharata.

160.sa: समाहिता वेदविदो ब्राह्मणा वृत्तसम्मताः। गोरथैर्भरतं यान्तमनुजग्मु स्सहस्रशः।।2.83.16।।
160.e: Brahmins learned in the Vedas and renowned for their virtuous conduct followed Bharta in their thousands on bullock carts with composed minds.

160.sa: सुवेषा श्शुद्धवसनास्ताम्रमृष्टानुलेपनाः। सर्वे ते विविधैर्यानै श्शनैर्भरतमन्वयुः।।2.83.17।।
160.e: Dressed well in clean clothes and anointed with pure red sandalpaste, they all slowly followed Bharata, mounting on various vehicles.

160.sa: प्रहृष्टमुदिता सेना साऽन्वयात्कैकयीसुतम्। भ्रातुरानयने यान्तं भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्।।2.83.18।।
160.e: The army, overwhelmed with joy and cheer followed the devoted brother Bharata who had set out to bring back Rama.

160.sa: ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं रथयानाश्वकुञ्जरैः। समासेदुस्ततो गङ्गां शृङ्गीबेरपुरं प्रति।।2.83.19।। यत्र रामसखो वीरो गुहो ज्ञातिगणैर्वृतः। निवसत्यप्रमादेन देशं तं परिपालयन्।।2.83.20।।
160.e: After travelling a long distance on chariots, carriages, horses and elephants, they reached the river Ganga close to Srngiberapura, a country ruled vigilantly by Rama's friend, the valiant Guha who lived there along with his relatives.

160.sa: ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं रथयानाश्वकुञ्जरैः। समासेदुस्ततो गङ्गां शृङ्गीबेरपुरं प्रति।।2.83.19।। यत्र रामसखो वीरो गुहो ज्ञातिगणैर्वृतः। निवसत्यप्रमादेन देशं तं परिपालयन्।।2.83.20।।
160.e: After travelling a long distance on chariots, carriages, horses and elephants, they reached the river Ganga close to Srngiberapura, a country ruled vigilantly by Rama's friend, the valiant Guha who lived there along with his relatives.

160.sa: उपेत्य तीरं गङ्गायाश्चक्रवाकैरलङ्कृतम्। व्यवातिष्ठत सा सेना भरतस्यानुयायिनी।।2.83.21।।
160.e: The army following Bharata reached the bank of the river Ganga, graced by chakravakas (ruddy geese) and halted there.

160.sa: निरीक्ष्यानुगतां सेनां तां च गङ्गां शिवोदकाम्। भरतस्सचिवान्सर्वानब्रवीद्वाक्यकोविदः।।2.83.22।।
160.e: As he beheld the army following him and the river Ganga of sacred waters in front of him, Bharata who was proficient in speech said to his ministers:

160.sa: निवेशयत मे सैन्यमभिप्रायेण सर्वतः। विश्रान्ताः प्रतरिष्यामश्श्व इदानीमिमां नदीम्।।2.83.23।।
160.e: You may, according to your convenience, halt the army anywhere here and, after taking rest (for the night), we shall cross the river Ganga tomorrow.

160.sa: दातुं च तावदिच्छामि स्वर्गतस्य महीपतेः। और्ध्वदेहनिमित्तार्थमवतीर्योदकं नदीम्।।2.83.24।।
160.e: Meanwhile, I shall get into this river and offer libations with water to the departed king for the good of his life in the other world.

160.sa: तस्यैवं ब्रुवतोऽमात्यास्तथेत्युक्त्वा समाहिताः। न्यवेशयंस्तां छन्देन स्वेन स्वेन पृथक्पृथक्।।2.83.25।।
160.e: While he (Bharata's) was speaking this way, all the ministers assented by saying 'Be it so' and made arrangement for their troops to rest separately according to their pleasure.

160.sa: निवेश्य गङ्गामनु तां महानदीं चमूं विधानैः परिबर्हशोभिनीम्। उवास रामस्य तदा महात्मनो विचिन्तयानो भरतो निवर्तनम्।।2.83.26।।
160.e: The army encamped by Bharata looked splendid with royal insigaia. After making necessary arrangements for the army on the bank of the mighty river Ganga and pondering over the means of bringing back the magnanimous Rama, Bharata stayed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्र्यशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightythird sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

161.sa: ततो निविष्टां ध्वजिनीं गङ्गामन्वाश्रितां नदीम्। निषादराजो दृष्ट्वैव ज्ञातीन्सन्त्वरितोऽऽब्रवीत्।।2.84.1।।
161.e: Guha, king of the nishadas, observed the bannered army encamped all along the bank of the river Ganga, hurried off and said to his kinsmen:

161.sa: महतीयमितस्सेना सागराभा प्रदृश्यते। नास्यान्तमधिगच्छामि मनसापि विचिन्तयन्।।2.84.2।।
161.e: Here is an army as vast as the ocean, and I am unable to comprehend its magnitude even mentally.

161.sa: यथा तु खलु दुर्बुद्धिर्भरत स्स्वयमागतः। स एष हि महाकायः कोविदारध्वजो रथे।।2.84.3।।
161.e: It appears that the evilminded Bharata himself has come here. The emblem of a huge kovidara (pomegranate) tree is seen on his chariot.

161.sa: बन्धयिष्यति वा दाशानथवाऽस्मान्वधिष्यति। अथ दाशरथिं रामं पित्रा राज्याद्विवासितम्।।2.84.4।। सम्पन्नां श्रियमन्विच्छन्स्तस्य राज्ञ स्सुदुर्लभाम्। भरतः कैकयीपुत्रो हन्तुं समधिगच्छति।।2.84.5।।
161.e: Could it be that Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, has come here to bind us with the cords or to slay us? Or is he marching forward with the intention of taking possession of a prosperous, rare kingdom by slaying Rama who has been banished by his father:

161.sa: बन्धयिष्यति वा दाशानथवाऽस्मान्वधिष्यति। अथ दाशरथिं रामं पित्रा राज्याद्विवासितम्।।2.84.4।। सम्पन्नां श्रियमन्विच्छन्स्तस्य राज्ञ स्सुदुर्लभाम्। भरतः कैकयीपुत्रो हन्तुं समधिगच्छति।।2.84.5।।
161.e: Could it be that Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, has come here to bind us with the cords or to slay us? Or is he marching forward with the intention of taking possession of a prosperous, rare kingdom by slaying Rama who has been banished by his father:

161.sa: भर्ताचैव सखाचैव रामो दाशरथिर्मम। तस्यार्थकामास्सन्नद्धा गङ्गाऽनूपे प्रतिष्ठत।।2.84.6।।
161.e: Rama, son of Dasaratha, is not only my master but also my friend. Therefore, to safeguard his interests remain stationed here on the bank of the river Ganga.

161.sa: तिष्ठन्तु सर्वे दाशाश्च गङ्गामन्वाश्रिता नदीम्। बलयुक्ता नदीरक्षा मांसमूलफलाशनाः।।2.84.7।।
161.e: Let all the fishermen, who live on meat, roots and fruits and protect the river, stay here with the troops by taking up positions along the banks of the river Ganga.

161.sa: नावां शतानां पञ्चानां कैवर्तानां शतं शतम्। सन्नद्धानां तथा यूनां तिष्ठन्त्वित्यभ्यचोदयत्।।2.84.8।।
161.e: Let five hundred boats, each manned by a hundred young fishermen fully equipped, be in readiness he exhorted them.

161.sa: यदाऽऽदुष्टस्तु भरतो रामस्येह भविष्यति। सेयं स्वस्तिमती सेना गङ्गामद्य तरिष्यति।।2.84.9।।
161.e: Should it happen that Bharata is not illdisposed toward Rama, the army will safe cross the river Ganga today itself.

161.sa: इत्युक्त्वोपायनं गृह्य मत्स्यमांसमधूनि च। अभिचक्राम भरतं निषादाधिपतिर्गुहः।।2.84.10।।
161.e: Having spoken thus, Guha, lord of the nishadas, approached Bharata, taking with him fish, meat and wine as offerings.

161.sa: तमायान्तं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। भरतायाऽचचक्षेऽथ विनयज्ञो विनीतवत्।।2.84.11।।
161.e: The valiant Sumantra, conversant with ways of modesty, observed Guha approaching them and humbly informed Bharata.

161.sa: एष ज्ञातिसहस्रेण स्थपतिः परिवारितः। कुशलो दण्डकारण्ये वृद्धो भ्रातुश्च ते सखा।।2.84.12।।
161.e: Guha who has come here surrounded by too many thousands of his relations is fully acquainted with the Dandaka forest. He is an aged man and a friend of your brother said Sumatra.

161.sa: तस्मात्पश्यतु काकुत्स्थ त्वां निषादाधिपो गुहः। असंशयं विजानीते यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।2.84.13।।
161.e: O scion of the Kakusthas (Bharata) therefore, give audience to the overlord of the nishadas, Guha, who undoubtedly knows the whereabouts of Rama and Lakshmana.

161.sa: एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुमन्त्राद्भरत श्शुभम्। उवाच वचनं शीघ्रं गुहः पश्यतु मामिति।।2.84.14।।
161.e: On hearing these auspicious words of Sumantra, Bharata said Let Guha see me at once.

161.sa: लब्ध्वाऽभ्यनुज्ञां संहृष्टो ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। आगम्य भरतं प्रह्वो गुहो वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.84.15।।
161.e: Having obtaind the permission, a delighted Guha, escorted by his relatives,  approached Bharata and humbly said:

161.sa: निष्कुटश्चैव देशोऽयं वञ्चिताश्चापि ते वयम्। निवेदयामस्ते सर्वे स्वके दासकुले वस।।2.84.16।।
161.e: This country is like a pleasuregarden at the backyard of your palace. All of us are  subordinate to you and we solicit you to stay in the house of  this servant of yours.

161.sa: अस्ति मूलं फलञ्चैव निषादैस्समुपाहृतम्। आर्द्रं च मांसं शुष्कं च वन्यं चोच्चावचं महत्।।2.84.17।।
161.e: Here are roots, fruits and a great variety of forest produce, fresh and dried meat brought by the nishadas.

161.sa: आशंसे स्वाशिता सेना वत्स्यतीमां विभावरीम्। अर्चितो विविधैः कामै श्श्व स्ससैन्यो गमिष्यसि।।2.84.18।।
161.e: We hope your army having  refreshed themselves will spend the night here. With our hospitality extended, you can proceed tomorrow. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुरशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

162.sa: एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्। प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंहितम्।।2.85.1।।
162.e: When thus spoken to, Bharata, a great intellectual, replied to Guha with these well thought out and meaningful words.

162.sa: ऊर्जितः खलु ते कामः कृतो मम गुरोस्सखे। यो मे त्वमीदृशीं सेनामेकोऽभ्यर्चितुमिच्छसि।।2.85.2।।
162.e: O dear friend of my elder brother, your desire to extend hospitality to this large army all alone is indeed noble.

162.sa: इत्युक्त्वा तु महातेजा गुहं वचनमुत्तमम्। अब्रवीद्भरत श्श्रीमाननिषादाधिपतिं पुनः।।2.85.3।।
162.e: Having spoken to Guha courteously, the majestic, radiant Bharata continued:

162.sa: कतरेण गमिष्यामि भरद्वाजाश्रमं गुह। गहनोऽयं भृशं देशो गङ्गाऽनूपो दुरत्ययः।।2.85.4।।
162.e: O Guha this region of Ganga with its dense forest is very difficult to cross. How can I reach the hermitage of Bharadwaja?

162.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं गुहो गहनगोचरः।।2.85.5।।
162.e: When he heard those words of the sagacious Bharata, Guha the forest ranger answered him reverentially with folded palms.

162.sa: दाशास्त्वाऽनुऽगमिष्यन्ति धन्विनस्सुसमाहिताः। अहं त्वानुगमिष्यामि राजपुत्र महायशः।।2.85.6।।
162.e: O prince of great renown I shall follow you, wellprepared with these fishermen, armed with bows.

162.sa: कच्छिन्नदुष्टो व्रजसि रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। इयं ते महती सेना शङ्कां जनयतीव मे।।2.85.7।।
162.e: Are you not going to that place with the evil intention of causing harm to Rama of unwearied actions? This large army of yours arouses doubts in me.

162.sa: तमेवमभिभाषन्तमाकाश इव निर्मलः। भरतश्श्लक्ष्णया वाचा गुहं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.85.8।।
162.e: When he heard Guha thus speaking, Bharata who was as tranquil as the sky, said to him in a gentle voice.

162.sa: माभूत्स कालो यत्कष्टं न मां शङ्कितुमर्हसि। राघव स्सहि मे भ्राता ज्येष्ठः पितुसमो मतः।।2.85.9।।
162.e: That calmitous time will never come (again). You should not suspect me. I look upon Rama, my eldest brother, as my father.

162.sa: तं निवर्तयितुं यामि काकुत्स्थं वनवासिनम्। बुद्धिरन्या न ते कार्या गुह सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते।।2.85.10।।
162.e: I am going to bring back that scion of the kakutsthas (Rama) who resides in the forest. O Guha, do not entertain any other thought. I am tellng you the truth.

162.sa: स तु संहृष्टवदन श्श्रुत्वा भरतभाषितम्। पुनरेवाब्रवीद्वाक्यं भरतं प्रति हर्षितः।।2.85.11।।
162.e: When he heard those words of Bharata, Guha was delighted and his face beamed with joy as he said to Bharata:

162.sa: धन्यस्त्वं न त्वया तुल्यं पश्यामि जगतीतले। अयत्नादागतं राज्यं यस्त्वं त्यक्तुमिहेच्छसि।।2.85.12।।
162.e: Blessed indeed you are as you desire to renounce the kingdom that has come to you effortlessly. I see none equal to you on this earth.

162.sa: शाश्वती खलु ते कीर्तिर्लोकाननुचरिष्यति। यस्त्वं कृच्छ्रगतं रामं प्रत्यानयितुमिच्छसि।।2.85.13।।
162.e: You desire to bring back Rama who is in great difficulty. This everlasting fame of yours will spread all over the world.

162.sa: एवं सम्भाषमाणस्य गुहस्य भरतं तदा। बभौ नष्टप्रभस्सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत।।2.85.14।।
162.e: As Guha was thus conversing with Bharata, the rays of the Sun diminished and the night set in.

162.sa: सन्निवेश्य स तां सेनां गुहेन परितोषितः। शत्रुघ्नेन सह श्रीमाञ्छयनं समुपागमत्।।2.85.15।।
162.e: Fortunate Bharata gratified by Guha encamped his army and retired to bed along with Satrughna.

162.sa: रामचिन्तामय श्शोको भरतस्य महात्मनः। उपस्थितो ह्यनर्हस्य धर्मप्रेक्षस्य तादृशः।।2.85.16।।
162.e: But the thought of Rama caused grief to the magnanimous Bharata, a man of righteous outlook who did not deserve such grief.

162.sa: अन्तर्दाहेन दहनस्सन्तापयति राघवम्। वनदाहाभिसन्तप्तं गूढोऽग्निरिव पादपम्।।2.85.17।।
162.e: Just like a concealed forestfire scorching the dried up forest, the fire of sorrow kindled in his mind scorched Bharata.

162.sa: प्रसृतस्सर्वगात्रेभ्यस्स्वेदं शोकाग्निसम्भवम्। यथा सूर्यांशुसन्तप्तो हिमवान् प्रसृतोहिमम्।।2.85.18।।
162.e: Like the ice melted by the heat of the Sun's rays flows down the Himalayas, sweat poured from all parts of his body caused by the fire of grief.

162.sa: ध्याननिर्धरशैलेन विनिश्श्वसितधातुना। दैन्यपादपसंघेन शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा।।2.85.19।। प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन सन्तापौषधिवेणुना। आक्रान्तो दुःखशैलेन महता कैकयीसुतः।।2.85.20।।
162.e: Bharata, son of Kaikeyi was stricken by a lofty mountain of grief. The cavityless rocks of that mountain were his contemplation, the minerals were his sighs, the multitude of trees were his desolation, peaks were his fatigue and mental distress, the unlimited number of animals were his stupor, the bamboo tree was his sorrow.

162.sa: ध्याननिर्धरशैलेन विनिश्श्वसितधातुना। दैन्यपादपसंघेन शोकायासाधिशृङ्गिणा।।2.85.19।। प्रमोहानन्तसत्त्वेन सन्तापौषधिवेणुना। आक्रान्तो दुःखशैलेन महता कैकयीसुतः।।2.85.20।।
162.e: Bharata, son of Kaikeyi was stricken by a lofty mountain of grief. The cavityless rocks of that mountain were his contemplation, the minerals were his sighs, the multitude of trees were his desolation, peaks were his fatigue and mental distress, the unlimited number of animals were his stupor, the bamboo tree was his sorrow.

162.sa: विनिश्श्वसन्वै भृशदुर्मनास्ततः प्रमूढसंज्ञः परमापदं गतः। शमं न लेभे हृदयज्वरार्दितो नरर्षभो यूथहतो यथर्षभः।।2.85.21।।
162.e: Then best of men, Bharata, with highly distraught mind and heaving sighs, with senses bewildered and oppressed by the fever raging in his heart and caught in a great calamity, like a bull separated from the herd enjoyed no peace of mind.

162.sa: गुहेन सार्धं भरतस्समागतो महानुभावस्सजनस्समाहितः। सुदुर्मनास्तं भरतं तदा पुनर्गुह स्समाश्वासयदग्रजं प्रति।।2.85.22।।
162.e: Bharata, a man of great magnanimity, joined Guha together with his people with composed mind. Then Guha, greatly distraught, again consoled  Bharata  regarding his elder brother Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

163.sa: आचचक्षेऽथ सद्भावं लक्ष्मणस्य महात्मनः। भरतायाप्रमेयाय गुहो गहनगोचरः।।2.86.1।।
163.e: Then Guha, the forest ranger, described to Bharata the countless qualities of the goodnatured, magnanimous Lakshmana:

163.sa: तं जाग्रतं गुणैर्युक्तं शरचापासिधारिणम्। भ्रातृगुप्त्यर्थमत्यन्तमहं लक्ष्मणमबृवम्।।2.86.2।।
163.e: I spoke to the virtuous Lakshmana, who was holding arrows, bow and sword in his hand and keeping awake completely for the protection of his brother.

163.sa: इयं तात सुखा शय्या त्वदर्थमुपकल्पिता। प्रत्याश्वसिहि शेष्वास्यां सुखं राघवनन्दन।।2.86.3।।
163.e: My friend, Lakshmana, the delight of the Raghavas this comfortable couch has been arranged for you. Lie down peacefully without any anxiety.

163.sa: उचितोऽयं जनस्सर्वो दुःखानां त्वं सुखोचितः। धर्मात्मंस्तस्य गुप्त्यर्थं जागरिष्यामहे वयम्।।2.86.4।।
163.e: O righteous one you are used to conforts where as all of our people are accustomed to hardships. So we will stay awake and protect Rama.

163.sa: नहि रामात्प्रियतरो ममास्ति भुवि कश्चन। मोत्सुकोऽभूर्ब्रवीम्येतदप्यसत्यं तवाग्रतः।।2.86.5।।
163.e: To me, there is none on earth dearer than Rama. Do not have any anxiety. I am telling you the truth.

163.sa: अस्य प्रसादादाशंसे लोकेऽस्मिन् सुमहद्यशः। धर्मावाप्तिं च विपुलामर्थकामौ च केवलम्।।2.86.6।।
163.e: By the grace of Rama, I want to acquire in this world great renown, abundance of righteousness, absolute artha (prosperity) and kama (pleasure).

163.sa: सोऽहं प्रियसखं रामं शयानं सह सीतया। रक्षिष्यामि धनुष्पाणि स्सर्वै स्स्वैर्ज्ञातिभिस्सह।।2.86.7।।
163.e: As for me, bow in hand and all my kinsmen with me, I shall protect my dear friend Rama who is resting with Sita.

163.sa: न हि मेऽविदितं किञ्चिद्वनेऽस्मिंश्चरत स्सदा। चतुरङ्गं ह्यपि बलं प्रसहेम वयं युधि।।2.86.8।।
163.e: Nothing is unknown to me in this forest in which I range about continually. We can withstand an army of four divisions in a battle.

163.sa: एवमस्माभिरुक्तेन लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। अनुनीता वयं सर्वे धर्ममेवानुपश्यता।। 2.86.9।।
163.e: The magnanimous Lakshmana, established in dharma, replied:

163.sa: कथं दाशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया। शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुं जीवितं वा सुखानि वा।।2.86.10।।
163.e: While Rama sleep on the ground with Sita, how can I find sleep or joy or comfort?

163.sa: यो न देवासुरैस्सर्वैश्शक्यः प्रसहितुं युधि। तं पश्य गुह संविष्टं तृणेषु सह सीतया।।2.86.11।।
163.e: O Guha behold Rama, whom gods and demons combined cannot withstand in a battle now lying on a bed of grass with Sita.

163.sa: महता तपसा लब्धो विविधैश्च परिश्रमैः। एको दशरथस्यैष पुत्रस्सदृशलक्षणः।।2.86.12।।
163.e: Rama is the only one among the sons who resembles his father in various virtues. Dasaratha obtained him after a great deal of austerities and efforts as well.

163.sa: अस्मिन्प्रव्राजिते राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति। विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति।।2.86.13।।
163.e: After Rama is exiled, king Dasaratha will not survive for long and surely the earth will soon be widowed.

163.sa: विनद्य सुमहानादं श्रमेणोपरताः स्त्रियः। निर्घोषो विरतो नूनमध्य राजनिवेशने।।2.86.14।।
163.e: The women of the inner apartment who lamented loudly, must have stopped weeping out of weariness. By now, the clamour in the king's palace would have surely subsided.

163.sa: कौसल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम। नाशंसे यदि जीवेयुस्सर्वे ते शर्वरीमिमाम्।।2.86.15।।
163.e: I doubt whether the king, Kausalya and my mother Sumitra and the rest of them will outlive this night.

163.sa: जीवेदपि च मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्यान्ववेक्षया। दुःखिता या तु कौसल्या वीरसूर्विनशिष्यति।।2.86.16।।
163.e: My mother might live, looking at Satrughna. But Kausalya, who is the mother of a hero, will die from extreme grief.

163.sa: अतिक्रान्तमतिक्रान्तमनवाप्य मनोरथम्। राज्ये राममनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति।।2.86.17।।
163.e: My father, king Dasaratha, failing to fulfil his cherished desires one after another and unable to place Rama on the throne, will pass away.

163.sa: सिद्धार्थाः पितरं वृत्तं तस्मिन्काले ह्युपस्थिते। प्रेतकार्येषु सर्वेषु संस्करिष्यन्ति भूमिपम्।।2.86.18।।
163.e: When the moment of death arrives for my father, those who perform the funeral rites for him would have fulfilled their desire.

163.sa: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादम्पन्नां सर्वरत्नविभूषिताम्।।2.86.19।। गजाश्वरथसंबाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसंपूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.86.20।। आरामोद्यानसंपूर्णां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.86.21।।
163.e: There in the capital of my father with its lovely crossroads and squares, welllaid  highways, full of mansions and palaces encrusted with all kinds of precious stones, teeming with elephants, horses and chariots, resounding with trumpets, and with wellbeing everywhere, and plenty of pleasuregardens, and parks and community festivals, people sound in health would be moving about in great comfort.

163.sa: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादम्पन्नां सर्वरत्नविभूषिताम्।।2.86.19।। गजाश्वरथसंबाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसंपूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.86.20।। आरामोद्यानसंपूर्णां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.86.21।।
163.e: There in the capital of my father with its lovely crossroads and squares, welllaid  highways, full of mansions and palaces encrusted with all kinds of precious stones, teeming with elephants, horses and chariots, resounding with trumpets, and with wellbeing everywhere, and plenty of pleasuregardens, and parks and community festivals, people sound in health would be moving about in great comfort.

163.sa: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादम्पन्नां सर्वरत्नविभूषिताम्।।2.86.19।। गजाश्वरथसंबाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसंपूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.86.20।। आरामोद्यानसंपूर्णां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.86.21।।
163.e: There in the capital of my father with its lovely crossroads and squares, welllaid  highways, full of mansions and palaces encrusted with all kinds of precious stones, teeming with elephants, horses and chariots, resounding with trumpets, and with wellbeing everywhere, and plenty of pleasuregardens, and parks and community festivals, people sound in health would be moving about in great comfort.

163.sa: अपिसत्यप्रतिज्ञेन सार्धं कुशलिना वयं। निवृत्ते समये ह्यस्मिन् सुखिताः प्रविशेमहि।।2.86.22।।
163.e: Can we ever reenter Ayodhya happily after safely fulfilling the vow and completing the term of exile?

163.sa: परिदेवयमानस्य तस्यैवं सुमहात्मनः। तिष्ठतो राजपुत्रस्य शर्वरी साऽत्यवर्तत।।2.86.23।।
163.e: While the highminded prince was lamenting this way and was waiting, the night passed off.

163.sa: प्रभाते विमले सूर्ये कारयित्वा जटा उभौ। अस्मिन् भागीरथीतीरे सुखं सन्तारितौ मया।।2.86.24।।
163.e: The next morning when the Sun shone bright, both of them matted their hair on the bank of the river Bhagirathi (Ganga) and I ferried them across comfortably.

163.sa: जटाधरौ तौ द्रुमचीरवाससौ महाबलौ कुञ्जरयूथपोपमौ। वरेषुचापासिधरौ परन्तपौ व्यपेक्षमाणौ सह सीतया गतौ।।2.86.25।।
163.e: Rama and Lakshmana, slayers of enemies, who are as strong as bull elephants, with their hair matted, wearing robes made of bark, armed with excellent bows, arrows and swords went along with Sita looking around (vigilantly). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षडशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightysixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

164.sa: गुहस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतो भृशमप्रियम्। ध्यानं जगाम तत्रैव यत्र तच्छ्रुतमप्रियम्।।2.87.1।।
164.e: Extremely unhappy over what he heard from Guha, Bharata was immersed in thought then and there.

164.sa: सुकुमारो महासत्त्वस्सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। पुण्डरीकविशालाक्ष स्तरुणः प्रियदर्शनः।।2.87.2।। प्रत्याश्वस्य मुहूर्तं तु कालं परमदुर्मनाः। पपात सहसा तोत्रैर्ह्यतिविद्ध इव द्विपः।।2.87.3।।
164.e: The delicate, youthful, highly energetic and mightyarmed Bharata of graceful appearance, with shoulders like that of a lion and wideeyed like lotus petals, recovered for a moment and with a mind deeply distressed fell down at once like an elephant smitten by a goad.

164.sa: सुकुमारो महासत्त्वस्सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। पुण्डरीकविशालाक्ष स्तरुणः प्रियदर्शनः।।2.87.2।। प्रत्याश्वस्य मुहूर्तं तु कालं परमदुर्मनाः। पपात सहसा तोत्रैर्ह्यतिविद्ध इव द्विपः।।2.87.3।।
164.e: The delicate, youthful, highly energetic and mightyarmed Bharata of graceful appearance, with shoulders like that of a lion and wideeyed like lotus petals, recovered for a moment and with a mind deeply distressed fell down at once like an elephant smitten by a goad.

164.sa: तदवस्थं तु भरतं शत्रुघ्नोऽनन्तरस्थितः। परिष्वज्य रुरोदोच्चैर्विसंज्ञश्शोककर्शितः।।2.87.4।।
164.e: Seeing Bharata in that state, Satrughna who was standing close by, smitten with grief clasped him, cried loudly and fell senseless.

164.sa: ततस्सर्वास्समापेतुर्मातरो भरतस्य ताः। उपवासकृशा दीना भर्तृव्यसनकर्शिताः।।2.87.5।।
164.e: Then Bharata's mothers, who were emaciated due to fasting and afflicted by the calamity of the death of their husband were desolate, rushed towards him.

164.sa: ताश्च तं पतितं भूमौ रुदन्त्यः पर्यवारयन्। कौसल्या त्वनुसृत्यैनं दुर्मनाः परिषस्वजे।।2.87.6।।
164.e: Sobbing, they gathered around Bharata who had fallen on the ground, while Kausalya approached him in a depressed state and took him into her arms.

164.sa: वत्सला स्वं यथा वत्समुपगूह्य तपस्विनी। परिपप्रच्छ भरतं रुदन्ती शोकलालसा।।2.87.7।।
164.e: Desolate Kausalya, in deep distress, clasped Bharata out of filial love as if he were her own child, wept and enquired of him:

164.sa: पुत्र व्याधिर्न ते कच्चिच्छरीरं परिबाधते। अद्य राजकुलस्यास्य त्वदधीनं हि जीवितम्।।2.87.8।।
164.e: O son I hope you are not affected by illness. Now the existence of this royal house devolves on you.

164.sa: त्वां दृष्ट्वा पुत्र जीवामि रामे सभ्रातृकेगते। वृत्ते दशरथे राज्ञि नाथ एकस्त्वमद्य नः।।2.87.9।।
164.e: O my son, with Rama gone to the forest along with your brother Lakshmana and with king Dasaratha departed from this world, I continue to live seeing you. From now on you alone are our sole protector.

164.sa: कच्चिन्न लक्ष्मणे पुत्र श्रुतं ते किंचदप्रियम्। पुत्रे वाऽप्येकपुत्राया स्सहभार्ये वनं गते।।2.87.10।।
164.e: O my son, I hope you have not heard any unpleasant news about Lakshmana or about my only son Rama who has gone to the forest along with his wife.

164.sa: स मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्य रुदन्नेव महायशाः। कौसल्यां परिसान्त्वेद्यं गुहं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.87.11।।
164.e: Highly renowned Bharata, composing himself for a moment and still weeping, reassured Kauslaya, and then said this to Guha:

164.sa: भ्राता मे क्वावसद्रात्रौ क्व सीता क्व च लक्ष्मणः। अस्वपच्छयने कस्मिन् किं भुक्त्वा गुह शंस मे।।2.87.12।।
164.e: O Guha where did my brother Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spend that night? What did they eat? On what couch did they sleep? Tell me all that.

164.sa: सोऽब्रवीद्भरतं हृष्टो निषादाधिपतिर्गुहः। यद्विधं प्रतिपेदे च रामे प्रियहितेऽतिथौ।।2.87.13।।
164.e: Thereupon delighted Guha, overlord of the nishadas, told Bharata all that he had provided to Rama, his beloved friend and guest:

164.sa: अन्नमुच्चावचं भक्षाः फलानि विविधानि च। रामायाभ्यवहारार्थं बहुचोपहृतं मया।।2.87.14।।
164.e: I offered Rama rice including a variety of eatables like fruits in great quantity for his food.

164.sa: तत्सर्वं प्रत्यनुज्ञासीद्राम स्सत्यपराक्रमः। न तु तत्प्रत्यगृह्णात्स क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्।।2.87.15।।
164.e: Rama whose prowess is his truth, acknowledged all that but remembering the duty enjoined on a kshatriya did not accept them.

164.sa: न ह्यस्माभिः प्रतिग्राह्यं सखे देयं तु सर्वदा। इति तेन वयं राजन्ननुनीता महात्मना।।2.87.16।।
164.e: O king that great Rama entreated us in a friendly manner by saying 'O friend we should always give to others but should never accept anything from others'.

164.sa: लक्ष्मणेन समानीतं पीत्वा वारि महायशाः। औपवास्यं तदाऽकार्षीद्राघवस्सह सीतया।।2.87.17।।
164.e: Illustrious Rama along with Sita only drank the water brought by Lakshamana and  undertook fasting.

164.sa: ततस्तु जलशेषेण लक्ष्मणोऽप्यकरोत्तदा। वाग्यतास्ते त्रय स्सन्ध्यां समुपासत संहिताः।।2.87.18।।
164.e: Thereafter Lakshmana also drank the remainder of water. Then all the three observing silence intently performed the evening worship.

164.sa: सौमित्रिस्तु ततः पश्चादकरोत्स्वास्तरं शुभम्। स्वयमानीय बर्हींषि क्षिप्रं राघवकारणात्।।2.87.19।।
164.e: Therafter, the son of Sumitra (Lakshmana) himself fetched darbha grass and quickly prepared an auspicious and comfortable bed for Rama.

164.sa: तस्मिन्समाविशद्राम स्स्वास्तरे सह सीतया। प्रक्षाल्य च तयोः पादावपचक्राम लक्ष्मणः।।2.87.20।।
164.e: Rama lay down upon the bed along with Sita. Thereafter Lakshmana, having washed their feet, moved to a distant place.

164.sa: एतत्तदिङ्गुदीमूलमिदमेव च तत्तृणम्। यस्मिन्रामश्च सीता च रात्रिं तां शयितावुभौ।।2.87.21।।
164.e: Here at the foot of the ingudi tree and upon that bed of grass both Rama and Sita rested that night.

164.sa: नियम्य पृष्ठे तु तलाङ्गुलित्रवान् शरैस्सुपूर्णाविषुधी परन्तपः। महाद्धनु स्सज्यमुपोह्य लक्ष्मणो निशामतिष्ठत्परितोऽस्य केवलम्।।2.87.22।।
164.e: Lakshmana, the scorcher of enemies, wearing protective covering for his palms and fingers (made of gohaskin), strapping on his back two quivers filled with arrows, holding a great bow, strung ready, stood sentinel throughout the night guarding the surrounding.

164.sa: तत स्त्वहंचोत्तमबाणचापधृत् स्थितोऽभवं तत्र स यत्र लक्ष्मणः। अतन्द्रितैर्ज्ञातिभिरात्तकार्मुकैर्महेन्द्रकल्पं परिपालयंस्तदा।।2.87.23।।
164.e: Then, holding the best of arrows and bow along with my indefatigable kinsmen similarly armed with bows, I stood by the side of Lakshmana guarding Rama who is comparable to Indra. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्ताशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

165.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा निपुणं सर्वं भरत स्सह मन्त्रिभिः। इङ्गुदीमूलमागम्य रामशय्यामवेक्ष्य ताम्।।2.88.1।। अब्रवीज्जननी स्सर्वा इह तेन महात्मना। शर्वरी शयिता भूमाविदमस्य विमर्दितम्।।2.88.2।।
165.e: After listening to all that Guha had said, Bharatha reached the foot of the ingudi tree accompanied by his ministers and gazing at Rama's bed, said to all his mothers the magnanimous Rama rested that night here on this ground in that crushed bed.

165.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा निपुणं सर्वं भरत स्सह मन्त्रिभिः। इङ्गुदीमूलमागम्य रामशय्यामवेक्ष्य ताम्।।2.88.1।। अब्रवीज्जननी स्सर्वा इह तेन महात्मना। शर्वरी शयिता भूमाविदमस्य विमर्दितम्।।2.88.2।।
165.e: After listening to all that Guha had said, Bharatha reached the foot of the ingudi tree accompanied by his ministers and gazing at Rama's bed, said to all his mothers the magnanimous Rama rested that night here on this ground in that crushed bed.

165.sa: महाभागकुलीनेन महाभागेन धीमता। जातो दशरथेनोर्व्यां न रामस्स्वप्तु मर्हति।।2.88.3।।
165.e: Rama, son of highly fortunate and sagacious Dasaratha, born of a noble lineage does not deserve to rest on this naked earth.

165.sa: अजिनोत्तरसंस्तीर्णे वरास्तरणसंचये। शयित्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रः कथं शेते महीतले।।2.88.4।।
165.e: How could Rama, the best among men used to a bed made of a pile of excellent spreads and overspread with deer skin, sleep on the bare ground?

165.sa: प्रासादाग्रविमानेषु वलभीषु च सर्वदा। हैमराजतभौमेषु वरास्तरणशालिषु।।2.88.5।। पुष्पसञ्चयचित्रेषु चन्दनागरुगन्धिषु। पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशेषु शुकसङ्घरूतेषुच।।2.88.6।। प्रासादवरवर्येषु शीतवत्सु सुगन्धिषु। उषित्वामेरुकल्पेषु कृतकाञ्चन भित्तिषु।।2.88.7।। गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषैर्वराभरणनिस्स्वनैः। मृदङ्गवरशब्दैश्च सततं प्रतिबोधितः।।2.88.8।। वन्दिभिर्वन्दितः काले बहुभि स्सूतमागधैः। गाथाभिरनुरूपाभि स्स्तुतिभिश्च परन्तपः।।2.88.9।।
165.e: Rama, scorcher of enemies, one who was accostomed to dwell in the attic of sevenstoreyed mansions with floors paved with gold, and silver, spread with excellent carpets, decked with bouquets of flowers and perfumed with sandal and agaru. The peaks of those palaces were bright like towering white clouds and echoed with cries of  parrots. They were cool and fragrant with perfumes. The marvellous palaces made of golden walls are comparable to mount Meru. He used to wake up to the sounds of songs and musical instruments, the tinkling of finest ornaments and the splendid sounds of the drums. Many bards, genealogists and panegyrists singing befitting ballads and extolling his virtues at appropriate time used to salute him in reverence (Bharata lamented).

165.sa: अश्रद्धेयमिदं लोके न सत्यं प्रतिभाति मा। मुह्यते खलु मे भाव स्स्वप्नोऽयमिति मे मतिः।।2.88.10।।
165.e: It is unbelievable that such a thing has happened to Rama in this world. It does not seem real to me and looks appears like a dream and my mind is bewildered.

165.sa: न नूनं दैवतं किंचित्कालेन बलवत्तरम्। यत्र दाशरथी रामो भूमावेव शयीत सः।।2.88.11।।
165.e: Dasaratha's son, Rama had to rest on the ground would admittedly mean that no divine power is mightier than Time (Destiny).

165.sa: विदेहराजस्य सुता सीता च प्रियदर्शना। दयिता शयिता भूमौ स्नुषा दशरथस्य च।।2.88.12।।
165.e: Sita, daughter of Janaka, king of Videha, and beloved daughterinlaw of Dasaratha who caused delight to the beholder, too had to rest on the bare ground.

165.sa: इयं शय्या मम भ्रातुरिदं हि परिवर्तितम्। स्थण्डिले कठिने सर्वं गात्रै र्विमृदितं तृणम्।।2.88.13।।
165.e: This is my brother's couch and it is here where he had tossed about. The grass spread on this hard surface is crushed by his limbs.

165.sa: मन्ये साभरणा सुप्ता सीताऽस्मिञ्छयनोत्तमे। तत्र तत्र हि दृश्यन्ते सक्ताः कनकबिन्दवः।।2.88.14।।
165.e: Some particles of gold dust are seen stuck to this bed here and there. I think Sita might have rested on this excellent bed with all her jewellery.

165.sa: उत्तरीयमिहाऽसक्तं सुव्यक्तं सीतया तदा। तथा ह्येते प्रकाशन्ते सक्ताः कौशेयतन्तवः।।2.88.15।।
165.e: That the upper garment of Sita might have been caught here is well evident from the shining silken threads stuck.

165.sa: मन्ये भर्तु स्सुखा शय्या येन बाला तपस्विनी। सुकुमारी सती दुःखं न हि विजानाति मैथिली।।2.88.16।।
165.e: Hapless Sita is young and delicate. Being a chaste lady, she, even in these (adverse) circumstances, does not feel the brunt. Hence, maybe she thinks her husbands' (hard) bed comfortable to her.

165.sa: हा हन्ताऽस्मि नृशंसोऽहं यत्सभार्यः कृते मम। ईदृशीं राघवश्शय्यामधिशेते ह्यनाथवत्।।2.88.17।।
165.e: Alas, what suffering Because of a cruel man like me Rama along with his spouse was condemned to recline upon such bed like an orphan.

165.sa: सार्वभौमकुले जात स्सर्वलोकस्य सम्मतः। सर्वलोकप्रियस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं सुखमनुत्तम्।।2.88.18।। कथमिन्दीवरश्यामो रक्ताक्षः प्रियदर्शनः। सुखभागी न दुःखार्ह श्शयितो भुवि राघवः।।2.88.19।।
165.e: How could such Rama sleep on the ground? He was born in the house of emperors, worthy of reverence by the entire world and beloved of all the worlds, with the complexion of a blue lotus, with red eyes, and pleasing looks, one who deserves to be happy and not to suffer by renouncing the kingdom and excellent comforts.

165.sa: सार्वभौमकुले जात स्सर्वलोकस्य सम्मतः। सर्वलोकप्रियस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं सुखमनुत्तम्।।2.88.18।। कथमिन्दीवरश्यामो रक्ताक्षः प्रियदर्शनः। सुखभागी न दुःखार्ह श्शयितो भुवि राघवः।।2.88.19।।
165.e: How could such Rama sleep on the ground? He was born in the house of emperors, worthy of reverence by the entire world and beloved of all the worlds, with the complexion of a blue lotus, with red eyes, and pleasing looks, one who deserves to be happy and not to suffer by renouncing the kingdom and excellent comforts.

165.sa: धन्यः खलु महाभागो लक्ष्मण श्शुभलक्षणः। भ्रातरं विषमे काले यो राममनुवर्तते।।2.88.20।।
165.e: Surely Lakshmana of great merit and auspicious virtues is fortunate since he is accompanying his brother Rama in times of adversity.

165.sa: सिद्धार्था खलु वैदेही पतिं याऽनुगता वनम्। वयं संशयिता स्सर्वे हीनास्तेन महात्मना।।2.88.21।।
165.e: Sita has, indeed, accomplished her object by accompanying her husband (to the forest). Bereft of that magnanimous Rama, all of us are in doubt (if he will accept our services).

165.sa: आकर्णधारा पृथिवी नौः इव प्रतिभाति मा। गते दशरथे स्वर्गं रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते।।2.88.22।।
165.e: King Dasaratha having ascended to heaven and Rama taken shelter in the forest, this kingdom appears to me like a ship without a helmsman.

165.sa: न च प्रार्थयते कच्चिन्मनसापि वसुन्धराम्। वनेऽपि वसतस्तस्य बाहुवीर्याभिरक्षिताम्।।2.88.23।।
165.e: No one, even in thought, would ever desire this kingdom, protected by the strength of his arms even while residing in the forest.

165.sa: शून्यसंवरणारक्षामयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम्। अपावृतपुरद्वारां राजधानीमरक्षिताम्।।2.88.24।। अप्रहृष्टबलां शून्यां विषमस्थामनावृताम्। शत्रवो नाभिमन्यन्ते भक्षान्विषकृतानिव।।2.88.25।।
165.e: Now the gates of our capital city (Ayodhya) are wide open. The city is unprotected and endangered. There are no guards to keep vigil over the ramparts. The horses and elephants are not in control (hence unprepared for battle). The army is unhappy and demoralised. At this state even the enemies will not like to seize the city, they will shun it like food mixed with poison.

165.sa: शून्यसंवरणारक्षामयन्त्रितहयद्विपाम्। अपावृतपुरद्वारां राजधानीमरक्षिताम्।।2.88.24।। अप्रहृष्टबलां शून्यां विषमस्थामनावृताम्। शत्रवो नाभिमन्यन्ते भक्षान्विषकृतानिव।।2.88.25।।
165.e: Now the gates of our capital city (Ayodhya) are wide open. The city is unprotected and endangered. There are no guards to keep vigil over the ramparts. The horses and elephants are not in control (hence unprepared for battle). The army is unhappy and demoralised. At this state even the enemies will not like to seize the city, they will shun it like food mixed with poison.

165.sa: अद्यप्रभृति भूमौ तु शयिष्येऽहं तृणेषु वा। फलमूलाशनो नित्यं जटाचीराणि धारयन्।।2.88.26।।
165.e: From today onwards, wearing matted hair and clad in robes made of bark and living on fruits and roots, I too shall sleep on the naked ground or on grass.

165.sa: तस्यार्थमुत्तरं कालं निवत्स्यामि सुखं वने। तं प्रतिश्रवमामुच्य नास्य मिथ्या भविष्यति।।2.88.27।।
165.e: Taking upon myself the vow of Rama, I too shall live in the forest cheerfully for the rest of the term on behalf of him so that his vow shall not prove untrue.

165.sa: वसन्तं भ्रातुरर्थाय शत्रुघ्नो माऽनुवत्स्यति। लक्ष्मणेन सहत्वार्यो ह्ययोध्यां पालयिष्यति।।2.88.28।।
165.e: As I live in the forest on behalf of my brother Rama, Satrughna will live with me. My esteemed brother Rama will rule Ayodhya along with Lakshmana.

165.sa: अभिषेक्ष्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमयोध्यायां द्विजातयः। अपि मे देवताः कुर्युरिमं सत्यं मनोरथम्।।2.88.29।।
165.e: In Ayodhya the brahmins shall coronate Rama. Will the gods make this desire of mine true?

165.sa: प्रसाद्यमान श्शिरसा मया स्वयं बहुप्रकारं यदि नाभिपत्स्यते। ततोऽनुवत्स्यामि चिराय राघवम् वनेचरन्नार्हति मामुपेक्षितुम्।।2.88.30।।
165.e: I will seek his grace in many ways by bowing down my head. Even then if Rama does not grant my wish, I shall also live with him as long as it takes. He will not be able to ignore a forester like me. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टाशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyeigth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

166.sa: उष्य रात्रिं तु तत्रैव गङ्गाकूले स राघवः। भरतः काल्यमुत्थाय शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.89.1।।
166.e: Bharata got up at daybreak after spending the night on the bank of the Ganga at that very place where Rama, the descendent of Raghu, had stayed. And said these words to Satrughna:

166.sa: शत्रुघ्नोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्। शीघ्रमानय भद्रं ते तारयिष्यति वाहिनीम्।।2.89.2।।
166.e: O Satrughna, blessings to you Why are you still alseep? Arise fetch Guha the king of the nishadas quickly. He will ferry the army across the river.

166.sa: जागर्मि नाहं स्वपिमि तमेवाऽर्यं विचिन्तयन्। इत्येवमब्रवीद्भ्रात्ता शत्रुघ्नोऽपि प्रचोदितः।।2.89.3।।
166.e: Urged by his brother Bharata, Satrughna replied 'I am not asleep. I am awake. I am deeply thinking of our esteemed brother, Rama'

166.sa: इति संवदतोरेवमन्योन्यं नरसिंहयोः। आगम्य प्राञ्जलिः काले गुहो भरतमब्रवीत्।।2.89.4।।
166.e: While the two lions among men, Bharata and Satrughna were thus conversing with each other, Guha came in the appropriate time and said to Bharata with folded palms:

166.sa: कच्चित्सुखं नदीतीरेऽवात्सीः काकुत्स्थ शर्वरीम्। कच्चित्ते सह सैन्यस्य तावत्सर्वमनामयम्।।2.89.5।।
166.e: O scion of the Kakutstha race (Bharata) I trust, you and your army passed the night on the river bank comfortably without any inconvenience.

166.sa: गुहस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तत्तु स्नेहादुदीरितम्। रामस्यानुवशो वाक्यं भरतोऽपीदमब्रवीत्।।2.89.6।।
166.e: On hearing Guha's affectionate words Bharata, ever obedient to Rama, replied:

166.sa: सुखा न श्शर्वरी राजन् पूजिताश्चापि ते वयम्। गङ्गां तु नौभिर्बह्वीभिर्दाशास्सन्तारयन्तु नः।।2.89.7।।
166.e: O king (Guha) the night passed comfortably for us. We have been honoured by you in many ways. Let your fishermen be ordered to ferry us across the Ganga in their boats.

166.sa: ततो गुह स्सन्त्वरितं श्रुत्वा भरतशासनम्। प्रति प्रविश्य नगरं तं ज्ञातिजनमब्रवीत्।।2.89.8।।
166.e: Then at Bharata's command Guha returned to his habitation quickly and said to his relations:

166.sa: उत्तिष्ठत प्रबुध्यध्वं भद्रमस्तु च वस्सदा। नाव स्समनुकर्षध्वं तारयिष्याम वाहिनीम्।।2.89.9।।
166.e: Arise and awake. May you be ever blessed. Haul down the boats into the river. We have to ferry the army (across the river).

166.sa: ते तथोक्ता स्समुत्थाय त्वरिता राजशासनात्। पञ्चनावां शतान्याशु समानिन्युस्समन्ततः।।2.89.10।।
166.e: On hearing these words, they arose in haste and immediately brought five hundred boats from every direction in accordance with the command of their king (Guha).

166.sa: अन्या स्स्वस्तिकविज्ञेया महाघंटाधरा वराः। शोभमानाः पताकाभिर्युक्तवातास्सुसंहताः।।2.89.11।।
166.e: They brought excellent boats known as Swastika, solidly built, they lookd magnificent, filled with large bells, sails and flags.

166.sa: तत स्स्वस्तिकविज्ञेयां पाण्डुकम्बलसंवृताम्। सनन्दिघोषां कल्याणीं गुहो नावमुपाहरत्।।2.89.12।।
166.e: Then Guha personally brought an auspicious boat known as Swastika covered with white canvas and generating captivating sounds.

166.sa: तामारुरोह भरतश्शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।।2.89.13।। पुरोहितश्च तत्पूर्वं गुरवो ब्राह्मणाश्च ये। अनन्तरं राजदारास्तदैव शकटापणाः।।2.89.14।।
166.e: The family priest (Vasistha) and other brahmins were the first to board. Next mighty Bharata and Satrughna, Kausalya, Sumitra, women of the palace including the other wives of the king and wagons and supplies followed.

166.sa: तामारुरोह भरतश्शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।।2.89.13।। पुरोहितश्च तत्पूर्वं गुरवो ब्राह्मणाश्च ये। अनन्तरं राजदारास्तदैव शकटापणाः।।2.89.14।।
166.e: The family priest (Vasistha) and other brahmins were the first to board. Next mighty Bharata and Satrughna, Kausalya, Sumitra, women of the palace including the other wives of the king and wagons and supplies followed.

166.sa: आवासमादीपयतां तीर्थं चाप्यवगाहताम्। भाण्डानि चाददानानां घोषस्त्रिदिवमस्पृशत्।।2.89.15।।
166.e: The clamour of the people setting fire to the temporary shelters in that camp, descending down the river and transporting the supplies into the boats reached the heaven.

166.sa: पताकिन्यस्तु ता नावस्स्वयं दाशैरधिष्ठिताः। वहन्त्यो जनमारूढं तदा सम्पेतुराशुगाः।।2.89.16।।
166.e: Those boats adorned with flags were propelled by the fishermen occupying them. They sailed with men rowing on board fast.

166.sa: नारीणामभिपूर्णा स्तु काश्चित् काश्चिच्च वाजिनाम्। काश्चिदत्र वहन्ति स्म यानयुग्यं महाधनम्।।2.89.17।।
166.e: Some boats were filled with women, some others with horses. while still others transported draught animals for drawing carriages and the great treasures.

166.sa: ता स्स्म गत्वा परं तीरमवरोप्य च तं जनम्। निवृत्ताः काण्डचित्राणि क्रियन्ते दाशबन्धुभिः।।2.89.18।।
166.e: Having reached the other bank, the men disembarked. While returning, the fisherfolk exhibited their craft of lovely formations.

166.sa: सवैजयन्तास्तु गजा गजारोहप्रचोदिताः। तरन्त स्स्म प्रकाशन्ते सध्वजा इव पर्वताः।।2.89.19।।
166.e: The elephants, embellished with banners and goaded by their mahouts looked splendid like mountains with banners while crossing in the water.

166.sa: नावस्त्वारुरुहुश्चान्ये प्लवैस्तेरु स्तथापरे। अन्ये कुम्भघटैस्तेरुरन्येतेरुश्च बाहुभिः।।2.89.20।।
166.e: Only some of the people were able to board the boats. Some others crossed on rafts and on large pots. Still others swam with their arms.

166.sa: सा पुण्या ध्वजिनी गङ्गां दाशैस्सन्तारिता स्वयम्। मैत्रे मुहूर्ते प्रययौ प्रयागवनमुत्तमम्।।2.89.21।।
166.e: The auspicious army, ferried across the river Ganga by the fishermen, reached the great forest of Prayaga at the auspicious hour of Maitra.

166.sa: आश्वासयित्वा च चमूं महात्मा निवेशयित्वा च यथोपजोषम्। द्रष्टुं भरद्वाजमृषिप्रवर्य मृत्विग्वृतस्सन्भरतः प्रतस्थे।।2.89.22।।
166.e: The noble Bharata, got his army encamped according to their pleasure and set out, accompanied by his priests, to see the distinguished sage Bharadwaja.

167.sa: भरद्वाजाश्रमं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशादेव नरर्षभः। बलं सर्वमवस्थाप्य जगाम सह मन्त्रिभिः।।2.90.1।। पद्भ्यामेव हि धर्मज्ञो न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः। वसानो वाससी क्षौमे पुरोधाय पुरोधसम्।।2.90.2।।
167.e: Bharata, the knower of righteous ways and the best among men, saw the hermitage of Bharadwaja from a distance of one krosa and brought his entire army to a halt. He laid aside all his royal robes and weapons. Clad in silk garments, he went on foot along with his ministers, with the family priest Vasistha ahead of him.

167.sa: भरद्वाजाश्रमं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशादेव नरर्षभः। बलं सर्वमवस्थाप्य जगाम सह मन्त्रिभिः।।2.90.1।। पद्भ्यामेव हि धर्मज्ञो न्यस्तशस्त्रपरिच्छदः। वसानो वाससी क्षौमे पुरोधाय पुरोधसम्।।2.90.2।।
167.e: Bharata, the knower of righteous ways and the best among men, saw the hermitage of Bharadwaja from a distance of one krosa and brought his entire army to a halt. He laid aside all his royal robes and weapons. Clad in silk garments, he went on foot along with his ministers, with the family priest Vasistha ahead of him.

167.sa: तत स्सन्दर्शने तस्य भरद्वाजस्य राघवः। मन्त्रिणस्तानवस्थाप्य जगामानुपुरोहितम्।।2.90.3।।
167.e: Then the scion of the Raghu race (Bharata) halted his ministers within sight of Bharadwaja's (hermitage) and went along following his priest Vasistha.

167.sa: वसिष्ठमथ दृष्ट्वैव भरद्वाजो महातपाः। सञ्चचाऽलासनात्तूर्णं शिष्यानर्घ्यमिति ब्रुवन्।।2.90.4।।
167.e: On seeing Vasistha, the great ascetic Bharadwaja immediately left his seat and said to his disciples, Bring offerings of water.

167.sa: समागम्य वसिष्ठेन भरतेनाभिवादितः। अबुद्ध्यत महातेजास्सुतं दशरथस्य तम्।।2.90.5।।
167.e: After meeting Vasistha and greeted by Bharata, the radiant Bharadwaja could recognize he was the son of Dasaratha.

167.sa: ताभ्यामर्घ्यं च पाद्यं च दत्वा पश्चात्फलानि च। आनुपूर्व्याच्छ धर्मज्ञः पप्रच्छ कुशलं कुले।।2.90.6।।
167.e: Offering them both in order arghya (welcomeoffering), water to wash their feet and fruits in accordance with the practice, he enquired Bharata about the welfare of the family.

167.sa: अयोध्यायां बले कोशे मित्रेष्वपि च मन्त्रिषु। जानन् दशरथं वृत्तं न राजानमुदाहरत्।।2.90.7।।
167.e: He enquired about the welfare of Ayodhya, of the army, treasury, friends and the ministers. But knowingly did not mention about Dasaratha's wellbeing (the knew Dasaratha was dead).

167.sa: वसिष्ठो भरतश्चैनं पप्रच्छतुरनामयम्। शरीरेऽग्निषु वृक्षेषु शिष्येषु मृगपक्षिषु।।2.90.8।।
167.e: Vasistha and Bharata also enquired about his health and welfare of his sacred fires, his disciples, animals and birds and trees of the hermitage.

167.sa: तथेति तत्प्रतिज्ञाय भरद्वाजो महातपाः। भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं राघवस्नेहबन्धनात्।।2.90.9।।
167.e: Saying, all is well, the great ascetic Bharadwaja, out of his affection for Rama, said to Bharata:

167.sa: किमिहाऽगमने कार्यं तव राज्यं प्रशासतः। एतदाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं न हि मे शुद्ध्यते मनः।।2.90.10।।
167.e: Why have you come here when you ought to be ruling the kingdom? Tell me everything about this. My mind is not clear in this matter.

167.sa: सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्यानऽन्दवर्धनम्। भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.90.11।। नियुक्तः स्त्रीनियुक्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः। वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश।।2.90.12।। कच्छिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च।।2.90.13।।
167.e: Rama, destroyer of enemies and enhancer of the delight of his mother Kausalya, has been banished to the forest for a long time along with his wife and brother. That illustrious one has been ordered by his father to live in the forest for fourteen years through the pursuasion of a woman. To enjoy the kingdom without obstacles do you intend to cause any harm to that irreproachable Rama and his brother?

167.sa: सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्यानऽन्दवर्धनम्। भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.90.11।। नियुक्तः स्त्रीनियुक्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः। वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश।।2.90.12।। कच्छिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च।।2.90.13।।
167.e: Rama, destroyer of enemies and enhancer of the delight of his mother Kausalya, has been banished to the forest for a long time along with his wife and brother. That illustrious one has been ordered by his father to live in the forest for fourteen years through the pursuasion of a woman. To enjoy the kingdom without obstacles do you intend to cause any harm to that irreproachable Rama and his brother?

167.sa: सुषुवे यममित्रघ्नं कौसल्यानऽन्दवर्धनम्। भ्रात्रा सह सभार्यो यश्चिरं प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.90.11।। नियुक्तः स्त्रीनियुक्तेन पित्रा योऽसौ महायशाः। वनवासी भवेतीह समाः किल चतुर्दश।।2.90.12।। कच्छिन्न तस्यापापस्य पापं कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। अकण्टकं भोक्तुमना राज्यं तस्यानुजस्य च।।2.90.13।।
167.e: Rama, destroyer of enemies and enhancer of the delight of his mother Kausalya, has been banished to the forest for a long time along with his wife and brother. That illustrious one has been ordered by his father to live in the forest for fourteen years through the pursuasion of a woman. To enjoy the kingdom without obstacles do you intend to cause any harm to that irreproachable Rama and his brother?

167.sa: एवमुक्तो भरद्वाजं भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। पर्यश्रुनयनो दुःखाद्वाचा संसज्जमानया।।2.90.14।।
167.e: At these words, Bharata, eyes filled with tears of grief, replied to Bharadwaja in a   stumbling voice:

167.sa: हतोऽस्मि यदि मामेवं भगवानपि मन्यते। मत्तो न दोषमाशङ्के नैवं मामनुशास्तु हि।2.90.15।।
167.e: When one so venerable like you too misunderstands me, I am gone. There is no danger for him from me. Do not rebuke me this way.

167.sa: न चैतदिष्टं माता मे यदवोचन्मदन्तरे। नाहमेतेन तुष्टश्च न तद्वचनमाददे।।2.90.16।।
167.e: I do not approve of whatever my mother said in my absence. I am not happy with those words and I do not accept them.

167.sa: अहं तु तं नरव्याघ्रमुपयातः प्रसादकः। प्रतिनेतुमयोध्यां च पादौ तस्याभिवन्दितुम्।।2.90.17।।
167.e: I have come to worship the feet of Rama, the best of men and persuade him to return to Ayodhya.

167.sa: त्वं मामेवंगतं मत्वा प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि। शंस मे भगवन्रामः क्व सम्प्रति महीपतिः।।2.90.18।।
167.e: O venerable one in consideration of the circumstances I am in, be kind to me and tell me the whereabouts of Rama, lord of the earth.

167.sa: वशिष्ठादिभिः ऋत्विग्भिर्याचितो भगवांस्ततः। उवाच तं भरद्वाजः प्रसादाद्भरतं वचः।2.90.19।।
167.e: Likewise besought by Vasistha and other priests, the venerable Bharadwaja was pleased to tell Bharata:

167.sa: त्वय्येतत्पुरुषव्याघ्र युक्तं राघववंशजे। गुरुवृत्तिर्दमश्चैव साधूनामनुयायिता।।2.90.20।।
167.e: O best of men (Bharata) your conduct towards the preceptors, your selfrestraint and devotion to the virtuous are all in keeping with those born in the race of Raghu.

167.sa: जाने चैतन्मनस्थं ते दृढीकरणमस्त्विति। अपृच्छं त्वां तथाऽत्यर्थं कीर्तिं समभिवर्धयन्।।2.90.21।।
167.e: I am aware of the feelings in your heart. Even then I enquired in order to confirm it  and to further your fame.

167.sa: जाने च रामं धर्मज्ञं ससीतं सहलक्ष्मणम्। असौ वसति ते भ्राता चित्रकूटे महागिरौ।।2.90.22।।
167.e: I know your brother who is conversant with righteousness is living on Chitrakuta mountain with Sita and Lakshmana.

167.sa: श्वस्तु गन्तासि तं देशं वसाद्य सह मन्त्रिभिः। एतन्मे कुरु सुप्राज्ञ कामं कामार्थकोविद।।2.90.23।।
167.e: O supremely sagacious prince gifted with the knowledge of kama (desire) and artha (wealth), tomorrow you go, but to night stay here with your ministers and fulfil my desire.

167.sa: ततस्तथेत्येवमुदारदर्शनः प्रतीतरूपो भरतोऽब्रवीद्वचः। चकार बुद्धिं च तदा तदाश्रमे निशानिवासाय नराधिपाऽत्मजः।।2.90.24।।
167.e: A man of liberal disposition, Bharata expressed his intention, saying, 'Be it so'. Then the prince made up him mind to spend the might in that hermitage. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे नवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetieth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

168.sa: कृतबुद्धिं निवासाय तत्रैव स मुनिस्तदा। भरतं कैकयीपुत्रमातिथ्येनन्यमन्त्रयत्।।2.91.1।।
168.e: With the decision of Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, to stay there for the night, sage Bharadwaja extended to him all hospitality.

168.sa: अब्रवीद्भरतस्त्वेनं नन्विदं भवता कृतम्। पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथाऽतिथ्यं वने यदुपपद्यते।।2.91.2।।
168.e: Bharata said to Bharadwaja, You have already extended the hospitality in offering water for washing the feet with and of arghya befitting a guest as available in the forest.

168.sa: अथोवाच भरद्वाजो भरतं प्रहसन्निव। जाने त्वां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं तुष्येस्त्वं येन केनचित्।।2.91.3।।
168.e: Bharadwaja then said to Bharata with a gentle smile, I know you are full of love and content with whatever is offered you.

168.sa: सेनायास्तु तवैतस्याः कर्तुमिच्छामि भोजनम्। मम प्रीतिर्यथारूपा तथार्हो मनुजर्षभ।।2.91.4।।
168.e: O Bharata, the best of men, I want to treat your army with food. This will please me and I hope you will act accordingly.

168.sa: किमर्थं चापि निक्षिप्य दूरे बलमिहागतः। कस्मान्नेहोपयातोऽसि सबलः पुरुषर्षभः।।2.91.5।।
168.e: Why did you, O Bharata, the best of men, station your army at a distance before coming here? Could you not approach me along with your army?

168.sa: भरतः प्रत्युवाचेदं प्राञ्जलिस्तं तपोधनम्। ससैन्यो नोपयातोऽस्मि भगवन्भगवद्भयात्।।2.91.6।।
168.e: With folded palms (in reverence), Bharata said to sage Bharadwaja whose penance was his wealth: I did not approach you with the army for fear of you, O venerable one.

168.sa: राज्ञा च भगवन्नित्यं राजपुत्रेण वा सदा। यत्नतः परिहर्तव्या विषयेषु तपस्विनः।।2.91.7।।
168.e: O venerable one a king or a prince ought to intentionally avoid those places occupied by ascetics.

168.sa: वाजिमुख्या मनुष्याश्च मत्ताश्च वरवारणाः। प्रच्छाद्य भगवन्भूमिं महतीमनुयान्ति माम्।।2.91.8।।
168.e: O venerable sage spirited horses, men and mighty rutting elephants follow me covering a wide expanse of land.

168.sa: ते वृक्षानुदकं भूमिमाश्रमेषूटजां स्तथा। न हिंस्युरिति तेनाऽहमेक एव समागतः।।2.91.9।।
168.e: Lest the army should damage the huts, trees, land, and defile the water in the ashram, I came here alone.

168.sa: आनीयतामितस्सेनेत्याज्ञप्तः परमर्षिणा। ततस्तु चक्रे भरतस्सेनायास्समुपागमम्।।2.91.10।।
168.e: Thus commanded the great ascetic, 'Let the army be brought here'. Accordingly, Bharata ordered the army to come.

168.sa: अग्निशालां प्रविश्याथ पीत्वाऽपः परिमृज्य च। आतिथ्यस्य क्रियाहेतोर्विश्वकर्माणमाह्वयत्।।2.91.11।।
168.e: Then Bharadwaja entered the fire sanctuary, sipped water and washed his hands with water and invoked Visvakarma to provide hospitality.

168.sa: आह्वये विश्वकर्माणमहं त्वष्टारमेव च। आतिथ्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि तत्र मे संविधीयताम्।।2.91.12।।
168.e: I intend to provide hospitality for which I am invoking Visvakarma and Tvastara who builds houses. Let adequate arrangements be made.

168.sa: आह्वये लोकपालांस्त्रीन् देवान् शक्रमुखांस्तथा। आतिथ्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि तत्र मे संविधीयताम्।।2.91.13।।
168.e: I invoke the three deities, guardians of the four quarters headed by Indra to extend hospitality (to Bharata). Let them make adequate arrangements in this regard.

168.sa: प्राक्स्रोतसश्च या नद्यः प्रत्यक्स्रोतस एव च। पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च समायान्त्वद्य सर्वशः।।2.91.14।।
168.e: Let the rivers flowing towards the east, and the west, flowing on the earth and in the sky, flowing everywhere reach here and now.

168.sa: अन्या स्रवन्तु मैरेयं सुरामन्यास्सुविष्ठिताम्। अपरा श्चोदकं शीतमिक्षुकाण्डरसोपमम्।।2.91.15।।
168.e: Let some rivers flow with liquor made of datepalms, some with wellprepared wine and some with cool water which tastes like sugarcane juice.

168.sa: आह्वये देवगन्धर्वान्विश्वावसुहहाहुहून्। तथैवाप्सरसो देवीर्गन्धर्वीश्चापि सर्वशः।।2.91.16।।
168.e: I invoke the gandharvas, Visvavasu, Ha Ha and Hu Hu, and also goddesses like gandharvas (heavenly musicians) and apsaras (nymphs) from all regions.

168.sa: घृताचीमथ विश्वाचीं मिश्रकेशीमलंबुसाम्। नागदन्तां च हेमां च हिमामद्रिकृतस्थलाम्।।2.91.17।।
168.e: I summon also Grutachi, Visvachi, Misrakesi, Alambusa, Nagadantha, Hema and Hima whose abode is on the mountain.

168.sa: शक्रं याश्चोपतिष्ठन्ति ब्रह्माणं याश्च योषितः। सर्वास्तुम्बुरुणा सार्धमाह्वये सपरिच्छदाः।।2.91.18।।
168.e: I invoke all the women who attend on Indra and Bramha along with tumbur with all their (musical) instruments.

168.sa: वनं कुरुषु यद्दिव्यं वासोभूषणपत्रवत्। दिव्यनारीफलं शश्वत्तत्कौबेरमिहैतु च।।2.91.19।।
168.e: Let Kubera's divine forest situated in the land of Kurus, where leaves serve as raiment and ornaments and celestial women as its fruits come here.

168.sa: इह मे भगवान् सोमो विधत्तामन्नमुत्तमम्। भक्ष्यंभोज्यं च चोष्यं च लेह्यं च विविधं बहु।।2.91.20।।
168.e: Let the blessed Moon furnish me with excellent food of every kind -- solid, liquid, soft and those which are to be sucked and licked in great variety and quantity.

168.sa: विचित्राणि च माल्यानि पादपप्रच्युतानि च। सुरादीनि च पेयानि मांसानि विविधानि च।।2.91.21।।
168.e: Let her furnish me with manycoloured garlands of fresh flowers from trees, wines and other drinks and meat of different kinds.

168.sa: एवं समाधिना युक्तस्तेजसाऽप्रतिमेन च। शीक्षास्वरसमायुक्तं तपसा चाब्रवीन्मुनिः।।2.91.22।।
168.e: The valiant ascetic of incomparable lustre and power of penance in profound meditation said this in an accent in conformity with Vedic instruction.

168.sa: मनसा ध्यायतस्तस्य प्राङ्मुखस्य कृताञ्जलेः। आजग्मुस्तानि सर्वाणि दैवतानि पृथक्पृथक्।।2.91.23।।
168.e: As Bharadwaja with folded palms was thus meditating with his face turned eastward, all the deities appeared there one by one.

168.sa: मलयं दर्दुरं चैव ततस्स्वेदनुदोऽनिलः। उपस्पृश्य ववौ युक्त्या सुप्रियात्मा सुखश्शिवः।।2.91.24।।
168.e: Meanwhile, soft auspicious and pleasant breeze passing over Malaya and Dardura mountains, comforting and cooling the sweat, began to blow.

168.sa: ततोऽभ्यवर्षन्त घना दिव्याः कुसुमवृष्टयः। दिव्यदुन्दुभिघोषश्च दिक्षु सर्वासु शुश्रुवे।।2.91.25।।
168.e: Then divine clouds rolled in and showered celestial flowers. The sounds of heavenly gongs could be heard in every direction.

168.sa: प्रववुश्चोत्तमा वाता ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः। जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वा वीणाः प्रमुमुचुस्स्वरान्।।2.91.26।।
168.e: Gentle breeze began to blow. Troops of apsaras danced. Gandharvas and gods sang and the lyres rang.

168.sa: स शब्दो द्यां च भूमिं च प्राणिनां श्रवणानि च। विवेशोच्चरितश्श्लक्ष्णस्समो लयसमन्वितः।।2.91.27।।
168.e: That soft, melodious, rhythmic and wellmodulated sound entered the heaven and earth as well as the ears of all living beings.

168.sa: तस्मिन्नुपरते शब्दे दिव्ये श्रोत्र सुखे नृणाम्। ददर्श भारतं सैन्यं विधानं विश्वकर्मणः।।2.91.28।।
168.e: When the celestial sounds pleasing to the ears of men had subsided, the army of Bharata beheld the wonderful creations of Visvakarma.

168.sa: बभूव हि समा भूमिस्समन्तात्पञ्चयोजना। शाद्वलैर्भहुभिश्चन्ना नीलवैढूर्यसन्निभैः।।2.91.29।।
168.e: The ground was levelled on every side for five yojanas and covered with several grass lawns resembling lapis lazuli (blue sapphire) and cat's eye.

168.sa: तस्मिन्बिल्वाः कपित्थाश्च पनसा बीजपूरकाः। आमलक्यो बभूवुश्च चूताश्च फलभूषणाः।।2.91.30।।
168.e: There the best of fruitbearing trees like bilva trees, woodapple trees, citrons, emblic myrobalan trees and mango trees laden with fruits sprang up.

168.sa: उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश्च वनं दिव्योपभोगवत्। आजगाम नदी दिव्या तीरजैर्भहुभिर्वृता।।2.91.31।।
168.e: From the forests of the northern Kuru kingdom, with all delights of heaven, a divine river with innumerable trees that grow on river banks came into existence.

168.sa: चतुश्शालानि शुभ्राणि शालाश्च गजवाजिनाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधास्तोरणानि शुभानि च।।2.91.32।।
168.e: Bright quadrangles, stables for elephants and horses, auspicious arch ways for palaces and mansions sprang up.

168.sa: सितमेघनिभं चापि राजवेश्म सुतोरणम्। दिव्यमाल्यकृताकारं दिव्यगन्धसमुक्षितम्।।2.91.33।। चतुरश्रमसंबाधं शयनासनयानवत्। दिव्यैस्सर्वरसैर्युक्तं दिव्यभोजनवस्त्रवत्।।2.91.34।। उपकल्पितसर्वान्नं धौतनिर्मलभाजनम्। क्लुप्तसर्वासनं श्रीमत्स्वास्तीर्णशयनोत्तमम्।।2.91.35।।
168.e: An auspicious royal palace with splendid archs resembling white clouds sprang up. It was sprinkled with celestial perfumes and adorned with beautiful garlands. That royal palace forming a quadrangle was furnished with couches, seats and carriages and furnished with celestial drinks of every kind, delicious food and splendid garments. It was stocked with food of every variety in clean and spotless vessels. Seats for every one and magnificent couches covered with excellent bedstead were arranged.

168.sa: सितमेघनिभं चापि राजवेश्म सुतोरणम्। दिव्यमाल्यकृताकारं दिव्यगन्धसमुक्षितम्।।2.91.33।। चतुरश्रमसंबाधं शयनासनयानवत्। दिव्यैस्सर्वरसैर्युक्तं दिव्यभोजनवस्त्रवत्।।2.91.34।। उपकल्पितसर्वान्नं धौतनिर्मलभाजनम्। क्लुप्तसर्वासनं श्रीमत्स्वास्तीर्णशयनोत्तमम्।।2.91.35।।
168.e: An auspicious royal palace with splendid archs resembling white clouds sprang up. It was sprinkled with celestial perfumes and adorned with beautiful garlands. That royal palace forming a quadrangle was furnished with couches, seats and carriages and furnished with celestial drinks of every kind, delicious food and splendid garments. It was stocked with food of every variety in clean and spotless vessels. Seats for every one and magnificent couches covered with excellent bedstead were arranged.

168.sa: सितमेघनिभं चापि राजवेश्म सुतोरणम्। दिव्यमाल्यकृताकारं दिव्यगन्धसमुक्षितम्।।2.91.33।। चतुरश्रमसंबाधं शयनासनयानवत्। दिव्यैस्सर्वरसैर्युक्तं दिव्यभोजनवस्त्रवत्।।2.91.34।। उपकल्पितसर्वान्नं धौतनिर्मलभाजनम्। क्लुप्तसर्वासनं श्रीमत्स्वास्तीर्णशयनोत्तमम्।।2.91.35।।
168.e: An auspicious royal palace with splendid archs resembling white clouds sprang up. It was sprinkled with celestial perfumes and adorned with beautiful garlands. That royal palace forming a quadrangle was furnished with couches, seats and carriages and furnished with celestial drinks of every kind, delicious food and splendid garments. It was stocked with food of every variety in clean and spotless vessels. Seats for every one and magnificent couches covered with excellent bedstead were arranged.

168.sa: प्रविवेश महाबाहुरनुज्ञातो महर्षिणा। वेश्म तद्रत्नसम्पूर्णं भरतः कैकयीसुतः।।2.91.36।।
168.e: Longarmed Bharata, son of Kaikeyi entered that palace full of jewels with the permission of the great sage.

168.sa: अनुजग्मुश्च तं सर्वे मन्त्रिणस्सपुरोहिताः। बभूवुश्च मुदा युक्ता दृष्ट्वा तं वेश्मसंविधिम्।।2.91.37।।
168.e: All the ministers, priests followed him and were glad to see the arrangement in that mansion.

168.sa: तत्र राजासनं दिव्यं व्यजनं छत्रमेव च। भरतो मन्त्रिभिस्सार्धमभ्यवर्तत राजवत्।।2.91.38।।
168.e: There where stood an exquisite throne, a fan and a parasol Bharata stayed in the company of ministers.

168.sa: आसनं पूजयामास रामायाभिप्रणम्य च। वालव्यजनमादाय न्यषीदत्सचिवासने।।2.91.39।।
168.e: He bowed in reverence and worshipped the throne (as though Rama were seated there). Taking hold of a fan made of yak's tail he sat in a minister's seat.

168.sa: आनुपूर्व्यान्निषेदुश्च सर्वे मन्त्रिपुरोहिताः। ततस्सेनापतिः पश्चात्प्रशास्ताच निषेदतुः।।2.91.40।।
168.e: First the ministers and priests took their respective seats in accordance with their rank, and then the army chief and finally the supervisor of the camp.

168.sa: तत स्तत्र मुहूर्तेन नद्यः पायसकर्दमाः। उपातिष्ठन्त भरतं भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्।।2.91.41।।
168.e: Rivers filled with payasam (rice cooked in milk and sugar) in the shape of mud flowed towards Bharata at the command of Bharadwaja.

168.sa: तासामुभयतः कूलं पाण्डुमृत्तिकलेपनाः। रम्याश्चावसधा दिव्या ब्रह्मणस्तु प्रसादजा:।।2.91.42।।
168.e: On both the banks of those rivers, charming, celestial houses plastered with white clay appeared by the grace of Brahma.

168.sa: तेनैव च मूहूर्तेन दिव्याऽभरणभूषिताः। आगुर्विंशतिसाहस्राः ब्रह्मणा प्रहिताः स्त्रियः।।2.91.43।।
168.e: At that very moment twenty thousand women adorned with beautiful ornaments sent by Brahma presented themselves.

168.sa: सुवर्णमणिमुक्तेन प्रवालेन च शोभिताः। आगुर्विंशतिसाहास्राः कुबेरप्रहिताः स्त्रियः।।2.91.44।।
168.e: Twenty thousand women adorned with gold, gems and corals sent by Kubera came.

168.sa: याभिर्गृहीतः पुरुषस्सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते। आगुर्विंशतिसाहस्रा नन्दनादप्सरोगणाः।।2.91.45।।
168.e: Troops of twenty thousand apsaras by whom any man when taken hold of in their arms could be intoxicated with intense passion, came from Nandana gardens.

168.sa: नारदस्तुम्भुरुर्गोपः प्रवरास्सूर्यवर्चसः। एते गन्धर्वराजानो भरतस्याग्रतो जगुः।।2.91.46।।
168.e: There along with Narada, Tumburu and Gopa, distinguished kings of the gandharvas, looking bright like the Sun, began to sing in the presence of Bharata.

168.sa: अलम्बुसा मिश्रकेशी पुण्डरीकाऽथ वामना। उपानृत्यंस्तु भरतं भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्।।2.91.47।।
168.e: Thereafter, the apsaras, Alambusa, Misrakesi, Pundarika and Vamana danced near Bharata at the command of Bharadwaja.

168.sa: यानि माल्यानि देवेषु यानि चैत्ररथे वने। प्रयागे तान्यदृश्यन्त भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्।।2.91.48।।
168.e: The garlands of the gods available in Chitraratha's (Kubera's) garden could not match those obtained under the orders of Bharadwaja.

168.sa: बिल्वा मार्दङ्गिका आसन् शम्याग्राहा विभीतकाः। अश्वत्था नर्तकाश्चासन्भरद्वाजस्य शासनात्।।2.91.49।।
168.e: At the command of Bharadwaja, bilva trees acted as drummers, vibhitaka trees as cymbalists and the pipal trees as dancers.

168.sa: ततस्सरलतालाश्च तिलका नक्तमालकाः। प्रहृष्टास्तत्र सम्पेतुः कुब्जा भूत्वाऽथ वामनाः।।2.91.50।।
168.e: Thereafter pine, palmyra, tilaka, and naktamala trees were transformed into hunchbacks and dwarfs and moved about in great delight.

168.sa: शिंशुपामलकीजम्ब्वो याश्चान्याः काननेषु ताः मालती मल्लिका जातिर्याश्चान्याः कानने लताः। प्रमदाविग्रहं कृत्वा भरद्वाजाश्रमेऽवदन्।।2.91.51।।
168.e: Asohka, emblic myrobalan and all other trees found in the forest malati, mallika and jati creepers assumed the form of women, came over to the hermitage of Bharadwaja and said:

168.sa: सुरास्सुरापाः पिबत पायसं च बुभुक्षिताः।।2.91.52।। मांसानि च सुमेध्यानि भक्ष्यन्तां यावदिच्छथ।।2.91.53।।
168.e: 'O wine drinkers, drink as much as you can those who are hungry partake payasam and sacred meat'.

168.sa: सुरास्सुरापाः पिबत पायसं च बुभुक्षिताः।।2.91.52।। मांसानि च सुमेध्यानि भक्ष्यन्तां यावदिच्छथ।।2.91.53।।
168.e: 'O wine drinkers, drink as much as you can those who are hungry partake payasam and sacred meat'.

168.sa: उच्छाद्य स्नापयन्ति स्म नदीतीरेष वल्गुषु। अप्येकमेकं पुरषं प्रमदास्सप्त चाष्ट च।।2.91.54।।
168.e: Every single warrior was attended by seven or eight women who applied oil and massaged his body and bathed him on the lovely banks of the river.

168.sa: संवाहन्त्यस्समापेतुर्नार्यो रुचिरलोचनाः। परिमृज्य तथाऽन्योन्यं पाययन्ति वराङ्गनाः।।2.91.55।।
168.e: Some women with beautiful eyes quickly approached them for massaging. The  best of ladies wiped their bodies dry and gave each other wine to drink.

168.sa: हयान् गजान् खारानुष्ट्रान्तथैव सुरभेस्सुतान्। अभोजयन्वाहनपास्तेषां भोज्यं यथाविधि।।2.91.56।।
168.e: The attendants of draughtanimals fed the horses, elephants, donkeys, camels and oxen their appropriate food.

168.sa: इक्षूंश्च मधुलाजांश्च भोजयन्ति स्म वाहनान्। इक्ष्वाकुवरयोधानां चोदयन्तो महाबला:।।2.91.57।।
168.e: The draughtaimals of the illustrious warriors of Ikshvaku kings were urged by the highly energetic attendants to eat more and more of parched grain mixed with sugarcane and honey.

168.sa: नाश्वबन्धोऽश्वमाजानान्नगजं कुञ्जरग्रहः। मत्तप्रमत्तमुदिता चमूः सा तत्र संबभौ।।2.91.58।।
168.e: The horserider no longer recognised the horse or the mahout the elephant and the whole army was inebriated with drinking and pleasure.

168.sa: तर्पितास्सर्वकामैस्ते रक्तचन्दनरूषिताः। अप्सरोगणसंयुक्तास्सैन्या वाचमुदैरयन्।।2.91.59।।
168.e: All the armymen with their desires gratified and anointing their bodies with red sandal paste surrounded by apsaras exclaimed.

168.sa: नैवायोध्यां गमिष्यामो नगमिष्याम दण्डकान्। कुशलं भरतस्यास्तु रामस्यास्तु तथा सुखम्।।2.91.60।।
168.e: We will neither return to Ayodhya, nor enter Dandaka (forest). May Bharata and Rama be happy.

168.sa: इति पादातयोधाश्च हस्त्यश्वारोहबन्धकाः। अनाथास्तं विधिं लब्ध्वा वाचमेतामुदीरयन्।।2.91.61।।
168.e: Having enjoyed the hospitality of Bharadwaja the foot soldiers, horse and elephant riders made utterances ignoring their leaders.

168.sa: संम्प्रहृष्टा विनेदुस्ते नरास्तत्र सहस्रशः। भरतस्यानुयातारस्स्वर्गोऽयमिति चाब्रुवन्।।2.91.62।।
168.e: The exceedingly delighted soldiers of Bharata's retinue in their thousands cried out with excitement This is the very heaven.

168.sa: नृत्यन्ति स्म हसन्ति स्म गायन्ति स्म च सैनिकाः समन्तात्परिधावन्ति माल्योपेतास्सहस्रशः।।2.91.63।।
168.e: Those thousands of soldiers wearing flower garlands ran about dancing, singing, and laughing.

168.sa: ततो भुक्तवतां तेषां तदन्नममृतोपमम्। दिव्यानुद्वीक्ष्य भक्ष्यां स्तानभवद्भक्षणे मतिः।।2.91.64।।
168.e: Glancing at the ambrosial food, a desire arose in the minds of those soldiers to eat once again although they had already partaken it.

168.sa: प्रेष्याश्चेट्यश्च वध्वश्च बलस्थाश्च सहस्रशः। बभूवुस्ते भृशं दृप्तास्सर्वे चाहतवाससः।।2.91.65।।
168.e: Messengers, maidservants, female attendants, and soldiers -- all of them in their thousands dressed in fresh garments felt exceedingly proud of themselves.

168.sa: कुञ्जराश्च खरोष्ट्राश्च गोऽश्वाश्च मृगपक्षिणः। बभूवुस्सुभृतास्तत्र नान्यो ह्यन्यमकल्पयत्।।2.91.66।।
168.e: There the elephants, donkeys and camels, cows and horses and also beasts and birds were wellnourished. No one troubled the other.

168.sa: नाऽशुक्लवासा स्तत्राऽसीत्क्षुधितो मलिनोऽपि वा। रजसा ध्वस्तकेशो वा नरः कश्चिददृश्यत।।2.91.67।।
168.e: In that army there was none who could be seen without wearing garments of sparkling white, who was hungry or dirty or with decayed hair.

168.sa: आजैश्चापि च वाराहैर्निष्ठानवरस़ञ्चयैः। फलनिर्यूह संसिद्दैस्सूपैर्गन्ध रसान्वितैः।।2.91.68।। पुष्पध्वजवतीः पूर्णाश्शुक्लस्यान्नस्य चाभितः। ददृशुर्विस्मितास्तत्रनरा लौहीस्सहस्रशः।।2.91.69।।
168.e: There the soldiers beheld in amazement thousands of iron containers decked with flags and flowers and filled with white rice, mutton, pork, choicest condiments, fruit juice, fragrant and tasty soup.

168.sa: आजैश्चापि च वाराहैर्निष्ठानवरस़ञ्चयैः। फलनिर्यूह संसिद्दैस्सूपैर्गन्ध रसान्वितैः।।2.91.68।। पुष्पध्वजवतीः पूर्णाश्शुक्लस्यान्नस्य चाभितः। ददृशुर्विस्मितास्तत्रनरा लौहीस्सहस्रशः।।2.91.69।।
168.e: There the soldiers beheld in amazement thousands of iron containers decked with flags and flowers and filled with white rice, mutton, pork, choicest condiments, fruit juice, fragrant and tasty soup.

168.sa: बभूवुर्वनपार्श्वेषु कूपाः पायसकर्दमाः। ताश्चकामदुघा गावो द्रुमाश्चासन्मधुश्च्युतः।।2.91.70।।
168.e: Along the edge of the forest, wells were filled with thick payasam. There were wishfulfilling cows and honeydripping trees.

168.sa: वाप्यो मैरेयपूर्णाश्च मृष्टमांसचयैर्वृताः। प्रतप्तपिठरैश्चापि मार्गमायूरकौक्कुटैः।।2.91.71।।
168.e: The wells were found filled with datepalm liquor and surrounded by pots of well cooked meat of peacocks, chicken and other animals.

168.sa: पात्रीणां च सहस्राणि स्थालीनां नियुतानि च। न्यर्बुधानि च पात्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च।।2.91.72।। स्थाल्यः कुम्भ्य करम्भ्य श्च दधिपूर्णास्सुसंस्कृताः। यौवनस्थस्य गौरस्य कपित्थस्य सुगन्धिनः।।2.91.73।। ह्रदाः पूर्णा रसालस्य दध्नश्श्वेतस्य चापरे। बभूवुः पायसस्यान्ये शर्करायावसञ्चयाः।।2.91.74।।
168.e: There were thousands of pots, lakhs of plates, crores of vessels -- all made of gold and filled with wellgarnished food. Curd was kept in earthern pots like jugs and jars and pots with a wide mouth. Tanks were formed, some filled with white curd of good flavour and of the colour of woodapple, some with white curd blended with spices and some with payasam and heaps of barely powder mixed with sugar.

168.sa: पात्रीणां च सहस्राणि स्थालीनां नियुतानि च। न्यर्बुधानि च पात्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च।।2.91.72।। स्थाल्यः कुम्भ्य करम्भ्य श्च दधिपूर्णास्सुसंस्कृताः। यौवनस्थस्य गौरस्य कपित्थस्य सुगन्धिनः।।2.91.73।। ह्रदाः पूर्णा रसालस्य दध्नश्श्वेतस्य चापरे। बभूवुः पायसस्यान्ये शर्करायावसञ्चयाः।।2.91.74।।
168.e: There were thousands of pots, lakhs of plates, crores of vessels -- all made of gold and filled with wellgarnished food. Curd was kept in earthern pots like jugs and jars and pots with a wide mouth. Tanks were formed, some filled with white curd of good flavour and of the colour of woodapple, some with white curd blended with spices and some with payasam and heaps of barely powder mixed with sugar.

168.sa: पात्रीणां च सहस्राणि स्थालीनां नियुतानि च। न्यर्बुधानि च पात्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च।।2.91.72।। स्थाल्यः कुम्भ्य करम्भ्य श्च दधिपूर्णास्सुसंस्कृताः। यौवनस्थस्य गौरस्य कपित्थस्य सुगन्धिनः।।2.91.73।। ह्रदाः पूर्णा रसालस्य दध्नश्श्वेतस्य चापरे। बभूवुः पायसस्यान्ये शर्करायावसञ्चयाः।।2.91.74।।
168.e: There were thousands of pots, lakhs of plates, crores of vessels -- all made of gold and filled with wellgarnished food. Curd was kept in earthern pots like jugs and jars and pots with a wide mouth. Tanks were formed, some filled with white curd of good flavour and of the colour of woodapple, some with white curd blended with spices and some with payasam and heaps of barely powder mixed with sugar.

168.sa: कल्कान्चूर्णकषायांश्च स्नानानि विविधानि च। ददृशुर्भाजनस्थानि तीर्थेषु सरतां नराः।।2.91.75।।
168.e: The soldiers saw on the river banks at landing places levigated powder, fragrant powder and extracts and other bathing requisites of different kinds stored in receptacles.

168.sa: शुक्लानंशुमतश्चापि दन्तधावनसञ्चयान्। शुक्लांश्चन्दनकल्कांश्च समुद्गेष्ववतिष्ठतः।।2.91.76।। दर्पणापरिमृष्टांश्च वाससां चापि सञ्चयान्। पादुकोपानहां चैव युग्मानिच सहस्रशः।।2.91.77।। आञ्जनीः कङ्कतान्कूर्चान् शस्त्राणि च धनूंषि च। मर्मत्राणानि चित्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च।।2.91.78।। प्रतिपानह्रदान्पूर्णन्खरोष्ट्रगजवाजिनाम्। अवगाह्यसुतीर्थांश्चह्रदान् सोत्पलपुष्करान्।2.91.79।। आकाश वर्णप्रतिमान् स्वच्छतोयान्सुखप्लवान्। नीपवैडूर्यवर्णांश्च मृदून्यवससञ्चयान्। निर्वापार्थान् पशूनां ते ददृशुस्तत्र सर्वशः।।2.91.80।।
168.e: There the soldiers beheld on every side stacks of toothbrushing sticks, white and bristled, white lumps of sandal paste placed in dishes made of leaves, well cleaned mirrors, collection of clothes, several pairs of footwear, collyrium boxes, combs, brushes for cleaning moustaches, weapons, parasoles, bows and shining armour, different kinds of couches, and seats. There were pools of drinking water for donkeys, camels, elephants and horses and excellent landing places filled with flowering lotuses and water lilies. The lakes were of transparent waters resembling the hue of the sky easy and comfortable for swimming. There they saw heaps of soft grass as green as sapphire and kadamva trees for animals to refresh themselves under.

168.sa: शुक्लानंशुमतश्चापि दन्तधावनसञ्चयान्। शुक्लांश्चन्दनकल्कांश्च समुद्गेष्ववतिष्ठतः।।2.91.76।। दर्पणापरिमृष्टांश्च वाससां चापि सञ्चयान्। पादुकोपानहां चैव युग्मानिच सहस्रशः।।2.91.77।। आञ्जनीः कङ्कतान्कूर्चान् शस्त्राणि च धनूंषि च। मर्मत्राणानि चित्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च।।2.91.78।। प्रतिपानह्रदान्पूर्णन्खरोष्ट्रगजवाजिनाम्। अवगाह्यसुतीर्थांश्चह्रदान् सोत्पलपुष्करान्।2.91.79।। आकाश वर्णप्रतिमान् स्वच्छतोयान्सुखप्लवान्। नीपवैडूर्यवर्णांश्च मृदून्यवससञ्चयान्। निर्वापार्थान् पशूनां ते ददृशुस्तत्र सर्वशः।।2.91.80।।
168.e: There the soldiers beheld on every side stacks of toothbrushing sticks, white and bristled, white lumps of sandal paste placed in dishes made of leaves, well cleaned mirrors, collection of clothes, several pairs of footwear, collyrium boxes, combs, brushes for cleaning moustaches, weapons, parasoles, bows and shining armour, different kinds of couches, and seats. There were pools of drinking water for donkeys, camels, elephants and horses and excellent landing places filled with flowering lotuses and water lilies. The lakes were of transparent waters resembling the hue of the sky easy and comfortable for swimming. There they saw heaps of soft grass as green as sapphire and kadamva trees for animals to refresh themselves under.

168.sa: शुक्लानंशुमतश्चापि दन्तधावनसञ्चयान्। शुक्लांश्चन्दनकल्कांश्च समुद्गेष्ववतिष्ठतः।।2.91.76।। दर्पणापरिमृष्टांश्च वाससां चापि सञ्चयान्। पादुकोपानहां चैव युग्मानिच सहस्रशः।।2.91.77।। आञ्जनीः कङ्कतान्कूर्चान् शस्त्राणि च धनूंषि च। मर्मत्राणानि चित्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च।।2.91.78।। प्रतिपानह्रदान्पूर्णन्खरोष्ट्रगजवाजिनाम्। अवगाह्यसुतीर्थांश्चह्रदान् सोत्पलपुष्करान्।2.91.79।। आकाश वर्णप्रतिमान् स्वच्छतोयान्सुखप्लवान्। नीपवैडूर्यवर्णांश्च मृदून्यवससञ्चयान्। निर्वापार्थान् पशूनां ते ददृशुस्तत्र सर्वशः।।2.91.80।।
168.e: There the soldiers beheld on every side stacks of toothbrushing sticks, white and bristled, white lumps of sandal paste placed in dishes made of leaves, well cleaned mirrors, collection of clothes, several pairs of footwear, collyrium boxes, combs, brushes for cleaning moustaches, weapons, parasoles, bows and shining armour, different kinds of couches, and seats. There were pools of drinking water for donkeys, camels, elephants and horses and excellent landing places filled with flowering lotuses and water lilies. The lakes were of transparent waters resembling the hue of the sky easy and comfortable for swimming. There they saw heaps of soft grass as green as sapphire and kadamva trees for animals to refresh themselves under.

The lakes were of transparent waters resembling the hue of the sky easy and comfortable for swimming. There they saw heaps of soft grass as green as sapphire and kadamva trees for animals to refresh themselves under.
