177.sa: धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधाः। बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते।।2.100.39।।
177.e: While principal scriptures do exist, these superficial fellows take resort to the science of logic based on abstract reasoning, and indulge in futile talks.

177.sa: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
177.e: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

177.sa: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
177.e: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

177.sa: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यै स्स्वकर्मनिरतैस्सदा। जितेन्द्रियैर्महोत्साहैर्वृतामार्यै स्सहस्रशः।।2.100.41।। प्रासादैर्विविधाकारैर्वृतां वैद्यजनाकुलाम्। कच्चित्सुमुदितां स्फीतामयोध्यां परिरक्षसि।।2.100.42।।
177.e: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of venerable, selfcontrolled and highly energetic brahmins, kshatriyas and vaisyas engaged in their respective professions, filled with palaces of various kinds, abounding in learned people and a prosperous city where everything is available in abundance.

177.sa: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
177.e: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

177.sa: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
177.e: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

177.sa: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
177.e: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

177.sa: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सवशोभितः। सुकृष्टसीमा पशुमान्हिंसाभिः परिवर्जितः।।2.100.44।। अदेवमातृको रम्य श्श्वापदैः परिवर्जितः। परित्यक्तो भयैस्सर्वैः खनिभिश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.45।। विवर्जितो नरैः पापैर्मम पूर्वै स्सुरक्षितः। कच्चिज्जनपदस्स्फीतः सुखं वसति राघव।।2.100.46।।
177.e: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and rich in cattlewealth, free from violence and independent of rain. It is enchanting. It is safe from wild animals. With fears expelled, free from sinful people, adorned with mines and wellprotected by my ancestors, it is prosperous and I hope people are living comfortably.

177.sa: कच्चित्ते दयितास्सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः। वार्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते।।2.100.47।।
177.e: I trust all those men who live on agriculture and cattlerearing are favourable to you. The world's prosperity, dear brother, grows on the profession of cattle rearing.

177.sa: तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारैः कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम्। रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिनः।।2.100.48।।
177.e: I trust you nourish them and also afford portection and prevent adversities. A king must protect all those people living in his country in accordanc with righteousness.

177.sa: कच्चिस्त्रिय स्सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिताः। कच्चिन्न श्रद्धास्यासां कच्चिद्गुह्यं न भाषसे।।2.100.49।।
177.e: I trust, you keep the women pacified and wellprotected, you do not believe their words and do not divulge any secrets to them.

177.sa: कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित्ते सन्ति धेनुकाः। कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि।।2.100.50।।
177.e: I trust, you protect the habitat of elephants and you have a large number of milch cows. I trust you are not contented with the existing number of female and male elephants and horses.

177.sa: कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम्। उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे।।2.100.51।।
177.e: O prince, I trust, you rise early daily and present yourself welladomed to the people on the thoroughfare.

177.sa: कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ताः प्रत्यक्षास्तेऽविशङ्कया। सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम्।।2.100.52।।
177.e: All the servants, I trust, do not present themselves to you directly. At the same time they do not remain out of sight with fear at a distance. The middle course is the best way for the welfare of every one.

177.sa: कच्चित्सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकैः। यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः।।2.100.53।।
177.e: Hope all the forts are adequately provided with wealth, foodgrains, weapons and water, with machines of war and craftsmen and archers.

177.sa: आयस्ते विपुलः कच्चित्कच्चिदल्पतरो व्ययः। अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव।।2.100.54।।
177.e: O Bharata, I trust, your revenues are abundant and expenditure much less. I trust you do not give away your treasure to undeserving persons.

177.sa: देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थेब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च। योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्ययः।।2.100.55।।
177.e: I trust, you are spending only on gods, ancestors, brahmins, guests, warriors and hosts of friends.

177.sa: कच्चिदार्यो विशुद्धात्मा क्षारित श्चापरकर्मणा। अपृष्ट श्शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्वध्यते शुचिः।।2.100.56।।
177.e: I trust a man who is honest, purehearted and venerable, falsely accused of adultery is not slain out of avarice without consulting experts in scriptures.

177.sa: गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्टस्सकारणः। कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ।।2.100.57।।
177.e: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

177.sa: व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्गतस्य च राघव। अर्थं विरागाः पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुताः।।2.100.58।।
177.e: O Bharata, I trust that your ministers are wellinformed and look into all matters in times of hardship pertaining to whether a man is rich or poor without any bias to either.

177.sa: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव। तानि पुत्रान्पशून्घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः।।2.100.59।।
177.e: O Bharata, the tears falling from the eyes of persons, who are falsely accused and punished for the pleasure of the king will destroy his progeny and cattle as well.

177.sa: कच्चिद्वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च वैद्यामुख्यांश्च राघव। दानेन मनसा वाचा त्रिभिरेतैर्बुभूषसे।।2.100.60।।
177.e: O Bharata, I trust you wish to thrive by treating the old, children and foremost of learned people with the three expedients namely gifts, affection and kind words.

177.sa: कच्चिद्गुरूंश्च वृद्धांश्च तापसान् देवतातिथीन्। चैत्यांश्च सर्वान्सिध्दार्थान्ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यसि।।2.100.61।।
177.e: I trust you pay homage to the preceptors, the aged ones, ascetics, gods and guests, to shrines and to accomplished brahmins.

177.sa: कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुनः। उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन च न बाधसे।।2.100.62।।
177.e: I trust, righteousness for the sake of prosperity or prosperity for the sake of righteousness or both for the sake of sensual pleasure are not thwarted by you.

177.sa: कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर। विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान्वरद सेवसे।।2.100.63।।
177.e: O Bharata, the best among the victorious, conversant with timely actions and a bestower of boons you are the best of men. I trust, you allocate adequate time for attending to all the three expedients of life like dharma, artha and kama.

177.sa: कच्चित्ते ब्राह्मणा श्शर्म सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदाः। आशंसन्ते महाप्राज्ञ पौरजानपदैस्सह।।2.100.64।।
177.e: O highly sagacious Bharata, those brahmins who can comprehend the meaning of all scriptures along with the inhabitants of the city and country, I trust, are seeking your happiness.

177.sa: नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
177.e: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

177.sa: नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
177.e: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

177.sa: नास्तिक्यमनृतं क्रोधं प्रमादं दीर्घसूत्रताम्। अदर्शनं ज्ञानवतामालस्यं पञ्चवृत्तिताम्।।2.100.65।। एकचिन्तनमर्थानामनर्थज्ञैश्च मन्त्रणम्। निश्चितानामनारम्भं मन्त्रस्यापरिरक्षणम्।।2.100.66।। मङ्गलाद्यप्रयोगं च प्रत्युत्थानं च सर्वतः। कच्चित्वं वर्जयस्येतान्राजदोषांश्चतुर्दश।।2.100.67।।
177.e: I trust you eschew the fourteen faults of kings, like atheism, falsehood, anger, inattention, procrastination, evading the wise, indolence, gratification of all five senses, planning alone in the affairs of the kingdom, consultation with people who are proficient in worthless acts, failure to implement decisious, inability to keep the counsel secret and omission of auspicious practices and setting out against all the enemies at a time.

177.sa: दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
177.e: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

177.sa: दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
177.e: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

177.sa: दशपञ्चचतुर्वर्गान्सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वतः। अष्टवर्गं त्रिवर्गं च विद्यास्तिस्रश्च राघव।।2.100.68।। इन्द्रियाणां जयं बुद्ध्या षाड्गुण्यं दैवमानुषम्। कृत्यं विंशतिवर्गं च तथा प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.100.69।। यात्रादण्डविधानं च द्वियोनी सन्धिविग्रहौ। कच्चिदेतान्महाप्राज्ञ यथावदनुमन्यसे।।2.100.70।।
177.e: O highly sagacious Bharata, I trust, having understood their true nature you are appropriately following the ten, five and four divisions, the seven divisions, the eight divisions, the three divisions, three kinds of knowledge, victory over the senses, the six qualities, evils arising from destiny and human agency, kritya, division of twenty, similarly Prakriti and Mandalas and two sources of Yatra and chastisement and of peace and war.

177.sa: मन्त्रिभिस्त्वं यथोद्दिष्टैश्चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव वा। कच्चित्समस्तैर्व्यस्तैश्च मन्त्रं मन्त्रयसे मिथः।।2.100.71।।
177.e: I trust you deliberate in secrecy on your counsel with three or four counsellors, together and separately with each one, as laid down in sacred texts.

177.sa: कच्चित्ते सफला वेदाः कच्चित्ते सफलाः क्रियाः। कच्चित्ते सफला दाराः कच्चित्ते सफलं श्रुतम्।।2.100.72।।
177.e: I trust, the Vedas you have studied are fruitful, the acts which you commenced are productive, your wife is fruitful (blessed with a son) and the scriptures you studied are useful.

177.sa: कच्चिदेषैव ते बुद्धिर्यथोक्ता मम राघव। आयुष्या च यशस्या च धर्मकामार्थ संहिता।।2.100.73।।
177.e: O Bharata, I trust your intellect is in conformity with what I said conducive to long life, and fame in accordance with righteousness, (legitimate) pleasure and prosperity.

177.sa: यां वृत्तिं वर्तते तातो यां च नः प्रपितामहाः। तां वृत्तिं वर्तसे कच्चिद्याच सत्पथगा शुभा।।2.100.74।।
177.e: I trust, you walk the auspicious path of truth (virtue) followed by our father and forefathers.

177.sa: कच्चित्स्वादु कृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव। कच्चिदाशंसमानेभ्यो मित्रेभ्य स्सम्प्रयच्छसि।।2.100.75।।
177.e: O Bharata, I trust you do not partake delicious food all by yourself, and you share it with your friends when they want it.

177.sa: राजा तु धर्मेण हि पालयित्वा महामतिर्दण्डधरः प्रजानाम्। अवाप्य कृत्स्नां वसुधां यथावदितश्च्युत स्स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान्।।2.100.76।।
177.e: The highly sagacious and learned king, having acquired the entire earth and punishing the people in accordance with tradition and righteously ruling the kingdom, will ascend the his release (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे शततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

178.sa: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। किं मे धर्माद्विहीनस्य राजधर्मः करिष्यति।।2.101.1।।
178.e: On listening to Rama, Bharata replied Of what use shall be these royal duties to me, when I have fallen from righteousness?

178.sa: शाश्वतोऽयं सदा धर्मः स्थितोऽस्मासु नरर्षभ। ज्येष्ठेे पुत्रे स्थिते राजा न कनीयान् भवेन्नृपः।।2.101.2।।
178.e: O best of men there is an ancient tradition in our race that the younger son cannot become king when the eldest is there.

178.sa: स समृद्धां मया सार्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव। अभिषेचयचात्मानं कुलस्यास्य भवाय नः।।2.101.3।।
178.e: Therefore, O scion of the Raghu race, return along with me to prosperous Ayodhya and for the good of our race get your self coronated.

178.sa: राजानं मानुषं प्राहु र्देवत्वे सम्मतो मम। यस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वृत्तमाहुरमानुषम्।।2.101.4।।
178.e: Other think the king to be a human, but to me, he is divine since his conduct and the statecraft are superhuman as they are in conformity with righteousness.

178.sa: केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्य माश्रिते। दिवमार्यो गतो राजा यायजूक: सतां मतः।।2.101.5।।
178.e: While I was in Kekaya and you took refuge in the forest, venerable king (Dasaratha), who was always engaged in sacrifices and was held in high esteem by the virtuous, ascended to heaven.

178.sa: निष्क्रान्तमात्रे भवति ससीते सहलक्ष्मणे। दुःखशोकाभिभूतस्तु राजा त्रिदिवमभ्यगात्।।2.101.6।।
178.e: As soon as you set out for the forest along with Sita and Lakshmana, the king, overwhelmed with grief, attained heaven.

178.sa: उत्तिष्ठ पुरुषव्याघ्र क्रियतामुदकं पितुः। अहं चायं च शत्रुघ्नः पूर्वमेव कृतोदकौ।।2.101.7।।
178.e: Arise, O best of men and offer libations to our father. I and Satrughna have already done so.

178.sa: प्रियेण किल दत्तं हि पितृलोकेषु राघव। अक्षय्यं भवतीत्याहुर्भवांश्चैव पितुः प्रियः।।2.101.8।।
178.e: O son of Raghu's race, it is said that whatever is offered by a dear son becomes eternal in the world of manes. You alone are the beloved son of our father.

178.sa: त्वामेव शोचंस्तव दर्शनेप्सुस्त्वय्येव सक्तामनिवर्त्य बुद्धिम्। त्वया विहीन स्तव शोकमग्नस्त्वां संस्मरन्नस्तमितः पिता ते।।2.101.9।।
178.e: Your father, deprived of you, brooding over you, wishing to behold you, unable to divert his mind fixed on you, remembering you alone and immersed in sorrow departed (from this world). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोत्तर शततम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredone sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

179.sa: तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम्। राघवो भरते नोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः।।2.102.1।।
179.e: Having heard the words of Bharata regarding the death of his father, Rama became unconscious.

179.sa: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
179.e: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

179.sa: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
179.e: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

179.sa: तं तु वज्रमिवोत्सृष्टमाहवे दानवारिणा वाग्वज्रंभरते नोक्त ममनोज्ञं परन्तपः।।2.102.2।। प्रगृह्य रामो बाहू वैपुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुमः। वने परशुना कृत्तस्तथा भुवि पपात ह।।2.102.3।।
179.e: On hearing the thunderlike words spoken by Bharata afflicting the mind, like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra (enemy of demons) in a battle, Rama, the scorcher of enemies, stretching forth both his arms, fell down on the ground like a tree with flowering tops severed by an axe in the forest.

179.sa: तथा हि पतितं रामं जगत्यां जगतीपतिम्। कूलघातपरिश्रान्तं प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।2.102. 4।। भ्रातरस्ते महेष्वासं सर्वतश्शोककर्शितम्। रुदन्तस्सह वैदेह्या सिषिचुस्सलिलेन वै।।2.102.5।।
179.e: Those brothers on all sides, with Sita lamenting, sprinkled water on Rama, the great archer and lord of the earth who, afflicted with grief, had fallen down on the ground, and was lying like an elephant exhausted from repeatedly striking a river bank.

179.sa: स तु संज्ञां पुनर्लब्ध्वा नेत्राभ्यामस्रमुत्सृजन्। उपाक्रामत काकुत्स्थ कृपणं बहु भाषितुम्।।2.102.6।।
179.e: On regaining consciousness, shedding tears profusely, Rama again started speaking piteously.

179.sa: स रामस्स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा पितरं पृथिवीपतिम्। उवाच भरतं वाक्यं धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम्।।2.102.7।।
179.e: On hearing that his father, king Dasaratha, the lord of the world had attained heaven, righteous Rama said to Bharata in conformty with his rightful conduct.

179.sa: किं करिष्याम्ययोध्यायां ताते दिष्टां गतिं गते। कस्तां राजवराध्दीनामयोध्यां पालयिष्यति।।2.102.8।।
179.e: What shall I do in Ayodhya now that my father has followed the path ordained by the gods? Who will rule that Ayodhya deprived of that best of kings?

179.sa: किं नु तस्य मया कार्यं दुर्जातेन महात्मनः। यो मृतो मम शोकेन मया चापि न संस्कृतः।।2.102.9।।
179.e: I could not even perform the last rites of that magnanimous one who died of grief on account of me. What use is my life with an unlucky birth?

179.sa: अहो भरत सिद्धार्थो येन राजा त्वयाऽनघ। शत्रुघ्नेन च सर्वेषु प्रेतकृत्येषु सत्कृतः।।2.102.10।।
179.e: O irreproachable Bharata, it is gratifying that you and Satrughna are indeed fortunate to have fulfilled your cherished desire since the king was wellhonoured by you with all the obsequial rites.

179.sa: निष्प्रधानामनेकाग्रां नरेन्द्रेण विनाकृताम्। निवृत्तवनवासोऽपि नायोध्यां गन्तु मुत्सहे।।2.102.11।।
179.e: Even after the completion of my exile I do not wish to return to Ayodhya which is directionless, bereft of its chief, the king.

179.sa: समाप्तवनवासं मामयोध्यायां परन्तप। कोऽनु शासिष्यति पुनस्ताते लोकान्तरं गते।।2.102.12।।
179.e: O subduer of enemies, when father has gone to the other world, who will guide me in Ayodhya after I complete my term of exile?

179.sa: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्। वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतश्श्रोत्रसुखान्यहम्।।2.102.13।।
179.e: On seeing my good conduct our father used to say comforting words to me. Now from whom can I hear such words pleasing to the ears?

179.sa: एवमुक्त्वा स भरतं भार्यामभ्येत्य राघवः। उवाच शोकसन्तप्तः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्।।2.102.14।।
179.e: Having thus spoken to Bharata, Rama, overwhelmed with grief, approached his wife Sita whose face looked like the full Moon, and said to her.

179.sa: सीते मृतस्ते श्वशुरः पित्रा हीनोऽसि लक्ष्मण। भरतो दुःखमाचष्टे स्वर्गतं पृथिवीपतिम्।।2.102.15।।
179.e: O Sita, your fatherinlaw is dead. O Lakshmana, you are deprived of your father. Bharata is relating to me the sad news that king Dasaratha has attained his heavenly abode.

179.sa: ततो बहुगुणं तेषां बाष्पं नेत्रेष्वजायत। तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कुमाराणां यशस्विनाम्।।2.102.16।।
179.e: While the scion of the Kakutsthas was saying thus, copious tears welled up from the eyes of all those illustrious sons of Dasaratha.

179.sa: ततस्ते भ्रातर  स्रव्रॆ भृशमाश्वास्य दु:खितम्। अब्रुवन् जगतीभर्तुः क्रियतामुदकं पितुः।।2.102.17।।
179.e: All the brothers, having consoled Rama as best they could, told him, Let the libations be offered to our father, the protector of the world.

179.sa: सा सीता स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा श्वशुरं  तं महानृपम्। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्या शशाकेक्षितुं प्रियम्।।2.102.18।।
179.e: On hearing that her fatherinlaw, king Dasaratha, had attained heaven, Sita, her eyes filled with tears could not look at her husband in the face.

179.sa: सान्त्वयित्वा तु तां रामो रुदन्तीं जनकात्मजाम्। उवाच लक्ष्मणं तत्र दुःखितो दुःखितं वचः।।2.102.19।।
179.e: Having consoled Sita, daughter of Janaka, griefstricken Rama said to Lakshmana who was also distressed with grief.

179.sa: आनयेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं चीरमाहर चोत्तरम्। जलक्रियार्थं तातस्य गमिष्यामि महात्मनः।।2.102.20।।
179.e: I shall go and offer libations to my magnanimous father. Go and fetch the dried pulp of ingudi fruit and an upper garment made of bark.

179.sa: सीता पुरस्ताद्व्रजतु त्वमेनामभितो व्रज। अहं पश्चाद्गमिष्यामि गतिर्ह्येषा सुदारुणा।।2.102.21।।
179.e: Let us proceed in this order -- you first, Sita second and I last. This procession  in mourning is terrible indeed.

179.sa: ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः। मृदुर्दान्तश्च कान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान्।।2.102.22।। सुमन्त्र स्तैर्नृपसुतैस्सार्धमाश्वस्य राघवम्। अवातारयदालम्ब्य नदीं मन्दाकिनीं शिवाम्।।2.102.23।।
179.e: Thereafter, their constant follower Sumantra who was conversant in spiritual knowledge, a highminded person, softnatured, selfcontrolled, tranquilminded and staunchly devoted to Rama consoled him. Holding the hands of the princes, Sumantra helped their descent into the auspicious river Mandakini for taking bath.

179.sa: ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामतिः। मृदुर्दान्तश्च शान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान्।।2.102.22।। सुमन्त्रस्तैर्नृपसुतैः सार्धमाश्वास्य राघवम्। अवातारयदालम्ब्य नदीं मन्दाकिनीं शिवाम्।।2.102.23।।
179.e: Thereafter, their constant follower Sumantra who was conversant in spiritual knowledge, a highminded person, softnatured, selfcontrolled, tranquilminded and staunchly devoted to Rama consoled him. Holding the hands of the princes, Sumantra helped their descent into the auspicious river Mandakini for taking bath.

179.sa: ते सुतीर्थां ततः कृच्छ्रादुपागम्य यशस्विनः। नदीं मन्दाकिनीं रम्यां सदा पुष्पितकाननाम्।।2.102.24।। शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्दमम्। सिषिचु स्तूदकं राज्ञे तत एतद् भवत्विति।।2.102.25।।
179.e: The illustrious brothers approached with great difficulty the swiftflowing and enchanting river Mandakini which had convenient descent and endowed with forests always in bloom. They descended at an auspicious place that was not slushy and offered libations of water saying 'O father, let these offerings be yours'.

179.sa: ते सुतीर्थां ततः कृच्छ्रादुपागम्य यशस्विनः। नदीं मन्दाकिनीं रम्यां सदा पुष्पितकाननाम्।।2.102.24।। शीघ्रस्रोतसमासाद्य तीर्थं शिवमकर्दमम्। सिषिचु स्तूदकं राज्ञे तातैतत्ते भवत्विति।।2.102.25।।
179.e: The illustrious brothers approached with great difficulty the swiftflowing and enchanting river Mandakini which had convenient descent and endowed with forests always in bloom. They descended at an auspicious place that was not slushy and offered libations of water saying 'O father, let these offerings be yours'.

179.sa: प्रगृह्य च महीपालो जलपूरितमञ्जलिम्। दिशं याम्यामभिमुखो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.102.26।।
179.e: Rama, the ruler of the earth, held water with both palms cupped and, facing the south, the direction of Yama (the god of death) said these words, sobbing:

179.sa: एतत्ते राजशार्दूल विमलं तोयमक्षयम्। पितृलोकगत स्याद्य मद्दत्तमुपतिष्ठतु।।2.102.27।।
179.e: 'O best of kings, you are gone to the world of the manes, and let this inexhaustible libation of pure water reach you'.

179.sa: ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरात्प्रत्युत्तीर्य स राघवः। पितुश्चकार तेजस्वी निर्वापं भ्रातृभि सह।।2.102.28।।
179.e: Then, the powerful scion of the Raghu race reached bank, from the bathing spot of the river Mandakini along with his brothers and offered pinda (an offering of rice flour to the departed) to his late lamented father.

179.sa: ऐङ्गुदं बदरीमिश्रं पिण्याकं दर्भसंस्तरे। न्यस्य रामस्सदुःखार्तो रुदन्वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.102.29।।
179.e: Placing the balls of ingudi pulp mixed with badari fruit on a spread of darbha grass, Rama, was overcome with grief and weeping, said:

179.sa: इदं भुङ्क्ष्वमहाराज प्रीतो यदशना वयम्। यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्ना स्तस्य देवताः।।2.102.30।।
179.e: O great king, we offer you such food as we partake now. Be pleased to accept it. For,  his gods are offered the food a man takes.

179.sa: तत स्तेनैव मार्गेण प्रत्युत्तीर्य सरित्तटात्। आरुरोह नरव्याघ्रो रम्यसानुं महीधरम्।।2.102.31।।
179.e: Rama, the tiger among men, ascending the riverbank and proceeding on the same path (he had come), climbed the (Chitrakuta) mountain of charming slopes.

179.sa: ततः पर्णकुटीद्वारमासाद्य जगतीपतिः। परिजग्राह बाहुभ्यामुभौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ।।2.102.32।।
179.e: Rama, lord of the earth, reached the door of the leafhut and took Bharata and Lakshmana in his arms.

179.sa: तेषां तु रुदतां शब्दात् प्रतिशब्दोऽभवद् गिरौ। भ्रातॄणां सह वैदेह्या सिंहानां नर्दतामिव।।2.102.33।।
179.e: The mountain echoed with the sound of lamentations of all the brothers along with Sita which resembled the roar of lions.

179.sa: महाबलानां रुदतां कुर्वतामुदकं पितुः। विज्ञाय तुमुलं शब्दं त्रस्ता भरत सैनिकाः।।2.102.34।
179.e: The soldiers of Bharata were alarmed on hearing the tumultuous sounds raised by those mighty brothers offering libations of water and lamenting.

179.sa: अब्रुवंश्चापि रामेण भरत संगतो ध्रुवम्। तेषामेव महान् श‌ब्द: शोचतां पितरं मृतम्।।2.102.35।।
179.e: They said, 'Bharata must have joined Rama. That loud noise must be their wailing over their deceased father'.

179.sa: अथ वासान्परित्यज्य तं सर्वेऽभिमुखास्स्वनम्। अप्येकमनसो जग्मुर्यथास्थानं प्रधाविताः।।2.102.36।।
179.e: Then all of them left their camps with one single thought (of seeing Rama) in their minds and ran in the direction from where that sound emanated.

179.sa: हयैरन्ये गजैरन्ये रथैरन्ये स्वलङ्कृतैः। सुकुमारा स्तथैवान्ये पद्भिरेव नरा ययुः।।2.102.37।।
179.e: Some rode horses, some, elephants, while others mounted welldecorated chariots, while the young went on foot.

179.sa: अचिरप्रोषितं रामं चिरविप्रोषितं यथा। द्रष्टुकामो जनः सर्वो जगाम सहसाऽऽश्रमम्।।2.102.38।।
179.e: The whole multitude of people at once rushed towards the hermitage wishing to see Rama as if he had left long ago though he had gone on exile very recently.

179.sa: भ्रातृ़णां त्वरितास्ते तु द्रष्टुकामा स‌मागमम्। ययुर्बहुविधैर्यानै: खुरनेमिस्वनाकुलैः।।2.102.39।।
179.e: Eager to see the union of brothers, all those people went by every sort of vehicle filled with the sounds of hooves and wheels.

179.sa: सा भूमिर्बहुभिर्यानैः रथ‌नेमिसमाहता। मुमोच तुमुलं शब्दं द्यौरिवाभ्रसमागमे।।2.102.40।।
179.e: The earth crushed by several vehicles, hooves (of horses) and wheels (of chariots) emitted tumultuous sounds like the sky in the gathering stormclouds.

179.sa: तेन वित्रासिता नागाः करेणुपरिवारिताः। आवासयन्तो गन्धेन जग्मुरन्यद्वनं ततः।।2.102.41।।
179.e: Frightened by the sound, the elephants followed by their females, spreading all the way the odour of the ichor, moved to other forests.

179.sa: वराह वृकसङ्घाश्च महिषा: सृमरास्तथा । व्याघ्रगोकर्णगवया वित्रेसुः पृषतै स‌ह।।2.102.42।।
179.e: Hearing that sound, hosts of boars and deer, buffaloes, serpents and apes, tigers, antelopes with ears like the cows', gavayas as well as dappled antelopes were all frightened.

179.sa: रथाङ्गसाह्वा नत्यूहा हंसाः कारण्डवाः परे। तथा पुंस्कोकिलाः क्रौञ्चा विसंज्ञा भेजिरे दिशः।।2.102.43।।
179.e: Ducks, watercranes, geese, karandavas, cranes, male cuckoos and kraunchas fled senselessly in different directions.

179.sa: तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तैराकाशं पक्षिभिर्वृतम्। मनुष्यैरावृता भूमिरुभयं प्रबभौ तदा।।2.102.44।।
179.e: The sky was filled with birds frightened by the sound and the earth covered with people. Both looked extremely beautiful.

179.sa: ततस्तं पुरषव्याघ्रं यशस्विनमकल्पषम्। आसीनं स्थण्डिले रामं ददर्श सहसा जनः।।2.102.45।।
179.e: All at once the people saw the illustrious Rama, the best of men, and the subduer of enemies squatting on the bare earth.

179.sa: विगर्हमाणः कैकेयीं मन्थरासहितामपि। अभिगम्य जनो रामं बाष्पपूर्णमुखोऽभवत्।।2.102.46।।
179.e: All those men with faces full of tears, reproaching Kaikeyi and Manthara (all the way), approached Rama.

179.sa: तान्नरान्बाष्पपूर्णाक्षान्समीक्ष्याथ सुदुःखितान्। पर्यष्वजत धर्मज्ञः पितृवन्मातृवच्च सः।।2.102.47।।
179.e: Thereafter, beholding those people deeply afflicted, their eyes full of tears, Rama embraced them as if they were his own father and mother.

179.sa: स तत्र कांश्चित्परिषस्वजे नरान्नरास्तु केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन्। चकार सर्वान्सवयस्यबान्धवान्यथार्ह मासाद्य तदा नृपात्मजः।।2.102.48।।
179.e: Rama embraced some, while others paid him obeisance. Therafter, he honoured his erstwhile companions and relations in accordance with their status.

179.sa: स तत्र तेषां रुदतां महात्मनां भुवं च खं चानुनिनादयन्स्वनः। गुहा गिरीणां च दिशश्च सन्ततं मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिमः प्रशुश्रुवे।।2.102.49।।
179.e: The weeping and the tumult of those magnanimous people made the earth, sky, mountaincaves and all quarters reverberate incessantly like the beating of drums. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्व्युत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundred and second sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

180.sa: वसिष्ठः पुरतः कृत्वा दारान्दशरथस्य च। अभिचक्राम तं देशं रामदर्शनतर्षितः।।2.103.1।।
180.e: Longing to see Rama, Vasistha, headed by the wives of Dasaratha, set out on foot (where Rama was offering libations).

180.sa: राजपत्न्यश्च गच्छन्त्यो मन्दं मन्दाकिनीं प्रति। ददृशु स्तत्र तत् तीर्थं रामलक्ष्मणसेवितम्।।2.103.2।।
180.e: The wives of the king while proceeding slowly towards the river Mandakini beheld the bathing place frequented by Rama and Lakshmana.

180.sa: कौसल्या बाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता। सुमित्रामब्रवीद्दीना याश्चान्या राजयोषितः।।2.103.3।।
180.e: Kausalya, with eyes filled with tears and her face emaciated, addressing Sumitra and the other wives of the king sadly said:

180.sa: इदं तेषामनाथानां क्लिष्टमक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्। वने प्राक्कलनं तीर्थं ये ते निर्विषयीकृताः।।2.103.4।।
180.e: This is a sacred place to the east of the forest used by the unfortunate Rama, and Lakshmana of untiring energy and Sita expelled from the country and undergoing suffering.

180.sa: इत स्सुमित्रे पुत्रस्ते सदा जलमतन्द्रितः। स्वयं हरति सौमित्रिर्मम पुत्रस्य कारणात्।।2.103.5।।
180.e: O Sumitra, your son Lakshmana, free from laziness, always carries water from here for the sake of my son.

180.sa: जघन्यमपि ते पुत्रः कृतवान् न तु गर्हितः। भ्रातुर्यदर्थरहितं सर्वं तद् गर्हितंं गुणैः।।2.103.6।।
180.e: Your son, though engaged in servile tasks (like bringing water), is not to be held contemptible because all the services intended for the benefit of his brother are prompted by virtue.

180.sa: अद्यायमपि ते पुत्रः क्लेशानामतथोचितः। नीचानर्थ समाचारं सज्जं कर्म प्रमुञ्चतु।।2.103.7।।
180.e: This your son unaccustomed to, and undeserving of, any suffering may now give up this mean and distressing duty entrusted to him.

180.sa: दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु सा ददर्श महीतले। पितुरिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं न्यस्तमायतलोचना।।2.103.8।।
180.e: That largeeyed Kausalya beheld the cakes of ingudi pulp placed by Rama for his father on a spread of darbha grass whose blades pointed toward the south.

180.sa: तं भूमौ पितुरार्तेन न्यस्तं रामेण वीक्ष्य सा। उवाच देवी कौसल्या सर्वा दशरथस्त्रियः।।2.103.9।।
180.e: Seeing the pinda (edible offering made to the departed soul) placed on the ground for his father by the distressed Rama, queen Kausalya, addressing all the wives of Dasaratha, said:

180.sa: इदमिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः। राघवेण पितुर्दत्तं पश्यतैतद्यथाविधि।।2.103.10।।
180.e: Have darsan of this pinda offered by Rama according to tradition to his magnanimous father, Dasaratha, lord of the Ikshvaku race.

180.sa: तस्य देवसमानस्य पार्थिवस्य महात्मनः। नैतदौपयिकं मन्ये भुक्तभोगस्य भोजनम्।।2.103.11।।
180.e: I do not think that this is an appropriate food for that godlike and great lord of the earth who enjoyed all luxury.

180.sa: चतुरन्तां महीं भुक्त्वा महेन्द्रसदृशो विभुः। कथमिङ्गुदिपिण्याकं स भुक्ते वसुधाधिपः।।2.103.12।।
180.e: How can Indralike Dasaratha, having ruled the earth bounded by four oceans, eat a cake of ingudi pulp?

180.sa: अतो दुःखतरं लोके न किञ्चित्प्रतिभाति मा। यत्र रामः पितुर्दद्यादिङ्गुदिक्षोदमृद्धिमान्।।2.103.13।।
180.e: Rama (who was once) highly prosperous, had to offer the cake of ingudi pulp to his father. Nothing appears more painful to me than this in this world.

180.sa: रामेणेङ्गुदिपिण्याकं पितुर्दत्तं समीक्ष्य मे। कथं दुःखेन हृदयं न स्फोटति सहस्रधा।।2.103.14।।
180.e: Seeing the offering of cake of ingudi pulp by Rama to his father, how is it that my heart does not break into a thousand pieces in sorrow?

180.sa: श्रुतिस्तु खल्वियं सत्या लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा। यदन्नः पुरुषो भवति तदन्नास्तस्य देवताः।।2.103.15।।
180.e: The wellknown saying in this world is that 'whatever food a man partakes, his gods also partake the same'. This dictum appears true (now).

180.sa: एवमार्तां सपत्न्यस्ता जग्मुराश्वास्य तां तदा। ददृशुश्चाश्रमे रामं स्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम्।।2.103.16।।
180.e: The cowives, having thus consoled the distressed Kausalya, went to the hermitage. There they beheld Rama who looked like a god dislodged from heaven.

180.sa: सर्वभोगैः परित्यक्तं रामं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मातरः। आर्ता मुमुचुरश्रूणि सस्वरं शोककर्शिताः।।2.103.17।।
180.e: Beholding Rama devoid of all luxury, his mothers afflicted with grief, and overcome with sorrow, cried aloud, tears streaming down.

180.sa: तासां रामस्समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणान् शुभान्। मात्रूणां मनुजव्याघ्रस्सर्वासां सत्यसङ्गरः।।2.103.18।।
180.e: Rama, the best among men and true to his promise, rose and touched the auspicious feet of all his mothers (in reverence).

180.sa: ताः पाणिभि स्सुखस्पर्शैर्मृद्वङ्गुलितलै श्शुभैः। प्रममार्जू रजः पृष्ठाद्रामस्यायतलोचनाः।।2.103.19।।
180.e: Those largeeyed queens, their palms with delicate fingers and with auspicious hands with a pleasant touch, wiped the dust from the back of his body.

180.sa: सौमित्रिरपि ता स्सर्वा मातृ़स्सम्प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितः। अभ्यवादयतासक्तं शनै रामादनन्तरम्।।2.103.20।।
180.e: On seeing his mothers, Lakshmana, too, was overcome with grief and with devotion followed Rama and slowly bowed to them with reverence.

180.sa: यथा रामे तथा तस्मिन्सर्वा ववृतिरे स्त्रियः। वृत्तिं दशरथाज्जाते लक्ष्मणे शुभलक्षणे।।2.103.21।।
180.e: All the queens treated Lakshmana, born of Dasaratha and endowed with auspicious qualities, with the same love as they did to Rama.

180.sa: सीताऽपि चरणांस्तासामुपसङ्गृह्य दुःखिता। श्वश्रूणामश्रुपूर्णाक्षी सा बभूवाग्रतः स्थिता।।2.103.22।।
180.e: Sita, too, overcome with grief, grasped the feet of her mothersinlaw and stood before them, her eyes full of tears.

180.sa: तां परिष्वज्य दुःखार्तां माता दुहितरं यथा। वनवासकृशां दीनां कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.103.23।।
180.e: Like a mother to her daughter, Kausalya embraced the wretched Sita, who was afflicted with sorrow, and emaciated due to her stay in the forest, and said to her:

180.sa: विदेहराजस्य सुता स्नुषा दशरथस्य च। रामपत्नी कथं दुःखं सम्प्राप्ता निर्जने वने।।2.103.24।।
180.e: How is it that Sita, daughter of Janaka, king of Videha, daughterinlaw of Dasaratha and wife of Rama, has to undergo such hardships in the lonely forest.

180.sa: पद्ममातपसन्तप्तं परिक्लिष्टमिवोत्पलम्। काञ्चनं रजसा ध्वस्तं क्लिष्टं चन्द्रमिवाम्बुदैः।।2.103.25।। मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाऽश्रयम्। भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भवः।।2.103.26।।
180.e: O Sita, after looking at your countenance, which is like a lotus, scorched by the sunshine, or like a withered waterlily or gold defiled by dust or the Moon obscured by the clouds, the fire of sorrow is burning my mind. The grief in my mind is like fire kindled from the arani (sacrificial faggots) that consumes its own souree. (On a circular wood piece, a wooden stick is placed and churned to produce fire specially in sacrifices is called arani.)

180.sa: पद्ममातपसन्तप्तं परिक्लिष्टमिवोत्पलम्। काञ्चनं रजसा ध्वस्तं क्लिष्टं चन्द्रमिवाम्बुदैः।।2.103.25।। मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाऽश्रयम्। भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भवः।।2.103.26।।
180.e: O Sita, after looking at your countenance, which is like a lotus, scorched by the sunshine, or like a withered waterlily or gold defiled by dust or the Moon obscured by the clouds, the fire of sorrow is burning my mind. The grief in my mind is like fire kindled from the arani (sacrificial faggots) that consumes its own souree. (On a circular wood piece, a wooden stick is placed and churned to produce fire specially in sacrifices is called arani.)

180.sa: ब्रुवन्त्यामेवमार्तायां जनन्यां भरताग्रजः। पादावासाद्य जग्राह वसिष्ठस्य च राघवः।।2.103.27।।
180.e: While Rama's mother was uttering such words in anguish, Rama reached Vasistha and clasped his feet with reverence.

180.sa: पुरोहितस्याग्निसमस्य वै तदा बृहस्पतेरिन्द्रमिवामराधिपः। प्रगृह्य पादौ सुसमृद्धतेजसस्सहैव तेनोपविवेश राघवः।।2.103.28।।
180.e: Rama touched the feet of the family priest Vasistha, a man equivalent to effulgent fire like Indra, the lord of the gods, does to Brihaspati and sat down along with him.

180.sa: ततो जघन्यं सहितै स्समन्त्रिभिः पुरप्रधानैश्च सहैव सैनिकैः। जनेन धर्मज्ञतमेन धर्मवानुपोपविष्टो भरत स्तदाऽग्रजम्।।2.103.29।।
180.e: After Vasistha and Rama sat down, righteous Bharata sat close to his elder brother. Behind him sat his companions, leading citizens, soldiers and righteous men.

180.sa: उपोपविष्ट स्तु तदा स वीर्यवांस्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम्। श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरतः कृताञ्जलिर्यथा महेन्द्रः प्रयतः प्रजापतिम्।।2.103.30।।
180.e: Beholding Rama attired like an ascetic but radiant with a majestic glow, the extremely valiant Bharata sat near him with folded palms like the great Indra purified by religious austerities sits near Brahma, the creator.

180.sa: किमेष वाक्यं भरतोऽद्य राघवं प्रणम्य सत्कृत्य च साधु वक्ष्यति। इतीव तस्यार्यजनस्य तत्त्वतो बभूव कौतूहलमुत्तमं तदा।।2.103.31।।
180.e: All noble people were truly filled with great curiosity as to what Bharata was going to speak, after paying his homage and honouring Rama.

180.sa: स राघव स्सत्यधृति श्च लक्ष्मणो महानुभावो भरत श्च धार्मिकः। वृताः सुहृद्भि श्च विरेजुरध्वरे यथा सदस्यै स्सहितास्त्रयोऽग्नयः।।2.103.32।।
180.e: Rama who was steadfast in truth, Lakshmana of great dignity and righteous Bharata surrounded by their friends were as resplendent as three sacrificial fires encircled by officiating priests. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्य्रुत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredthird sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

181.sa: तं तु राम स्समाश्वास्य भ्रातरं गुरवत्सलम्। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे।।2.104.1।।
181.e: Rama with his brother Lakshmana having consoled Bharata who is ever devoted to elders began to question:

181.sa: किमेतदिच्छेयमहं श्रोतुं प्रव्याहृतं त्वया। यस्मात्त्वमागतो देशमिमं चीरजटाजिनः।।2.104.2।।
181.e: I want to hear what brought you to this region with your barkrobes, matted locks and antelope skin.

181.sa: यन्निमित्तमिमं देशं कृष्णाजिनजटाधरः। हित्वा राज्यं प्रविष्टस्त्वं तत्सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि।।2.104.3।।
181.e: What made you come to this region, leaving the kingdom and wearing deer skin and matted hair? You should tell me everything.

181.sa: इत्युक्तः कैकयीपुत्रः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना। प्रगृह्य बलवद्भूयः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.104.4।।
181.e: Thus enquired by the magnanimous Rama, Bharata, joining his palms tightly, replied:

181.sa: आर्यं तातः परित्यज्य कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। गत: स्वर्ग महाबाहुः पुत्रशोकाभिपीडितः।।2.104.5।।
181.e: O my revered sire our mighty father, having performed an impossible task of banishing you to the forest, and tortured by grief due to separation from his son, went to heaven.

181.sa: स्त्रिया नियुक्तः कैकेय्या मम मात्रा परन्तप। चकार सा महत्पापमिदमात्मयशोहरम्।।2.104.6।।
181.e: O Rama, tormentor of enemies having been instigated by a woman, my mother Kaikeyi, committed this great sin of destroying his (Dasaratha's) reputation.

181.sa: सा राज्यफलमप्राप्य विधवा शोककर्शिता। पतिष्यति महाघोरे निरये जननी मम।।2.104.7।।
181.e: My mother, formented with grief and with the fruit of the kingdom forfeited, and cursed with widowhood, will fall into the dreadful hell.

181.sa: तस्य मे दासभूतस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि। अभिषिञ्चस्व चाद्येव राज्येन मघवानिव।।2.104.8।।
181.e: It behoves you to grant  me a favour. I am like your servant. Now get yourself coronated in the kingdom like Indra.

181.sa: इमाः प्रकृतय स्सर्वा विधवा मातरश्च याः। त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्ता प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि।।2.104.9।।
181.e: All these subjects and your widowed mothers have come to you. It behoves you to grant them this favour.

181.sa: तदानुपूर्व्या युक्तं च युक्तं चात्मनि मानद। राज्यं प्राप्नुहि धर्मेण सकामान्सुहृदः कुरु।।2.104.10।।
181.e: O bestower of honour by the law of primogeniture and as a worthy successor it is appropriate that you should accept the kingdom righteously and fulfil the desire of your friends.

181.sa: भवत्वविधवा भूमि स्समग्रा पतिना त्वया। शशिना विमलेनेव शारदी रजनी यथा।।2.104.11।।
181.e: Like an autumnal night with the immaculate Moon, let this entire earth cease to be a widow by securing you as her lord.

181.sa: एभिश्च सचिवैस्सार्धं शिरसा याचितो मया। भ्रातु  शिष्यस्य दासस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि।।2.104.12।।
181.e: With my head bowed down, I beseech you along with all these ministers to show favour to me who is your brother, disciple and slave.

181.sa: तदिदं शाश्वतं पित्र्यं सर्वं प्रकृतिमण्डलम्। पूजितं पुरुषव्याघ्र नातिक्रमितुमर्हसि।।2.104.13।।
181.e: O best among men, it does not behove you to transgress the prayers of the whole order of subjects and ministers to assume this hereditary and perpetual order.

181.sa: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहु स्सबाष्पः कैकयीसुतः। रामस्य शिरसा पादौ जग्राह भरत: पुन:।।2.104.14।।
181.e: Having said thus, the mightyarmed Bharata, in accordance with tradition, grasped with tearful eyes the feet of Rama again with his head.

181.sa: तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं निःश्वसन्तं पुन पुनः। भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्।।2.104.15।।
181.e: Rama embraced his brother Bharata who repeatedly heaved sighs and resembled an elephant in rut, and said:

181.sa: कुलीन:सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः। राज्यहेतोः कथं पापमाचरेत्त्वद्विधो जनः।।2.104.16।।
181.e: How can a man like you, born of a noble race, endowed with energy, powerful and adherent to vows, commit a sin for the sake of a kingdom?

181.sa: न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन। न चापि जननीं बाल्यात्त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि।।2.104.17।।
181.e: O destroyer of enemies, I do not find even slightest fault with you. Like a child, it does not behove you to reproach your mother.

181.sa: कामकारो महाप्राज्ञ गुरूणां सर्वदाऽनघ। उपपन्नेषु दारेषु पुत्रेषु च विधीयते।।2.104.18।।
181.e: O sagacious and sinless one, it is laid down (in sastras) that elders when married can always act at their free will towards their wives and sons.

181.sa: वयमस्य यथा लोके सङ्ख्याता: सौम्य साधुभिः। भार्याः पुत्राश्च शिष्याश्च त्वमनुज्ञातुमर्हसि।।2.104.19।।
181.e: O handsome one, you should treat us the way the virtuous treat their wives, sons and disciples in this world.

181.sa: वने वा चीरवसनं सौम्य कृष्णाजिनाम्बरम्। राज्ये वाऽपि महाराजो मां वासयितुमीश्वरः।।2.104.20।।
181.e: O handsome one, king Dasaratha is alone competent to accommodate me in the forest wearing bark robes and antelope skin as garment or install me in the kingdom.

181.sa: यावत पितरि धर्मज्ञे गौरवं लोकसत्कृतम्। तावद्धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ जनन्यामपि गौरवम्।।2.104.21।।
181.e: O best among the protectors of righteousness the honour shown to our father who is conversant with the ways of righteousness and much revered by the world ought to be shown towards our mother also.

181.sa: एताभ्यां धर्मशीलाभ्यां वनं गच्छेति राघव। मातापितृभ्यामुक्तोऽहं कथमन्यत्समाचरे।।2.104.22।।
181.e: O Bharata, I have been commanded by our righteous father and mother to go to the forest. How can any one act otherwise?

181.sa: त्वया राज्यमयोध्यायां प्राप्तव्यं लोकसत्कृतम्। वस्तव्यं दण्डकारण्ये मया वल्कलवाससा।।2.104.23।।
181.e: You shall rule the kingdom wellhonoured by the people in Ayodhya and I shall live in Dandaka forest wearing bark as garments.

181.sa: एवं कृत्वा महाराजो विभागं लोकसन्निधौ। व्यादिश्य च महातेजा दिवं दशरथो गतः।।2.104.24।।
181.e: The maharja of great radiance made this division in the presence of people and after commanding thus, ascended heaven.

181.sa: स च प्रमाणं धर्मात्मा राजा लोकगुरुस्तव। पित्रा दत्तं यथाभागमुपभोक्तुं त्वमर्हसि।।2.104.25।।
181.e: The proclamation of that righteous king revered by the world shall be your guide. You should enjoy that portion bestowed by father.

181.sa: चतुर्दश समास्सौम्य दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः। उपभोक्ष्ये त्वहं दत्तं भागं पित्रा महात्मना।।2.104.26।।
181.e: O handsome one, as for myself, I shall enjoy the portion bestowed on me by my magnanimous father and shall take refuge in the Dandaka forest for fourteen years.

181.sa: यदब्रवीन्मां नरलोकसत्कृतः पिता महात्मा विबुधाधिपोपमः। तदेव मन्ये परमात्मनो हितं न सर्वलोकेश्वर भावमप्ययम्।।2.104.27।।
181.e: I think what my great father, who is honoured by all men, and an equal to Indra, ordered is for my highest welfare. The will of the overlord of the world should not be done away with. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुरुत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

182.sa: ततः पुरुषसिंहानां वृतानां तै स्सुहृद्गणैः। शोचतामेव रजनी दुःखेन व्यत्यवर्तत।।2.105.1।।
182.e: That night passed off painfully for the four lion like brothers as they lamented, surrounded by their hosts of friends.

182.sa: रजन्यां सुप्रभातायां भ्रातरस्ते सुहृद्वृताः। मन्दाकिन्यां हुतं जप्यं कृत्वा राममुपागमन्।।2.105.2।।
182.e: When the night dawned, those brothers surrounded by their friends made (morning) ablutions and, after the prayers, returned to Rama.

182.sa: तूष्णीं ते समुपासीना न कश्चित्किञ्चिदब्रवीत्। भरतस्तु सुहृन्मध्ये रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.105.3।।
182.e: All of them sat together silently and no one uttered a word. Bharata alone from among  them addressed Rama saying:

182.sa: सान्त्विता मामिका माता दत्तं राज्यमिदं मम। तद्ददामि तवैवाहं भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्।।2.105.4।।
182.e: This kingdom was given to me for the satisfaction of my mother. I am bestowing it back on you. Enjoy it without any obstacles.

182.sa: महतेवाम्बुवेगेन भिन्नस्सेतुर्जलागमे। दुरावारं त्वदन्येन राज्यखण्डमिदं महत्।।2.105.5।।
182.e: Like a dyke bursts under pressure by the great surge of waters during the rainy season, this vast kingdom cannot be sustained by any one except yourself.

182.sa: गतिं खर इवाश्वस्य तार्क्ष्यस्येव पतत्रिणः। अनुगन्तुं न शक्तिर्मे गतिं तव महीपते।।2.105.6।।
182.e: O lord of the earth as an ass cannot follow the pace of a horse or a bird, the pace of Tarkshya (Garuda), I do not have the capability to follow you.

182.sa: सुजीवं नित्यशस्तस्य यः परैरुपजीव्यते। राम तेन तु दुर्जीवं यः परानुपजीवति।।2.105.7।।
182.e: O Rama, the life of a man on whom others depend for their sustenance is a happy life and the life of one who depends on others for his own mintenance is miserable.

182.sa: यथा तु रोपितो वृक्षः पुरुषेण विवर्धितः। ह्रस्वकेण दुरारोहो रूढस्कन्धो महाद्रुमः।।2.105.8।। स यदा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्। स तां नानुभवेत्प्रीतिं यस्य हेतोः प्ररोपितः।।2.105.9।। एषोपमा महाबाहो तमर्थं वेत्तु मर्हसि। यदि त्वमस्मान्वृषभो भर्ता भृत्यान्न शाधि हि।।2.105.10।।
182.e: O mightyarmed Rama, a man plants a tree, rears it till it grows into such a large tree with a big trunk that it becomes difficult for a dwarf to climb. When the tree flowers but does not bear fruit, the man who planted it gets no pleasure out of the purpose for which the tree was planted. Being a mighty protector, do not chastise us who are your servants. This is a simile. You may better comprehend its implications. (The meaning of the simile is that if you do not assume the throne, the desire of our father, who nurtured you right from your childhood and hoped that one day you will become king and rule the people, will be in vain.)

182.sa: यथा तु रोपितो वृक्षः पुरुषेण विवर्धितः। ह्रस्वकेण दुरारोहो रूढस्कन्धो महाद्रुमः।।2.105.8।। स यदा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्। स तां नानुभवेत्प्रीतिं यस्य हेतोः प्ररोपितः।।2.105.9।। एषोपमा महाबाहो तमर्थं वेत्तु मर्हसि। यदि त्वमस्मान्वृषभो भर्ता भृत्यान्न शाधि हि।।2.105.10।।
182.e: O mightyarmed Rama, a man plants a tree, rears it till it grows into such a large tree with a big trunk that it becomes difficult for a dwarf to climb. When the tree flowers but does not bear fruit, the man who planted it gets no pleasure out of the purpose for which the tree was planted. Being a mighty protector, do not chastise us who are your servants. This is a simile. You may better comprehend its implications. (The meaning of the simile is that if you do not assume the throne, the desire of our father, who nurtured you right from your childhood and hoped that one day you will become king and rule the people, will be in vain.)

182.sa: यथा तु रोपितो वृक्षः पुरुषेण विवर्धितः। ह्रस्वकेण दुरारोहो रूढस्कन्धो महाद्रुमः।।2.105.8।। स यदा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्। स तां नानुभवेत्प्रीतिं यस्य हेतोः प्ररोपितः।।2.105.9।। एषोपमा महाबाहो तमर्थं वेत्तु मर्हसि। यदि त्वमस्मान्वृषभो भर्ता भृत्यान्न शाधि हि।।2.105.10।।
182.e: O mightyarmed Rama, a man plants a tree, rears it till it grows into such a large tree with a big trunk that it becomes difficult for a dwarf to climb. When the tree flowers but does not bear fruit, the man who planted it gets no pleasure out of the purpose for which the tree was planted. Being a mighty protector, do not chastise us who are your servants. This is a simile. You may better comprehend its implications. (The meaning of the simile is that if you do not assume the throne, the desire of our father, who nurtured you right from your childhood and hoped that one day you will become king and rule the people, will be in vain.)

182.sa: श्रेणयस्त्वां महाराज पश्यन्त्वग्य्राश्च सर्वशः। प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं राज्ये स्थित मरिन्दमम्।।2.105.11।।
182.e: O great king and subduer of enemies, may all the leading guilds of traders and other subjects behold you all over installed in the kingdom like the resplendent Sun.

182.sa: तवानुयाने काकुत्स्थ मत्ता नर्दन्तु कुञ्जराः। अन्तःपुरगता नार्यो नन्दन्तु सुसमाहिताः।।2.105.12।।
182.e: O Rama, let the elephants following you, intoxicated with ichor, be heard trumpeting. Let the women of the inner apartment rejoice with composed minds (when they hear of your return).

182.sa: तस्य साध्वित्यमन्यन्त नागरा विविधा जनाः। भरतस्य वच श्श्रुत्वा रामं प्रत्यनुयाचतः।।2.105.13।।
182.e: Hearing the words of Bharata beseeching Rama to return, various classes of people of the city of Ayodhya, in approbation exclaimed well said.

182.sa: तमेवं दुःखितं प्रेक्ष्य विलपन्तं यशस्विनम्। रामः कृतात्मा भरतं समाश्वासयदात्मवान्।।2.105.14।।
182.e: Having seen the illustrious Bharata lamenting that way, Rama, a man of firm determination and selfpossession, consoled him thus:

182.sa: नाऽत्मनः कामकारोऽस्ति पुरुषोऽयमनीश्वरः। इतश्चेतरतश्चैनं कृतान्तः परिकर्षति।।2.105.15।।
182.e: A man is neither independent nor competent to do any act on his free will. Fate pulls him this way or the other.

182.sa: सर्वे क्षयान्ताः निचयाः पतनान्ता समुच्छ्रयाः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्।।2.105.16।।
182.e: All accumulations of wealth deplete at the end. Every man who attains elevated positions falls at the end. Every union culminates in separation. Every life ends in death.

182.sa: यथा फलानां पक्वानां नान्यत्र पतनाद्भयम्। एवं नरस्य जातस्य नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्।।2.105.17।।
182.e: The only fear of a ripened fruit is the fear of falling down (from the tree). In the same way every man who is born has no other fear except the fear of death.

182.sa: यथाऽगारं दृढस्थूणं जीर्णं भूत्वाऽवसीदति। तथैव सीदन्ति नरा जरामृत्युवशं गताः।।2.105.18।।
182.e: Even a house constructed with sturdy pillars gets dilapidated and ultimately decays. In the same way people under the sway of old age and death are destroyed (at last).

182.sa: अत्येति रजनी या तु सा न प्रतिनिवर्तते। यात्येव यमुना पूर्णा समुद्रमुदकाकुलम्।।2.105.19।।
182.e: A night that once passe off does not return like the waters of river Yamuna that flow into the ocean filled with water (the water do not flow back into Yamuna).

182.sa: अहोरात्राणि गच्छन्ति सर्वेषां प्राणिनामिह। अायूंषि क्षपयन्त्याशु ग्रीष्मे जलमिवांशवः।।2.105.20।।
182.e: The passing days and nights quickly decrease the life span of all living beings in this world, like sunrays drying up the water in summer.

182.sa: आत्मानमनुशोच त्वं किमन्यमनुशोचसि। आयुस्ते हीयते यस्य स्थितस्य च गतस्य च।।2.105.21।।
182.e: Whether you are static or moving, your lifespan decreases. Therefore, you should only grieve about yourself and not for any one else.

182.sa: सहैव मृत्युर्व्रजति सह मृत्युर्निषीदति। गत्वासुदीर्घमध्वानं सहमृत्युर्निवर्तते।।2.105.22।।
182.e: Death follows a man wherever he goes. When he sits, death sits with him. Even after travelling a very long distance, the man returns along with death.

182.sa: गात्रेषु वलयः प्राप्ता श्श्वेताश्चैव शिरोरुहाः। जरया पुरुषो जीर्णः किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्।।2.105.23।।
182.e: Wrinkels form on the body and hair turns grey in old age. In this way, decayed with age, what can a man do to have control over death.

182.sa: नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमितेऽहनि। आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्।।2.105.24।।
182.e: People rejoice when the Sun rises and rejoice when the Sun sets. But they are unaware of the decline of the life span of their own.

182.sa: हृष्यन्त्यृतुमुखं दृष्ट्वा नवं नवमिहागतम्। ऋतूनां परिवर्तेन प्राणिनां प्राणसङ्क्षयः।।2.105.25।।
182.e: At the advent of each new season men feel delighted to see the newly blossomed flowers and fruits. But with the change of the scasons the life span also diminishes.

182.sa: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन।।2.105.26।। एवं भार्याश्चपुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च धनानि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः।।2.105.27।।
182.e: In a mighty ocean, two pieces of logs meet one another, float together and in due course get separated. In the same way wives, sons, relatives and riches remain together for some time and thereafter get separated. Their separation is certain.

182.sa: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन।।2.105.26।। एवं भार्याश्चपुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च धनानि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः।।2.105.27।।
182.e: In a mighty ocean, two pieces of logs meet one another, float together and in due course get separated. In the same way wives, sons, relatives and riches remain together for some time and thereafter get separated. Their separation is certain.

182.sa: नात्र कश्चिद्यथाभावं प्राणी समभिवर्तते। तेन तस्मिन्न सामर्थ्यं प्रेतस्या स्त्यनुशोचतः।।2.105.28।।
182.e: No living being in this world can act as he likes. Therefore, no one should grieve for the dead.

182.sa: यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः। अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवता मिति।।2.105.29।। एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहो ध्रुवः। तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद्यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः।।2.105.30।।
182.e: Like a man standing on the wayside says to a passing caravan, 'I am following you', and follows them, the road taken by our fathers and forefathers is certain for every one and cannot be violated by a person treading that path. (So) why should a man grieve?

182.sa: यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात्कश्चित्पथि स्थितः। अहमप्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतो भवता मिति।।2.105.29।। एवं पूर्वैर्गतो मार्गः पितृपैतामहो ध्रुवः। तमापन्नः कथं शोचेद्यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः।।2.105.30।।
182.e: Like a man standing on the wayside says to a passing caravan, 'I am following you', and follows them, the road taken by our fathers and forefathers is certain for every one and cannot be violated by a person treading that path. (So) why should a man grieve?

182.sa: वयसः पतमानस्य स्रोतसो वाऽनिवर्तिनः। आत्मा सुखे नियोक्तव्यस्सुखभाजः प्रजाः स्मृताः।।2.105.31।।
182.e: Like the flow of water which never reverts to its source, age passes. Therefore, a man must employ his self in righteous acts that bring him happiness. By doing so, it is said, people will always be happy.

182.sa: धर्मात्मा स शुभैः कृत्स्नैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.32।।
182.e: Our righteous father and lord of the earth, Dasaratha, attained heaven by giving abundant charities and performing several sacrifices in accordance with tradition.

182.sa: भृत्यानां भरणात्सम्यक्प्रजानां परिपालनात्। अर्थादानाच्च धर्मेण पिता न स्त्रिदिवंगतः।।2.105.33।।
182.e: Our father nourished his dependents, splendidly governed his subjects and accepted  wealth through righteous ways. Because of these pious acts, he could go to heaven.

182.sa: कर्मभि स्तु शुभैरिष्टैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। स्वर्गं दशरथः प्राप्तः पिता नः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.34।।
182.e: Dasaratha, our father and lord of the earth, reached heaven by performing auspicious acts and offering abundant charities in sacrifices.

182.sa: इष्ट्वा बहुविधैर्यज्ञैर्भोगां श्चावाप्य पुष्कलान्। उत्तमं चायुरासाद्य स्वर्गतः पृथिवीपतिः।।2.105.35।।
182.e: King Dasaratha, lord of the earth, having performed various kinds of sacrifices and securing a long life, enjoyed abundance of pleasures and attained heaven.

182.sa: आयुरुत्तममासाद्य भोगानपि च राघवः। स न शोच्यः पिता तात स्वर्गत स्सत्कृत स्सताम्।।2.105.36।।
182.e: O dear our father, king Dasaratha, who was honoured by the virtuous and enjoyed the best of pleasures attained heaven after a long life. Therefore, he is not to be grieved over.

182.sa: स जीर्णं मानुषं देहं परित्यज्य पिता हि नः। दैवीमृद्धिमनुप्राप्तो ब्रह्मलोकविहारिणीम्।।2.105.37।।
182.e: Our father, king Dasaratha, abandoned the wornout mortal body, and obtained divine prosperity of wandering in the world of Brahma.

182.sa: तं तु नैवंविधः कश्चित्प्राज्ञ श्शोचितुमर्हति। तत्विधो मद्विधश्चापि श्रुतवान्बुद्धिमत्तरः।।2.105.38।।
182.e: No one like you or me should ever mourn about this highly sagacious and learned king who was proficient in scriptural knowledge.

182.sa: एते बहुविधा शोका विलापरुदिते तथा। वर्जनीया हि धीरेण सर्वावस्थासु धीमता।।2.105.39।।
182.e: A wise man, holding on to his fortitude in all circumstances, should avoid such occasions of grief, these words of lamentation and this crying.

182.sa: स स्वस्थो भव मा शोचेर्यात्वा चावसतां पुरीम्। तथा पित्रा नियुक्तोऽसि वशिना वदतां वर।।2.105.40।।
182.e: O foremost of the eloquent, compose yourself. Do not grieve. Return to the city (Ayodhya) and reside there. You have been commanded so by our father who was a man of selfcontrol.

182.sa: यत्राहमपि तेनैव नियुक्तः पुण्यकर्मणा। तत्रैवाहं करिष्यामि पितुरार्यस्य शासनम्।।2.105.41।।
182.e: I shall also stick to the command of our noble father who was a man of sacred deeds.

182.sa: न मया शासनं तस्य त्यक्तुं न्याय्य मरिन्दम। स त्वयापि सदा मान्यं स वै बन्धु स नः पिता।।2.105.42।।
182.e: O subduer of enemies, I cannot violate the order of the king. You also must respect it for he is our father and friend indeed.

182.sa: तद्वचः पितुरेवाहं सम्मतं धर्मचारिणः। कर्मणा पालयिष्यामि वनवासेन राघव।।2.105.43।।
182.e: O Bharata, I will, therefore, obey the command of our venerable father, the champion of righteousness, by living in the forest.

182.sa: धार्मिकेणानृशंसेन नरेण गुरुवर्तिना। भवितव्यं नरव्याघ्र परलोकं जिगीषता।।2.105.44।।
182.e: O best of men, if a man aspires to conquer the higher world, he should remain  virtuous, compassionate and obedient to his preceptors.

182.sa: आत्मानमनुतिष्ठत्वं स्वभावेन नरर्षभ। निशाम्यतु शुभं वृत्तं पितुर्दशरथस्य नः।।2.105.45।।
182.e: O best of men, having seen the auspicious life of our father Dasaratha and his conduct, you also stick to your own duty.

182.sa: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा पितुर्निदेश प्रतिपालनार्थम्। यवीयसं भ्रातरमर्थवच्च प्रभुर्मुहूर्ताद्विरराम रामः।।2.105.46।।
182.e: Rama, the magnanimous lord, addressed his younger brother Bharata with words full of significance, saying, Obey father's command and remained silent in a moment. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

183.sa: एवमुक्त्वा तु विरते रामे वचनमर्थवत्। ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरे रामं प्रकृतिवत्सलम्।।2.106.1।। उवाच भरत श्चित्रं धार्मिको धार्मिकं वचः।
183.e: Rama remained silent after saying these meaningful words on the bank of river Mandakini. Then the Bharata, conforming to righteousness, replied in clear words to the virtuous Rama who was affectionate by nature.

183.sa: को हि स्यादीदृशो लोके यादृश स्त्वमरिन्दमः।।2.106.2।। न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद्दुःखं प्रीतिर्वा नप्रहर्षयेत्। सम्मतश्चासि वृद्धानां तांश्च पृच्छसि संशयान्।।2.106.3।।
183.e: O subduer of enemies, you are of such nature that neither sorrow pains you nor pleasure delights you. There are none in this world like you. You are loved by the elders, for you seek their counsel whenever you have doubts.

183.sa: को हि स्यादीदृशो लोके यादृश स्त्वमरिन्दम।।2.106.2।। न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद्दुःखं प्रीतिर्वा नप्रहर्षयेत्। सम्मतश्चासि वृद्धानां तांश्च पृच्छसि संशयान्।।2.106.3।।
183.e: O subduer of enemies, you are of such nature that neither sorrow pains you nor pleasure delights you. There are none in this world like you. You are loved by the elders, for you seek their counsel whenever you have doubts.

183.sa: यथा मृत स्तथा जीवन्यथाऽसति तथा सति। यस्यैष बुद्धिलाभ स्स्यात्परितप्येत केन सः।।2.106.4।।
183.e: One should accept life and death, vice and virtue equally. How can one be afflicted when he has gained such an intellect?

183.sa: परावरज्ञो यश्च स्याद् यथा त्वं मनुजाधिप। स एव व्यसनं प्राप्य न विषीदितुमर्हति।।2.106.5।।
183.e: O lord of men, it is not proper for a person like you who knows the past and the future of human beings to feel distressed and lament over it.

183.sa: अमरोपमसत्त्व स्त्वं महात्मा सत्यसङ्गरः। सर्वज्ञ स्सर्वदर्शी च बुद्धिमांश्चासि राघव।।2.106.6।।
183.e: O magnanimous Rama, your nature is divine and you are true to your promises. You are omniscient, allseeing and wise.

183.sa: न त्वामेवं गुणैर्युक्तं प्रभवाभवकोविदम्। अविषह्यतमं दुःखमासादयितुमर्हति।।2.106.7।।
183.e: It is not proper for a virtuous man like you, who is cognizant in matters of life and death, to be overwhelmed by such insufferable grief.

183.sa: प्रोषिते मयि यत्पापं मात्रा मत्कारणात्कृतम्। क्षुद्रया तदनिष्टं मे प्रसीदतु भवान्मम।।2.106.8।।
183.e: When I was away from home, my meanminded mother committed a sin for my sake which I never wished. You may pardon me graciously.

183.sa: धर्मबन्धेन बद्धोऽस्मि तेनेमां नेह मातरम्। हन्मितीव्रेण दण्डेन दण्डार्हां पापकारिणीम्।।2.106.9।।
183.e: I am bound by a bond of righteousness for which I am unble to slay my mother who deserves severe punishment for her sinful acts.

183.sa: कथं दशरथा ज्जात श्शुद्धाभिजनकर्मणः। जानन् धर्ममधर्मिष्ठं कुर्यां कर्म जुगुप्सितम्।।2.106.10।।
183.e: How shall I, born to Dasaratha of noble race and righteous deeds, with the knowledge of dharma, do such a reprehensible and unrighteous deed?

183.sa: गुरुः क्रियावान्वृद्धश्च राजा प्रेतः पितेतिच। तातं न परिगर्हेयं दैवतं चेति संसदि।।2.106.11।।
183.e: King Dasaratha, my father and preceptor, is godlike to me. Devoted to meritorious acts, he departed from this world in his old age. For this reason, I cannot reproach him (publicly) in this assembly (of men).

183.sa: को हि धर्मार्थयोर्हीनमीदृशं कर्म किल्बिषम्। स्त्रियाः प्रियं चिकीर्षु स्सन्कुर्याद्धर्मज्ञ धर्मवित्।।2.106.12।।
183.e: O Rama, conversant with righteousness, will any one who knows the meaning of righteousness, do such a sinful act contrary to dharma and artha to please a woman?

183.sa: अन्तकाले हि भूतानि मुह्यन्तीति पुरा श्रुतिः। राज्ञैवं कुर्वता लोके प्रत्यक्षं सा श्रुतिः कृता।।2.106.13।।
183.e: There is an ancient saying that at the time of death, the intellect of people is deluded. By conducting himself in this way, king Dasaratha has proved it.

183.sa: साध्वर्थमभिसन्धाय क्रोधान्मोहाच्च साहसात्। तातस्य यदतिक्रान्तं प्रत्याहरतु तद्भवान्।।2.106.14।।
183.e: Our father has trangressed righteousness due to anger or delusion or recklessness. Therefore, you may think over the matter prudently and set it right.

183.sa: पितुर्हि समतिक्रान्तं पुत्रो यस्साधु मन्यते। तदपत्यं मतं लोके विपरीतमतोऽन्यथा।।2.106.15।।
183.e: One who sets right the wrongs done by his father is a true son. Otherwise the son becomes just the opposite. (He is not  a son to the father).

183.sa: तदपत्यं भवानस्तु मा भवान् दुष्कृतं पितुः। अभिपत्ता कृतं कर्म लोके धीरविगर्हितम्।।2.106.16।।
183.e: So be a worthy son and let not the sinful act committed by our father and condemned by men of wisdom be approved by you.

183.sa: कैकेयीं मां च तातं च सुहृदो बान्धवांश्च नः। पौरजानपदान्सर्वांस्त्रातु सर्वमिदं भवान्।।2.106.17।।
183.e: Protect this entire kingdom, Kaikeyi, me and father, our friends and relations, citizens of the city and inhabitants of the countryside.

183.sa: क्व चारण्यं क्वच क्षात्रं क्व जटाः क्व च पालनम्। ईदृशं व्याहतं कर्म न भवान्कर्तुमर्हति।।2.106.18।।
183.e: Where is the forest and where is kshatriya's duty? Where are matted locks and where is governance of the kingdom? It does not behave you to do such acts antithetical to each other.

183.sa: एष हि प्रथमो धर्मः क्षत्रियस्याभिषेचनम्। येन शक्यं महाप्राज्ञ प्रजानां परिपालनम्।।2.106.19।।
183.e: O sagacious one, the primary duty of a kshatriya is to be crowned. This enables him to rule his subjects.

183.sa: कश्च प्रत्यक्षमुत्सृज्य संशयस्थ मलक्षणम्। आयतिस्थं चरे द्धर्मं क्षत्रबन्दुरनिश्चितम्।।2.106.20।।
183.e: Will any kshatriya, setting aside his first duty, follow an uncertain course of piety which is contrary to his dharma and whose impact may be felt in a remote future.

183.sa: अथ क्लेशज मेव त्वं धर्मं चरितु मिच्छसि। धर्मेण चतुरो वर्णान्पालयन् क्लेश माप्नुहि।।2.106.21।।
183.e: If you so desire to follow the path of dharma acquired out of physical exertion, then bear the trouble of governing the four castes of the social order righteously.

183.sa: चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां हि गार्हस्थ्यं श्रेष्ठमुत्तमम्। आहुर्धर्मज्ञ धर्मज्ञास्तं कथं त्यक्तु मर्हसि।।2.106.22।।
183.e: O Rama, you are the one who knows his duty. The knowers of dharma maintain that the life of a householder is the foremost among the four modes of life. How can you renounce it?

183.sa: श्रुतेन बालः स्थानेन जन्मना भवतो ह्यहम्। स कथं पालयिष्यामि भूमिं भवति तिष्ठति।।2.106.23।।
183.e: Being younger to you in knowledge, position and birth, how can I rule the earth when you are present?

183.sa: हीनबुद्धिगुणो बालो हीनः स्थानेन चाप्यहम्। भवता च विनाभूतो न वर्तयितुमुत्सुहे।।2.106.24।।
183.e: I am a child, deficient in intelligence and virtue and even inferior in position. Deserted by  you, I do not wish to live.

183.sa: इदं निखिल मव्यग्रं राज्यं पित्र्यमकण्टकम्। अनुशाधि स्वधर्मेण धर्मज्ञ सहबान्धवैः।।2.106.25।।
183.e: O one, conversant with righteousness rule unhindered this entire kingdom along with our relations inherited from our father.

183.sa: इहैव त्वाऽभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वाः प्रकृतय स्सह। ऋत्विज स्सवसिष्ठाश्च मन्त्रविन्मन्त्रकोविदाः।।2.106.26।।
183.e: Let all ministers, subjects, and priests including Vasistha who are wellversed in Vedic hymns consecrate you here itself.

183.sa: अभिषिक्तस्त्वमस्माभिरयोध्यां पालने व्रज। विजित्य तरसा लोकान्मरुद्भिरिव वासवः।।2.106.27।।
183.e: After consecration, you too return to rule Ayodhya along with all of us like Indra who went back (to heaven), accompanied by Maruts after conquering all the worlds with his prowess.

183.sa: ऋणानि त्रीण्यपाकुर्वन्दुर्हृदस्साधु निर्दहन्। सुहृदस्तर्पयन्कामैस्त्वमेवात्रानुशाधि माम्।।2.106.28।।
183.e: Discharging completely the three debts, to gods, to ancestors and to sages, subduing your enemies and gratifying your friends, you alone (have the right) to dictate me.

183.sa: अद्याऽर्य मुदिता स्सन्तु सुहृदस्तेऽभिषेचने। अद्य भीताः पलायन्तां दुर्हृदस्ते दिशो दश।।2.106.29।।
183.e: O my esteemed brother let all your friends be delighted today at your enthronement and your enemies flee in terror in ten different directions.

183.sa: आक्रोशं मम मातुश्च प्रमृज्य पुरुषर्षभ। अद्य तत्र भवन्तं च पितरं रक्ष किल्बिषात्।।2.106.30।।
183.e: O best of men, wiping out all the censure on my mother, redeem our revered father from sin.

183.sa: शिरसा त्वाऽभियाचेऽहं कुरुष्व करुणां मयि। बान्धवेषु च सर्वेषु भूतेष्विव महेश्वरः।।2.106.31।।
183.e: I beseech you with my head bowed low, show mercy on me and every one of our relations, like Maheswara showing compassion on all living beings.

183.sa: अथैतत्पृष्ठतः कृत्वा वनमेव भवानितः। गमिष्यति गमिष्यामि भवता सार्धमप्यहम्।।2.106.32।।
183.e: If you turn your back on my solicitations and set out for the forest I shall also go along with you from here itself.

183.sa: तथाहि रामो भरतेन ताम्यता प्रसाद्यमानश्शिरसा महीपतिः। नचैव चक्रे गमनाय सत्त्ववान्मतिं पितुस्तद्वचने प्रतिष्ठितः।।2.106.33।।
183.e: Thus besought and propitiated by Bharata with his head bowed low and distressed, the virtuous lord of the world, Rama, firmly established in the words of his father, resolved not to go back to Ayodhya.

183.sa: तदद्भुतं स्थैर्यमवेक्ष्य राघवे समं जनो हर्षमवाप दुःखितः। न यात्ययोध्यामिति दुःखितोऽभवत् स्थिरप्रतिज्ञत्वमवेक्ष्य हर्षितः।।2.106.34।।
183.e: Having seen the wonderful deternmination of Rama, people were, at once, anguished and delighted, anguished because he would not return to Ayodhya, and delighted because he was firm in his resolve.

183.sa: तमृत्विजो नैगमयूथवल्लभास्तदा विसंज्ञाश्रुकलाश्च मातरः। तथा ब्रुवाणं भरतं प्रतुष्टुवुः प्रणम्य रामं च ययाचिरे सह।।2.106.35।।
183.e: All the priests, the chiefs of merchant organizations and mothers who had their senses switched off and theif tears drained dry extolled Bharata for his words. All of them, reverentially saluting Rama, implored him. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षडुत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredsixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

184.sa: पुनरेवं ब्रुवाणं तं भरतं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। प्रत्युवाच तत श्श्रीमान् ज्ञातिमध्येऽभिसत्कृतः।।2.107.1।।
184.e: Wellhonoured in the midst of relatives, the celebrated Rama, elder brother of Lakshmana, then said to Bharata who was going to speak again.

184.sa: उपपन्नमिदं वाक्यं यत्त्वमेवमभाषथाः। जातः पुत्रो दशरथात्कैकेय्यां राजसत्तमात्।।2.107.2।।
184.e: Appropriate are the words spoken by you born to the celebrated king Dasaratha through Kaikeyi.

184.sa: पुरा भ्रातः पिता न स्स मातरं ते समुद्वहन्। मातामहे समाश्रौषीद्राज्यशुल्कमनुत्तमम्।।2.107.3।।
184.e: Earlier when our father was to wed your mother, O dear brother, he had promised to your maternal grandfather that he would confer (on her) a kingdom with good revenue.

184.sa: दैवासुरे च सङ्ग्रामे जनन्यै तव पार्थिवः। सम्प्रहृष्टो ददौ राजा वरमाराधितः प्रभुः।।2.107.4।।
184.e: Thereafter in the battle between gods and demons, the able king (Dasaratha) pleased  (with your mother) granted her a boon (as a token of gratitude).

184.sa: ततस्सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी। अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी।।2.107.5।। तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा। तौ च राजा तदा तस्यै नियुक्तः प्रददौ वरौ।।2.107.6।।
184.e: Thereafter, O tiger among men, your illustrious mother of fair complexion, under oath demanded of that best of men, king Dasaratha, the two boons, namely kingdom for you and banishment for me. Bound by such agreement (oath), the king granted her the boons.

184.sa: ततः सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी। अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी।।2.107.5।। तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा। तच्च राजा तदा तस्यै नियुक्तः प्रददौ वरौ।।2.107.6।।
184.e: Thereafter, O tiger among men, your illustrious mother of fair complexion, under oath demanded of that best of men, king Dasaratha, the two boons, namely kingdom for you and banishment for me. Bound by such agreement (oath), the king granted her the boons.

184.sa: तेन पित्राऽहमप्यत्र नियुक्तः पुरुषर्षभ। चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वरदानिकम्।।2.107.7।।
184.e: O best of men, that is why I have been ordered by father to live in the forest for fourteen years as per the (condition of the) boon.

184.sa: सोऽहं वनमिदं प्राप्तो निर्जनं लक्ष्मणान्वितः। सीतया चाप्रतिद्वन्द्व स्सत्यवादे स्थितः पितुः।।2.107.8।।
184.e: I have come to this lonely forest accompanied by Lakshmana and Sita, bent upon upholding the truth of our unrivalled father's words.

184.sa: भवानपि तथेत्येव पितरं सत्यवादिनम्। कर्तुमर्हति राजेन्द्र क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचनात्।।2.107.9।।
184.e: O Indra among kings, let your coronation be performed without delay since you are worthy and at the same time the truthfulness of our father's words be honoured.

184.sa: ऋणान्मोचय राजानं मत्कृते भरत प्रभुम्। पितरं चापि धर्मज्ञं मातरं चाभिनन्दय।।2.107.10।।
184.e: O Bharata, release for my sake the competent king from his debt (of vow) and honour the righteous father and the mother as well.

184.sa: श्रूयते धीमता तात श्रुतिर्गीता यशस्विना। गयेन यजमानेन गयेष्वेव पितॄन् प्रति।।2.107.11।।
184.e: Dear (brother), it is heard that long ago an illustrious king while performing a sacrifice intended for ancestors at a sacred place known as Gaya, the sacrificer Gaya chanted a Vedic hymn as follows:

184.sa: पुन्नाम्नो नरकाद् यस्मात् पितरं त्रायते सुतः। तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः पितॄन् यः पाति सर्वतः।।2.107.12।।
184.e: Putra is so called as he delivers his father from a hell known as Put and protects the ancestors in all possible ways.

184.sa: एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा गुणवन्तो बहुश्रुताः। तेषां वै समवेतानामपि कश्चिद्गयां व्रजेत्।।2.107.13।।
184.e: One should desire many virtuous and learned sons so that at least one of them may go to Gaya (to perform the father's obsequies).

184.sa: एवं राजर्षय स्सर्वे प्रतीता राजनन्दन। तस्मात्राहि नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं नरकात्प्रभो।।2.107.14।।
184.e: O enhancer of the king's delight, O best of men rajarsis have decided this way. You may, therefore, O lord, protect your father against hell.

184.sa: अयोध्यां गच्छ भरत प्रकृतीरनुरञ्जय। शत्रुघ्नसहितो वीर सह सर्वैर्द्विजातिभिः।।2.107.15।।
184.e: O valiant Bharata, go to Ayodhya accompanied by Satrughna and the twiceborn (brahmins) and keep the subjects delighted like pleased (with your rule).

184.sa: प्रवेक्ष्ये दण्डकारण्यमहमप्यविलम्बयन्। आभ्यान्तु सहितो राजन् वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च।।2.107.16।।
184.e: O king (Bharata) I shall also enter the Dandaka forest without delay in the company of only these two -- the princess from Videha (Sita) and Lakshmana.

184.sa: त्वं राजा भरत भव स्वयं नराणां वन्यानामहमपि राजराण्मृगाणाम्। गच्छ त्वं पुरवरमद्य सम्प्रहृष्टस्संहृष्टस्त्वहमपि दण्डकान्प्रवेक्ष्ये।।2.107.17।।
184.e: O Bharata, be the king of men. I shall also become the supreme king of the wild beasts in the forest. Go now happily to Ayodhya, the best of cities, and I shall enter Dandaka forest with delight.

184.sa: छायां ते दिनकरभाः प्रबाधमानां वर्षत्रं भरत करोतु मूर्ध्नि शीताम्। एतेषामहमपि काननद्रुमाणां छायां तामतिशयिनीं सुखी श्रयिष्ये।।2.107.18।।
184.e: Let an umbrella protect you against (scorching) sunshine and provide its cool shade over your head, O Bharata As for me, I shall happily seek the shade of these dense woodland trees.

184.sa: शत्रुघ्नः कुशलमतिस्तु ते सहायस्सौमित्रिर्मम विदितः प्रधानमित्रम्। चत्वारस्तनयवरा वयं नरेन्द्रं सत्यस्थं भरत चराम मा विषीद।।2.107.19।।
