184.e: O Bharata, intelligent Satrughna will be your support and son of Sumitra (Lakshmana) as is wellknown will remain my best friend. All four of us, worthy sons of Dasaratha, shall follow the path of truth of our father. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

185.sa: आश्वासयन्तं भरतं जाबालिर्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः। उवाच रामं धर्मज्ञं धर्मापेतमिदं वचः।।2.108.1।।
185.e: While Rama, conversant with dharma, was consoling Bharata, Jabali an eminent brahmin addressed him in words contrary to righteousness.

185.sa: साधु राघव माऽभूत्ते बुध्दिरेवं निरर्थिका। प्राकृतस्य नरस्येव ह्यार्यबुद्धेर्मनस्विनः।।2.108.2।।
185.e: Very well, O scion of the Raghu race, you are nobleminded and highsouled. You, like a common man, must not entertain such nonsensical thought.

185.sa: कः कस्य पुरुषो बन्धुः किमाप्यं कस्य केनचित्। यदेको जायते जन्तुरेक एव विनश्यति।।2.108.3।।
185.e: Who is whose friend? who is to get what and from whom? Man is born alone and will die alone.

185.sa: तस्मान्माता पिता चेति राम सज्जेत यो नरः। उन्मत्त इव स ज्ञेयो नास्ति कश्चिद्धि कस्यचित्।।2.108.4।।
185.e: O Rama one who establishes relationship by saying, 'She is my mother he is my father' is to be regarded as a lunatic. In fact, no one belongs to any one.

185.sa: यथा ग्रामान्तरं गच्छन्नरः कश्चित्क्वचिद्वसेत्। उत्सृज्य च तमावासं प्रतिष्ठेतापरेऽहनि।।2.108.5।। एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु। अवासमात्रं काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते नात्र सज्जनाः।।2.108.6।।
185.e: A man who goes from one village to another takes rest somewhere on the way and the next day leaves the place and proceeds on his journey. Similarly, father, mother, home and wealth are restingplaces to a man. The wise do not get attached to them, O descendant the Kakutsthas

185.sa: यथा ग्रामान्तरं गच्छन्नरः कश्चित्क्वचिद्वसेत्। उत्सृज्य च तमावासं प्रतिष्ठेतापरेऽहनि।।2.108.5।। एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु। अवासमात्रं काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते नात्र सज्जनाः।।2.108.6।।
185.e: A man who goes from one village to another takes rest somewhere on the way and the next day leaves the place and proceeds on his journey. Similarly, father, mother, home and wealth are restingplaces to a man. The wise do not get attached to them, O descendant the Kakutsthas

185.sa: पित्र्यं राज्यं परित्यज्य स नार्हसि नरोत्तम। आस्थातुं कापथं दुःखं विषमं बहुकण्टकम्।।2.108.7।।
185.e: O most virtuous of men, you ought not to abandon this patrimonial kingdom, adopt a course, which is painful, difficult and full of thorns (dangers). This (course) is unwise and unworthy of you.

185.sa: समृद्धायामयोध्यायामात्मानमभिषेचय। एकवेणीधरा हि त्वां नगरी सम्प्रतीक्षते।।2.108.8।।
185.e: Go back to that prosperous city of Ayodhya and get yourself coronated. That city is a chaste woman wearing a single braid of hair awaiting you, her lord.
O king's son, enjoy inestimable royal pleasures in the city of Ayodhya like Indra in heaven.

185.sa: न ते कश्चिद्धशरथ स्त्वं च तस्य न कश्चन। अन्यो राजा त्वमन्य स्तस्मात्कुरु यदुच्यते।।2.108.10।।
185.e: Dasaratha was nobody to you and you are nobody to him. That king is one person and you are another. Therefore, do what I tell you. (It does not matter what you are to him and what he means to you).

185.sa: बीजमात्रं पिता जन्तो श्शुक्लं रुधिरमेव च। संयुक्तमृतुमन्मात्रा पुरुषस्येह जन्म तत्।।2.108.11।।
185.e: For a living being, the father is only a drop of white blood (semen). During her menstrual period this is blended in the mother's womb due to which a man is born in this world.

185.sa: गत स्स नृपतिस्तत्र गन्तव्यं यत्र तेन वै। प्रवृततिरेषा मर्त्यानां त्वं तु मिथ्या विहन्यसे।।2.108.12।।
185.e: That king (Dasaratha) has gone to the place where he ought to go. Such is the nature of mortals. You are fruitlessly undergoing difficulties.

185.sa: अर्थधर्मपरा ये ये तांस्तांछोचामि नेतरान्। ते हि दुःखमिह प्राप्य विनाशं प्रेत्य भेजिरे।।2.108.13।।
185.e: I prity those who yearn for dharma and artha and not for other things since those who have experienced adversities in this world (disregarding their own interest), will be ultimately destroyed any way by death.

185.sa: अष्टका पितृदैवत्यमित्ययं प्रसृतो जनः। अन्नस्योपद्रवं पश्य मृतो हि किमशिष्यति।।2.108.14।।
185.e: People perform ashtaka ceremony for the spirits of ancestors and offer them food. Look at the amount of food being wasted. Will the dead (ever) eat food?

185.sa: यदि भुक्तमिहान्येन देहमन्यस्य गच्छति। दद्यात्प्रवसत श्श्राद्धं न तत्पथ्यशनं भवेत्।।2.108.15।।
185.e: If something eaten by one in this world can enter the body of another, then a shraddha can be performed for a person who has set out on a distant journey. Will that offering turn into food for him on his way?

185.sa: दानसंवनना ह्येते ग्रन्था मेधाविभिः कृताः। यजस्व देहि दीक्षस्व तपस्तप्यस्व सन्त्यज।।2.108.16।।
185.e: It was to induce people to give charity that treatises are composed by intelligent men exhorting, 'perform sacrifices', 'give charity', 'be initiated', 'practise religious austerities', 'renounce', etc.

185.sa: स नास्ति परमित्येव कुरु बुद्धिं महामते। प्रत्यक्षं यत्तदातिष्ठ परोक्षं पृष्ठतः कुरु।।2.108.17।।
185.e: O highminded one thinking that the next world does not exist, practise whichever is evident and perceivable. And turn your back on what is beyond perception.

185.sa: सतां बुद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वलोकनिदर्शिनीम्। राज्यं त्वं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भरतेन प्रसादितः।।2.108.18।।
185.e: Honour the decision of the wise that serves as an instance to all and accept the kingdom offered by Bharata with pleasure इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

186.sa: जाबालेस्तु वचश्श्रुत्वा राम स्सत्यात्मनां वरः। उवाच परया भक्त्या स्वबुद्ध्या चाविपन्नया।।2.109.1।।
186.e: Hearing Jabali's words, Rama, the foremost among the truthful, gave a rejoinder, exercising his own judgment and firm conviction with due respect (to Jabali).

186.sa: भवान्मे प्रियकामार्थं वचनं यदिहोक्तवान्। अकार्यं कार्यसङ्काशमपथ्यं पथ्यसम्मतम्।।2.109.2।।
186.e: Althoug what you have said appears to be salutary, it is actually unwholesome. It appears to be beneficial but is really detrimental.

186.sa: निर्मर्यादस्तु पुरुषः पापाचारसमन्वितः। मानं न लभते सत्सु भिन्नचारित्रदर्शनः।।2.109.3।।
186.e: A man not bound by morality, engaged in evil deeds and conducts himself contrary to good character is not respected by the virtuous.

186.sa: कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्। चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाऽशुचिम्।।2.109.4।।
186.e: It is only the character that tells whether a man is highborn or not, brave or only proud of his manliness, honest or dishonest.

186.sa: अनार्यस्त्वार्यसङ्काश श्शौचाद्दीनस्ताथाऽशुचिः। लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुश्शीलश्शीलवानिव।।2.109.5।। अधर्मं धर्मवेशेण यदीमं लोकसङ्कुरम्। अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्।।2.109.6।। कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः। बहुमंस्यति मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्।।2.109.7।।
186.e: If like a man who appears noble, though ignoble, clean, though unclean or dishonest, auspicious, though inauspicious, a man of character, though depraved, I forsake auspicious ways for unrighteousness, abandon pious acts and scriptural practices and indulge, under the cloak of dharma, in acts of wickedness by causing harm and confusion to the world, will any sensible man with a sense of discrimination between should and should not hold me in high esteem?

186.sa: अनार्यस्त्वार्यसङ्काश श्शौचाद्दीनस्ताथाऽशुचिः। लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुश्शीलश्शीलवानिव।।2.109.5।। अधर्मं धर्मवेशेण यदीमं लोकसङ्कुरम्। अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्।।2.109.6।। कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः। बहुमंस्यति मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्।।2.109.7।।
186.e: If like a man who appears noble, though ignoble, clean, though unclean or dishonest, auspicious, though inauspicious, a man of character, though depraved, I forsake auspicious ways for unrighteousness, abandon pious acts and scriptural practices and indulge, under the cloak of dharma, in acts of wickedness by causing harm and confusion to the world, will any sensible man with a sense of discrimination between should and should not hold me in high esteem?

186.sa: अनार्यस्त्वार्यसङ्काश श्शौचाद्दीनस्ताथाऽशुचिः। लक्षण्यवदलक्षण्यो दुश्शीलश्शीलवानिव।।2.109.5।। अधर्मं धर्मवेशेण यदीमं लोकसङ्कुरम्। अभिपत्स्ये शुभं हित्वा क्रियाविधिविवर्जितम्।।2.109.6।। कश्चेतयानः पुरुषः कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः। बहुमंस्यति मां लोके दुर्वृत्तं लोकदूषणम्।।2.109.7।।
186.e: If like a man who appears noble, though ignoble, clean, though unclean or dishonest, auspicious, though inauspicious, a man of character, though depraved, I forsake auspicious ways for unrighteousness, abandon pious acts and scriptural practices and indulge, under the cloak of dharma, in acts of wickedness by causing harm and confusion to the world, will any sensible man with a sense of discrimination between should and should not hold me in high esteem?

186.sa: कस्य दास्याम्यहं वृत्तं केन वा स्वर्गमाप्नुयाम्। आनया वर्तमानो हि वृत्त्या हीनप्रतिज्ञया।।2.109.8।।
186.e: How can I advise others for a virtuous conduct or how can I attain heaven if I break the vow which I follow at present.

186.sa: कामवृत्तस्त्वयं लोकः कृत्स्न स्समुपवर्तते। यद्वृत्ता स्सन्ति राजानस्तद्वृत्ता स्सन्ति हि प्रजाः।।2.109.9।।
186.e: The entire world conducts itself as per its own sweet will. Therefore the subjects will follow the same path as their kings.

186.sa: सत्यमेवानृशंसं च राजवृत्तं सनातनम्। तस्मात्सत्यात्मकं राज्यं सत्ये लोकः प्रतिष्ठितः।।2.109.10।।
186.e: Truth and nonviolence are the perpetual principles of kings. Therefore, a kingdom is based on truth. This world is firmly established in truth.

186.sa: ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च सत्यमेव हि मेनिरे। सत्यवादी हि लोकेऽस्मिन्परमं गच्छति क्षयम्।।2.109.11।।
186.e: Sages and gods all accept truth (as the supreme virtue). A truthful man of this world, attains the highest state (abode).

186.sa: उद्विजन्ते यथा सर्पान्नरादनृतवादिनः। धर्म स्सत्यं परो लोके मूलं स्वर्गस्य चोच्यते।।2.109.12।।
186.e: People are frightened at the sight of a man speaking untruth as though they have seen a serpent. Truth in this world is the greatest virtue and is said to be the very foundation of heaven.

186.sa: सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्माश्रिता सदा। सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम्।।2.109.13।।
186.e: Truth is God. The goddess of wealth always takes refuge in truth. Truth is the root of everything. It is supreme and there is nothing above it.

186.sa: दत्तमिष्टं हुतं चैव तप्तानि च तपांसि च। वेदा स्सत्यप्रतिष्ठाना स्तस्मात्सत्यपरो भवेत्।।2.109.14।।
186.e: Charity, sacrifice, libations, mortifications, asceticism and the Vedas have truth as their foundation. Therefore, every one should be an adherent of truth.

186.sa: एकः पालयते लोकमेकः पालयते कुलम्। मज्जत्येको हि निरय एक स्स्वर्गे महीयते।।2.109.15।।
186.e: One protects the world. Another runs his family. One plunges into hell. Another is honoured in heaven. (These are the fruits of truth and untruth).

186.sa: सोऽहं पितुर्नियोगं तु किमर्थं नानुपालये। सत्यप्रतिश्रव स्सत्यं सत्येन समयीकृतः।।2.109.16।।
186.e: I am always true to any promise. I am bound by truth. Why shouId I (now) disobey  my father's command (to keep his promise)?

186.sa: नैव लोभान्न मोहाद्वा न ह्यज्ञानात्तमोऽन्वितः। सेतुं सत्यस्य भेत्स्यामि गुरो स्सत्यप्रतिश्रवः।।2.109.17।।
186.e: I am always true to my promise. I will not break the bridge of truth of my father out of either greed or delusion or ignorance or illusion.

186.sa: असत्यसन्धस्य सतश्चलस्यास्थिरचेतसः। नैव देवा न पितरः प्रतीच्छन्तीति नः श्रुतम्।।2.109.18।।
186.e: We have heard that the offerings of a man inclined to untruth, of an unstable and unsteady mind are accepted neither by the gods nor by the ancestors.

186.sa: प्रत्यगात्ममिमं धर्मं सत्यं पश्याम्यहं स्वयम्। भार स्सत्पुरुषाचीर्णस्तदर्थमभिमन्यते।।2.109.19।।
186.e: I personally regard this righteousness practised by the virtuous as an evident form of truth, as the supreme self. Therefore, this burden (difficult task of living as an exile) is gratifying to me.

186.sa: क्षात्रं धर्ममहंत्यक्ष्ये ह्यधर्मं धर्मसंहितम्। क्षुद्रैर्नृशंसैर्लुब्धैश्च सेवितं पापकर्मभिः।।2.109.20।।
186.e: I renounce the socalled kshatriya code of conduct followed by the mean the cruel, the greedy and by men of evil deeds which is unrighteousness under the cloak of  righteousness.

186.sa: कायेन कुरुते पापं मनसा सम्प्रधार्य तत्। अनृतं जिह्वया चाह त्रिविधं कर्मपातकम्।।2.109.21।।
186.e: At first a man conceives an evil idea in his mind, then executes it through evil deed with his body and tells a lie through his tongue. Thus sinful action is three dimensional (mental, physical and vocal).

186.sa: भूमिः कीर्तिर्यशो लक्ष्मीः पुरुषं प्रार्थयन्ति हि। सत्यं समनुवर्तने सत्यमेव भजेत तत:।।2.109.22।।
186.e: Land (kingdom) glory, and wealth pursue a man, they long for him even if he is in heaven. Therefore, every one must take recourse to truth alone.

186.sa: श्रेष्ठं ह्यनार्यमेव स्याद्यद्भवानवधार्य माम्। आह युक्ति करैर्वाक्यैरिदं भद्रं कुरुष्व ह।।2.109.23।।
186.e: The course you thought excellent and 'this auspicious act' you urged me in a cleverlyworded statement to perform is ignoble indeed.

186.sa: कथं ह्यहं प्रतिज्ञाय वनवासमिमं गुरॊ:। भरतस्य करिष्यामि वचो हित्वा गुरोर्वचः।।2.109.24।।
186.e: Having sworn before my father that I would live in the forest, how can I act upon Bharata's request in disregard to my father's words?

186.sa: स्थिरा मया प्रतिज्ञाता प्रतिज्ञा गुरुसन्निधौ। प्रहृष्यमाणा सा देवी कैकेयी चाभवत्तदा।।2.109.25।।
186.e: I had taken a firm vow in the presence of my father (about my stay in the forest). And then Devi Kaikeyi was immensely delighted.

186.sa: वनवासं वसन्नेव शुचिर्नियतभोजनः। मूलपुष्पफलैः पुण्यैः पित्रून् देवांश्च तर्पयन्।।2.109.26।। सन्तुष्टपञ्चवर्गोऽहं लोकयात्रां प्रवर्तये। अकुह श्श्रद्धधानस्सन्कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः।।2.109.27।।
186.e: I shall spend the term of my forest life with faith and holiness and purity of mind and with regulated food and with ancestors and gods satisfied with offerings of roots, flowers and fruits, with my five senses contented and with a mind that discriminates between what ought to be done and what ought not to be done.

186.sa: वनवासं वसन्नेवं शुचिर्नियतभोजनः। मूलैः पुष्पैः फलैः पुण्यैः पित्रून् देवांश्च तर्पयन्।।2.109.26।। सन्तुष्टपञ्चवर्गोऽहं लोकयात्रां प्रवर्तये। अकुह श्श्रद्धधानस्सन्कार्याकार्यविचक्षणः।।2.109.27।।
186.e: I shall spend the term of my forest life with faith and holiness and purity of mind and with regulated food and with ancestors and gods satisfied with offerings of roots, flowers and fruits, with my five senses contented and with a mind that discriminates between what ought to be done and what ought not to be done.

186.sa: कर्मभूमिमां प्राप्य कर्तव्यं कर्म यच्छुभम्। अग्निर्वायुश्च सोमश्च कर्मणां फलभागिनः।।2.109.28।।
186.e: Having reached this land of (religious) actions, one should perform auspicious rites. As fruit of their actions, Agni, Vayu and Soma have obtained their status.

186.sa: शतं क्रतूनामाहृत्य देवराट् त्रिदिवं गतः। तपांस्युग्राणि चास्थाय दिवं याता महर्षयः।।2.109.29।।
186.e: After performing a hundred sacrifices, king of the gods (Indra) obtained (dominion over) heaven. Great sages attained heaven after resorting to intense mortifications.

186.sa: अमृष्यमाणः पुनरुग्रतेजाः निशम्य तं नास्तिकवाक्यहेतुम्। अथाब्रवीत्तं नृपतेस्तनूजो विगर्हमाणो वचनानि तस्य।।2.109.30।।
186.e: The highly energetic prince, Rama, could not tolerate these atheistic arguments of Jabali for which he had to utter these words full of disdain:

186.sa: सत्यं च धर्मं च पराक्रमं च भूतानुकम्पां प्रियवादितां च। द्विजातिदेवातिधिपूजनं च पन्थानमाहुस्त्रिदिवस्य सन्तः।।2.109.31।।
186.e: The virtuous maintain that truthfulness, righteousness, valour, compassion towards all beings, speaking pleasing words, paying homage to gods, brahmins and guests -- all these are  paths to heaven.

186.sa: तेनैवमाज्ञाय यथावदर्थमेकोदयं सम्प्रतिपद्य विप्राः। धर्मं चरन्त स्सकलं यथावत्काङ्क्षन्ति लोकागममप्रमत्ताः।।2.109.32।।
186.e: Therefore, brahmins who have rightly understood the meaning of righteousness and adopt, with unmost care, the righteous ways as laid down in the scriptures seek attainment of higher positions.

186.sa: निन्दाम्यहं कर्म कृतं पितुस्तद्यस्त्वामगृह्णाद्विषमस्थबुद्धिम्। बुद्ध्याऽनयैवंविधया चरन्तं सुनास्तिकं धर्मपथादपेतम्।।2.109.33।।
186.e: You are a great atheist, you have fallen from the path of righteousness. You are guided by an intellect which is extremely peridous. I, therefore, disapprove of my father's decision in inducting a man like you (into the council of ministers).

186.sa: यथा हि चोर: स‌ तथा हि बुद्धस्तथागतं नास्तिकमत्र विद्धि। तस्माद्धि य: श‌ङ्क्यतमः प्रजानाम् न नास्तिकेनाभिमुखो बुध: स्यात्।।2.109.34।।
186.e: Just as a thief, so is the Buddha (a wise men). Know that the Tathagatas are atheists. They are men most distrusted among the people. A learned man should avoid atheists. (Note: Verses 31 to 39 appear to be interpolations, It is anachronistic to talk about Buddha in Tretayuga.)

186.sa: त्वत्तो जनाः पूर्वतरे  द्विजाच्श्र शुभानि कर्माणि बहूनि चक्रुः। जित्वा सदेमं च परं च लोकं तस्माव्दिजा स्व‌स्ति हुतं कृतं च।।2.109.35।।
186.e: Men superior to you in preceding generations had conquered this world and the other world by always performing many auspicious acts. Twiceborn brahmins perform religious acts and offer libations for the welfare of the world.

186.sa: धर्मे रता: स‌त्पुरुषै: स‌मेतास्तेजस्विनो दानगुणप्रधानाः। अहिंसका वीतमलाश्च लोके भवन्ति पूज्या मुनयः प्रधानाः।।2.109.36।।
186.e: Those supreme ascetics who are radiant, devoted to righteousness and associated with men of virtue, with charity as their chief virtue, eschewing violence and purged of their impurities are truly worthy of reverence in this world.

186.sa: इति ब्रुवन्तं वचनं सरोषं रामं महात्मानमदीनसत्त्वम्। उवाच पथ्यं पुनरास्तिकं च सत्यं वच: सानुनयं च विप्रः।।2.109.37।।
186.e: Having heard the wrathful words of the magnanimous Rama of fearless intellect, that brahmin (Jabali) thus humbly replied in palatable, truthful words full of faith (in god).

186.sa: न नास्तिकानां वचनं ब्रवीम्यहं न नास्तिकोऽहं न च नास्ति किञ्चन। समीक्ष्य कालं पुनरास्तिकोऽभवं भवेय काले पुनरेव नास्तिकः।।2.109.38।।
186.e: I do not speak the language of atheists. I am not an atheist. I do not say that the next world does not exist. In keeping with time (occasion) I shall speak the language of a believer or a nonbeliever.

186.sa: न चापि कालोऽय मुपागतश्शनैर्यथा मया नास्तिकवागुदीरिता। निवर्तनार्थं तव राम कारणात् प्रसादनार्थं च मयैतदीरितम्।।2.109.39।।
186.e: O Rama, since the appropriate time has slowly come, I have uttered this. In order to persuade you to return and to propitiate you I have said these words. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे नवोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

187.sa: क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय रामं तु वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह। जाबालिरपि जानीते लोकस्यास्य गतागतिम्।।2.110.1।।
187.e: Seeing Rama angry Vasistha intercedes, saying that Jabali is wellaware of the exits and entrances of humans on earth.

187.sa: निवर्तयितुकामस्तु त्वामेतद्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। इमां लोकसमुत्पत्तिं लोकनाथ निबोध मे।।2.110.2।।
187.e: O lord of the worlds, Jabali had spoken all this only with the intention to make you return (to Ayodhya). Listen I shall (now) relate to you the origin of the world.

187.sa: सर्वं सलिलमेवासीत्पृथिवी यत्र निर्मिता। तत: स‌मभवद्ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूर्दैवतै: स‌ह।।2.110.3।।
187.e: At the beginning, all this was water from which the earth was created. Thereafter, the selfexistent Brahma along with the gods came into existence.

187.sa: स वराहस्ततो भूत्वा प्रोज्जहार वसुन्धराम्। असृजच्च जगत्सर्वं सह पुत्रैः कृतात्मभिः।।2.110.4।।
187.e: Then he assumed the form of a boar and uplifted the earth and created this world   with his progeny of purified souls.

187.sa: आकाशप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य अव्ययः। तस्मान्मरीचि: संज‌ज्ञे मरीचेः कश्यप: सुतः।।2.110.5।।
187.e: Eternal, changeless and imperishable Brahma arose from space and to him was born Marichi and to Marichi, Kasyapa.

187.sa: विवस्वान्काश्यपात् जज्ञे मनुर्वैवस्वत: स्वयम्। स तु प्रजापतिः पूर्वमिक्ष्वाकुस्तु मनो: सुतः।।2.110.6।।
187.e: Kasyapa begot Vivaswat (the Sun) and Vivaswat, Manu. This Manu was the first Prajapati to him whom was born Ikshvaku.

187.sa: यस्येयं प्रथमं दत्ता समृद्धा मनुना मही। तमिक्ष्वाकुमयोध्यायां राजानं विद्धि पूर्वकम्।।2.110.7।।
187.e: Manu had orginally bestowed the most prosperous earth on Ikshvaku and you know  Ikshvaku was the first king of Ayodhya.

187.sa: इक्ष्वाकोस्तु सुत  श्रीमान्कुक्षिरेवेति विश्रुतः। कुक्षेरथात्मजो वीरो विकुक्षिरुदपद्यत।।2.110.8।।
187.e: Ikshvaku had an illustrious son, wellknown as Kukshi and to Kukshi was born the heroic Vikukshi.

187.sa: विकुक्षेस्तु महातेजा बाणः पुत्र प्रतापवान्। बाणस्य तु महाबाहुरनरण्यो महात‌पा:।।2.110.9।।
187.e: The son of Vikukshi was highly energetic and powerful Bana and to him was born the mightyarmed Anaranya of great renown.

187.sa: नानावृष्टिर्बभूवास्मिन्नदुर्भिक्षं सतां वरे। अनरण्ये महाराजे तस्करो नापि कश्चन।।2.110.10।।
187.e: When Anaranya, the best of the virtuous, was ruling the kingdom, there was no drought, no famine and not even a thief (in his kingdom).

187.sa: अनरण्यान्महाबाहुः पृथु राजा बभूव ह। तस्मात्पृथोमेहाराजस्त्रिशङ्कुरुदपद्यत।।2.110.11।। स सत्यवचनाद् वीर: स‌शरीरो दिवं गतः।
187.e: Mightyarmed king Prithu was the son of Anaranya and Prithu was father of the great king Trishanku. That heroic Trishanku, on account of his truthfulness ascended the heaven with his physical body.

187.sa: त्रिशङ्कोरभवत्सूनुर्दुन्धुमारो महायशाः।।2.110.12।। दुन्धुमारान्महातेजा युवनाश्वो व्यजायत।
187.e: Trishanku's son was illustrious Dundhumara, father of the exceedingly powerful Yuvanaswa.

187.sa: युवनाश्वसुत श्श्रीमान्मान्धाता समपद्यत।।2.110.13।। मान्धातुस्त महातेजा: सुसन्धिरुदपद्यत। सुसन्धेरपि पुत्रौ द्वौ ध्रुवसन्धिः प्रसेनजित्।।2.110.14।। यशस्वी ध्रुवसन्धेस्तु भरतो रिपुसूदनः।
187.e: Majestic Mandhata was Yuvanasva's son and father of mighty Susandhi. Sudsandhi had two sons Dhruvasandhi and Prasenjit. Renowned Bharata, slayer of enemies, was the son of Dhruvasandhi.

187.sa: युवनाश्वसुत श्श्रीमान्मान्धाता समपद्यत।।2.110.13।। मान्धातुस्त महातेजा स्सुसन्धिरुदपद्यत। सुसन्धेरपि पुत्रौ द्वौ ध्रुवसन्धिः प्रसेनजित्।।2.110.14।। यशस्वी ध्रुवसन्धेस्तु भरतो रिपुसूदनः।
187.e: Majestic Mandhata was Yuvanasva's son and father of mighty Susandhi. Sudsandhi had two sons Dhruvasandhi and Prasenjit. Renowned Bharata, slayer of enemies, was the son of Dhruvasandhi.

187.sa: भरतात्तु महाबाहोरसितो नाम जायत।।2.110.15।। यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शत्रवः। हैहयास्तालजङ्घाश्च शूराश्च शशिबिन्दवः।।2.110.16।।
187.e: Mightyarmed Bharata had a son named Asita against whom the Haihayas, Talajanghas and the indomitable Sasibindus, the rival kings rose as enenmies.

187.sa: भरतात्तु महाबाहोरसितो नाम जायत।।2.110.15।। यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शत्रवः। हैहयास्तालजङ्घाश्च शूराश्च शशिबिन्दवः।।2.110.16।।
187.e: Mightyarmed Bharata had a son named Asita against whom the Haihayas, Talajanghas and the indomitable Sasibindus, the rival kings rose as enenmies.

187.sa: तांस्तु सर्वान्प्रतिव्यूह्य युद्धे राजा प्रवासितः। स च शैलवरे रम्ये बभूवाभिरतो मुनिः।।2.110.17।।
187.e: Although king Asita engaged all of them in a battle, he was (defeated and) driven into exile. He retired to a delightful, tall mountain and lived a life of contentment of a sage.

187.sa: द्वे चास्य भार्ये गर्भिण्यौ बभूवतुरिति श्रुतिः। एका गर्भविनाशाय सपत्न्यै गरलं ददौ।।2.110.18।।
187.e: Both his wives became pregnant. It is said that one of them gave the other poison (with the motive) to destroy the embryo.

187.sa: भार्गवश्च्यवनो नाम हिमवन्तमुपाश्रितः। तमृषिं समुपागम्य कालिन्दी त्वभ्यवादयत्।।2.110.19।। स तामभ्यवदद्विप्रो वरेप्सुं पुत्रजन्मनि।
पुत्रस्ते भविता देवि महात्मा लोकविश्रुतः।।2.110.20।। धार्मिकश्च सुशीलश्च वंशकर्ताऽरिसूदनः।
187.e: O queen, you will beget a son who will be magnanimous, virtuous, renowned in the world. He will be the perpetuator of the race and destroyer of enemies.

187.sa: कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं हृष्टा मुनिंतमनुमान्य च।।2.110.21।। पद्मपत्रसमानाक्षं पद्मगर्भसमप्रभम्। तत: सा गृहमागम्य देवी पुत्रं व्यजायत।।2.110.22।।
187.e: The queen was happy. She circumambulated the sage, took leave of him and came back home. Thereafter, she gave birth to a son who had eyes like lotus petals and who looked resplendent like Brahma.

187.sa: कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं हृष्टा मुनिंतमनुमान्य च।।2.110.21।। पद्मपत्रसमानाक्षं पद्मगर्भसमप्रभम्। तत: सा गृहमागम्य देवी पुत्रं व्यजायत।।2.110.22।।
187.e: The queen was happy. She circumambulated the sage, took leave of him and came back home. Thereafter, she gave birth to a son who had eyes like lotus petals and who looked resplendent like Brahma.

187.sa: सपत्न्या तु गरस्तस्यै दत्तो गर्भजिघांसया। गरेण सह तेनैव जात स्स सगरोऽभवत्।।2.110.23।।
187.e: With a motive to destroy the embryo her cowife had poisoned her. That child was born with gara or poison for which he was called  Sagara.

187.sa: स राजा सगरो नाम य: स‌मुद्रमखानयत्। इष्ट्वा पर्वणि वेगेन त्रासयन इमाः प्रजाः।।2.110.24।
187.e: The king Sagara performed a sacrifice on the fullmoon day. And swiftly dug the ocean that frightened the people.

187.sa: असमञ्जस्तु पुत्रोऽभूत्सगरस्येति न श्श्रुतम्। जीवन्नेव स पित्रा तु निरस्तः पापकर्मकृत्।।2.110.25।।
187.e: We have heard that a son, Asamanja by name, was born to Sagara. For his sinful deeds he was banished by his father while he was still alive.

187.sa: अंशुमानिति पुत्रोऽभूदसमञ्जस्य वीर्यवान्। दिलीपोंशुमतः पुत्रो दिलीपस्य भगीरथः।।2.110.26।।
187.e: Valiant Anshuman was the son of Asamanja and the father of Dilipa. Dilipa's son was Bhagiratha.

187.sa: भगीरथात्ककुत्स्थस्तु काकुत्स्था येन विश्रुताः। ककुत्स्थस्य च पुत्रोऽभूद्रघुर्येन च राघवाः।।2.110.27।।
187.e: To Bhagiratha was born Kakutstha, by whom your race is wellknown. A son Raghu was born to Kakutstha and hence all of you are known as Raghavas.

187.sa: रघोस्तु पुत्रस्तेजस्वी प्रवृद्धः पुरुषादकः। कल्माषपाद स्सौदास इत्येवं प्रथितो भुवि।।2.110.28।।
187.e: The illustrious son of Raghu became famous in the world under the names of  Kalmasapada and Sowdasa. The curse of a sage turned him a devourer of men for some years.

187.sa: कल्माषपादपुत्रोऽभूच्छङ्खणस्त्विति विश्रुतः। यस्तु तद्वीर्यमासाद्य सहसैन्यो व्यनीनशत्।।2.110.29।।
187.e: Shankhana was the famous son of Kalmashapada. Whoever challenged his prowess was routed  with his entire army.

187.sa: शङ्खणस्य च पुत्रोऽभूच्छूर श्रीमान्सुदर्शनः। सुदर्शनस्याग्निवर्णः अग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगः।।2.110.30।। शीघ्रगस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रशुश्रुवः। प्रशुश्रुवस्य पुत्रोभूदम्बरीषो महाद्युतिः।।2.110.31।। अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोभून्नहुषः सत्यविक्रमः। नहुषस्य च नाभागः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः।।2.110.32।। अजश्च सुव्रतश्चैव नाभागस्य सुतावुभौ। अजस्यैव च धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्सुतः।।2.110.33।।
187.e: The son of Shankhana was the glorious Sudarshana, father of Agnivarna. Shighraga was the son of Agnivarna whose son was Maru. Maru's son was Prashushruva and to Prashushruva was born splendid Ambarisha. Nahusha of indisputable prowess was the son of Ambarisha whose son was the supremely righteous Nabhaga. Nabhaga had two sons, Aja and Suvrata and Aja's son was the righteous king Dasaratha.

187.sa: शङ्खणस्य च पुत्रोऽभूच्छूर श्रीमान्सुदर्शनः। सुदर्शनस्याग्निवर्णः अग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगः।।2.110.30।। शीघ्रगस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रशुश्रुवः। प्रशुश्रुवस्य पुत्रोभूदम्बरीषो महाद्युतिः।।2.110.31।। अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोभून्नहुषः सत्यविक्रमः। नहुषस्य च नाभागः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः।।2.110.32।। अजश्च सुव्रतश्चैव नाभागस्य सुतावुभौ। अजस्यैव च धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्सुतः।।2.110.33।।
187.e: The son of Shankhana was the glorious Sudarshana, father of Agnivarna. Shighraga was the son of Agnivarna whose son was Maru. Maru's son was Prashushruva and to Prashushruva was born splendid Ambarisha. Nahusha of indisputable prowess was the son of Ambarisha whose son was the supremely righteous Nabhaga. Nabhaga had two sons, Aja and Suvrata and Aja's son was the righteous king Dasaratha.

187.sa: शङ्खणस्य च पुत्रोऽभूच्छूर श्रीमान्सुदर्शनः। सुदर्शनस्याग्निवर्णः अग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगः।।2.110.30।। शीघ्रगस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रशुश्रुवः। प्रशुश्रुवस्य पुत्रोभूदम्बरीषो महाद्युतिः।।2.110.31।। अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोभून्नहुषः सत्यविक्रमः। नहुषस्य च नाभागः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः।।2.110.32।। अजश्च सुव्रतश्चैव नाभागस्य सुतावुभौ। अजस्यैव च धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्सुतः।।2.110.33।।
187.e: The son of Shankhana was the glorious Sudarshana, father of Agnivarna. Shighraga was the son of Agnivarna whose son was Maru. Maru's son was Prashushruva and to Prashushruva was born splendid Ambarisha. Nahusha of indisputable prowess was the son of Ambarisha whose son was the supremely righteous Nabhaga. Nabhaga had two sons, Aja and Suvrata and Aja's son was the righteous king Dasaratha.

187.sa: शङ्खणस्य च पुत्रोऽभूच्छूर श्रीमान्सुदर्शनः। सुदर्शनस्याग्निवर्णः अग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगः।।2.110.30।। शीघ्रगस्य मरुः पुत्रो मरोः पुत्रः प्रशुश्रुवः। प्रशुश्रुवस्य पुत्रोभूदम्बरीषो महाद्युतिः।।2.110.31।। अम्बरीषस्य पुत्रोभून्नहुषः सत्यविक्रमः। नहुषस्य च नाभागः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः।।2.110.32।। अजश्च सुव्रतश्चैव नाभागस्य सुतावुभौ। अजस्यैव च धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथस्सुतः।।2.110.33।।
187.e: The son of Shankhana was the glorious Sudarshana, father of Agnivarna. Shighraga was the son of Agnivarna whose son was Maru. Maru's son was Prashushruva and to Prashushruva was born splendid Ambarisha. Nahusha of indisputable prowess was the son of Ambarisha whose son was the supremely righteous Nabhaga. Nabhaga had two sons, Aja and Suvrata and Aja's son was the righteous king Dasaratha.

187.sa: तस्य ज्येष्ठोऽसि दायादो राम इत्यभिविश्रुतः। तद्गृहाण स्वकं राज्यमवेक्षस्व जनं नृप।।2.110.34।।
187.e: Being the eldest son of king Dasaratha and widely  known as Rama you happen to be the  heir apparent. Hence, O king, accept the kingdom and look after the people.

188.sa: वसिष्ठस्तु तदा राममुक्त्वा राजपुरोहितः। अब्रवीद्धर्मसंयुक्तं पुनरेवापरं वचः।।2.111.1।।
188.e: Vasistha, the family priest, continued to speak to Rama on righteousness.

188.sa: पुरुषस्येह जातस्य भवन्ति गुरवस्त्रयः। आचार्यश्चैव काकुत्स्थ पिता माता च राघव।।2.111.2।।
188.e: Every man born has three preceptors. They are his teacher, father and mother.

188.sa: पिता ह्येवं जनयति पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ। प्रज्ञां ददाति चाचार्यस्तस्मात्स गुरुरुच्यते।।2.111.3।।
188.e: O best of men, the father brings forth a son. The teacher imparts him wisdom. Therefore, the teacher is considered superior.

188.sa: सोऽहं ते पितुराचार्यस्तव चैव परन्तप। मम त्वं वचनं कुर्वन्नातिवर्तेस्सतां गतिम्।।2.111.4।।
188.e: I was preceptor to your father and also to you. O destroyer of foes, by following my words, you will not transgress the path of the virtuous.

188.sa: इमा हि ते परिषद श्श्रेणयश्च द्विजास्तथा। एषु तात चरन्धर्मं नातिवर्ते: स‌तां गतिम्।।2.111.5।।
188.e: All these learned men, guilds of merchants and the twiceborn (brahmins) of this assembly are your men. By fulfilling your duty towards them, you will never swerve from the path of the virtuous.

188.sa: वृद्धाया धर्मशीलाया मातुर्नार्हस्यवर्तितुम्। अस्या हि वचनं कुर्वन्नातिवर्तेस्सतां गतिम्।।2.111.6।।
188.e: Here is your aged and righteous mother. It does not behove you to deny your service to her. By obeying her, you will never deviate from the path of the virtuous.

188.sa: भरतस्य वचः कुर्वन्याचमानस्य राघव। आत्मानं नातिवर्तेस्त्वं सत्यधर्मपराक्रम।।2.111.7।।
188.e: O scion of the Raghus whose strength springs from truth and righteousness, if you accede to the prayers of Bharata, you will not ignore the call of your soul.

188.sa: एवं मधुरमुक्तस्सन् गुरुणा राघवस्स्वयम्। प्रत्युवाच समासीनं वसिष्ठं पुरुषर्षभः।।2.111.8।।
188.e: When Rama, the best of men, was advised personally by Vasistha, the preceptor, with sweet words, he replied to him who was sitting beside him:

188.sa: यन्मातापितरौ वृत्तं तनये कुरुत: स‌दा। न सुप्रतिकरं तत् तु मात्रा पित्रा च यत्कृतम्।।2.111.9।। यथाशक्ति प्रदानेन स्वापनोच्छादनेन च। नित्यं च प्रियवादेन तथा संवर्धनेन च।।2.111.10।।
188.e: The course of action the parents always adopt in respect of their son, the benefits they confer on him according to their resources, the way they lull him to sleep and clothe him, the affectionate words they always speak to him and the way they bring him up all these cannot be repaid.

188.sa: यन्मातापितरौ वृत्तं तनये कुरुतस्सदा। न सुप्रतिकरं तत्तु मात्रा पित्रा च यत्कृतम्।।2.111.9।। यथाशक्तिप्रदानेन स्वापनोच्छादनेन च। नित्यं च प्रियवादेन तथा संवर्धनेन च।।2.111.10।।
188.e: The course of action the parents always adopt in respect of their son, the benefits they confer on him according to their resources, the way they lull him to sleep and clothe him, the affectionate words they always speak to him and the way they bring him up all these cannot be repaid.

188.sa: स हि राजा जनयिता पिता दशरथो मम। आज्ञातं यन्मया तस्य न तन्मिथ्या भविष्यति।।2.111.11।।
188.e: King Dasaratha is my father who begot me. The promise I made him shall not prove false.

188.sa: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण भरतः प्रत्यनन्तरम्। उवाच परमोदारस्सूतं परमदुर्मनाः।।2.111.12।।
188.e: Having been addressed by Rama in this way, Bharata of great generosity, in extreme distress, addressing the charioteer who was standing nearby said:

188.sa: इह मे स्थण्डिले शीघ्रं कुशानास्तर सारथे। आर्यं प्रत्युपवेक्ष्यामि यावन्मे न प्रसीदति।।2.111.13।।
188.e: O charioteer, quickly spread kusa grass on the bare ground. Until my esteemed brother shows his grace, I shall lie down here -- waiting.

188.sa: अनाहारो निरालोको धनहीनो यथा द्विजः। शेष्ये पुरस्ताच्छालाया यावन्न प्रतियास्यति।।2.111.14।।
188.e: Like a poor brahmin, starving, my face muffled, I shall lie down in front of the hut until he agrees to return.

188.sa: स तु राममवेक्षन्तं सुमन्त्रं पेक्ष्य दुर्मनाः। कुशोत्तरमुपस्थाप्य भूमावेवाऽस्तरत्स्वयम्।।2.111.15।।
188.e: Bharata was mentally disturbed saw Sumantra waiting for Rama's order. Then he himself brought a heap of kusa grass and spread it on the ground.

188.sa: तमुवाच महातेजा रामो राजर्षिसत्तमः। किं मां भरत कुर्वाणं तात प्रत्युपवेक्ष्यसि।।2.111.16।।
188.e: Rama, the foremost of royal sages and highly powerful said, 'Dear Bharata, what wrong have I done that you should prevent me by lying down in front of me?'

188.sa: ब्राह्मणो ह्येकपार्श्वेन नरान्रोद्धुमिहार्हति। न तु मूर्धाभिषिक्तानां विधिः प्रत्युपवेशने।।2.111.17।।
188.e: A brahmin alone is competent in this world to prevent a person by lying down on one side (in front of him). One who is anointed king is not permitted by (scriptural) tradition to squat in protest.

188.sa: उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल हित्वैतद्दारुणं व्रतम्। पुरवर्यामितः क्षिप्रमयोध्यां याहि राघव।।2.111.18।।
188.e: O Bharata, O tiger among men, O scion of the Raghu race give up this formidable vow. Arise and quickly return to Ayodhya, the best of cities.

188.sa: आसीनस्त्वेव भरतः पौरजानपदं जनम्। उवाच सर्वतः प्रेक्ष्य किमार्यं नानुशासथ।।2.111.19।।
188.e: While remaining seated, Bharata looking all around at the inhabitants from towns and villages, questioned them 'why don't you all persuade my esteemed brother to return'.

188.sa: ते तदोचुर्महात्मानं पौरजानपदा जनाः। काकुत्स्थमभिजानीमः सम्यग् वदति राघवः।।2.111.20।।
188.e: Those inhabitants from towns and villages replied to the magnanimous Bharata 'we  know the scion of the Kakutha dynasty, Rama, very well. What he has said is proper'.

188.sa: एषोऽपि हि महाभागः पितुर्वचसि तिष्ठति। अत एव न शक्ताः स्मो व्यावर्तयितुमञ्जसा।।2.111.21।।
188.e: Highly distinguished Rama is firmly fixed on the command of his father. That is why we are incapable of making him return quickly.

188.sa: तेषामाज्ञाय वचनं रामो वचनमब्रवीत्। एवं निबोध वचनं सुहृदां धर्मचक्षुषाम्।।2.111.22।।
188.e: Having understood their words, Rama said to him, 'Listen to the words of our friends who have a righteous vision.'

188.sa: एतच्चैवोभयं श्रुत्वा सम्यक्सम्पश्य राघव। उत्तिष्ठ त्वं महाबाहो मां च स्पृश तथोदकम्।।2.111.23।।
188.e: O mightyarmed son of the Raghus, you have heard both (them and me). Carefully think over. Arise. Touch me and sip water.

188.sa: अथोत्थाय जलंस्पृष्ट्वा भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। श्रुण्वन्तु मे परिषदो मन्त्रिण श्श्रेणयस्तथा।।2.111.24।।
188.e: Then Bharata stood up and performed achamana (sipping of water) and said 'let the assembly of  learned men, counsellors and guildsmen hear me'.

188.sa: न याचे पितरं राज्यं नानुशासामि मातरम्। आर्यं परमधर्मज्ञं नानुजानामि राघवम्।।2.111.25।।
188.e: I never asked my father to confer the kingdom on me. I never urged my mother to seek the kingdom for me. I never supported the exile of my esteemed brother Rama, who is supreme in the knowleldge of righteousness.

188.sa: यदित्ववश्यं वस्तव्यं कर्तव्यं च पितुर्वचः। अहमेव निवत्स्यामि चतुर्दश समा वने।।2.111.26।।
188.e: If it is absolutely essential to live in the forest in accordance with the command of my father, I myself  shall also dwell in the forest for fourteen years.

188.sa: धर्मात्मा तस्य तथ्येन भ्रातुर्वाक्येन विस्मितः। उवाच राम स्सम्प्रेक्ष्य पौरजानपदं जनम्।।2.111.27।।
188.e: On hearing the genuine sentiments of his brother, righteous Rama was astonished. He said to the inhabitants from towns and villages:

188.sa: विक्रीतमाहितं क्रीतं यत्पित्रा जीवता मम। न तल्लोपयितुं शक्यं मया वा भरतेन वा।।2.111.28।।
188.e: Neither Bharata nor I can in any way annul anything which was sold, pledged or bought by my father during his lifetime.

188.sa: उपधिर्न मया कार्यो वनवासे जुगुप्सितः। युक्तमुक्तं च कैकेय्या पित्रा मे सुकृतं कृतम्।।2.111.29।।
188.e: As far as living in the forest is concerned it is reprehensible to keep a subsitute for me and it shall not be done. Kaikeyi has acted rightfully and my father has taken the proper decision.

188.sa: जानामि भरतं क्षान्तं गुरुसत्कारकारिणम्। सर्वमेवात्र कल्याणं सत्यसन्धे महात्मनि।।2.111.30।।
188.e: I know Bharata as a man of forbearance and one who honours elders. Everything will turn out well for this great soul wedded to truth.

188.sa: अनेन धर्मशीलेन वनात्प्रत्यागतः पुनः। भ्रात्रा सह भविष्यामि पृथिव्याः पतिरुत्तमः।।2.111.31।।
188.e: On returning from the forest, I shall become the supreme lord of this earth along with this virtuous brother.

188.sa: वृतो हि राजा कैकेय्या मया तद्वचनं कृतम्। अनृतान्मोचयानेन पितरं तं महीपतिम्।।2.111.32।।
188.e: The king (Dasaratha) was solicited by Kaikeyi and I shall abide. Therefore, you also release the lord of the earth, our father from the charge of falsehood. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकादशोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredeleventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

189.sa: तमप्रतिमतेजोभ्यां भ्रातृभ्यां रोमहर्षणम्। विस्मिता: स‌ङ्गमं प्रेक्ष्य समवेता महर्षयः।।2.112.1।।
189.e: The great sages assembled there were amazed at witnessing the meeting of the two brothers (Rama and Bharata) of umparalleled briliance.

189.sa: अन्तर्हिता मुनिगणास्सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। तौ भ्रातरौ महात्मानौ काकुत्स्थौ प्रशशंसिरे।।2.112.2।।
189.e: The hosts of sages, siddhas and devarshis watching invisible the two Kakutstha  brothers extoled them.

189.sa: स धन्यो यस्य पुत्रौ द्वौ धर्मज्ञौ धर्मविक्रमौ। श्रुत्वा वयं हि सम्भाषामुभयोस्स्पृहयामहे।।2.112.3।।
189.e: On hearing their dialogue we are deeply drawn towards them, these two sons of king Dasaratha who was fortunate to have these practioners of righteousness and whose strength is dharma.

189.sa: ततस्त्वृषिगणाः क्षिप्रं दशग्रीववधैषिणः। भरतं राजशार्दूलमित्यूचु: स‌ङ्गता वचः।।2.112.4।।
189.e: Thereafter hosts of rishis desiring the speedy destruction of tenheaded Ravana said these words to Bharata, the best of kings.

189.sa: कुले जात महाप्राज्ञ महावृत्त महायशः। ग्राह्यं रामस्य वाक्यं ते पितरं यद्यवेक्षसे।।2.112.5।।
189.e: O Bharata, born in an illustrious race, highly sagacious and a man of virtuous conduct and great renown, accept Rama's proposal if you have any regard for your father.

189.sa: सदाऽनृणमिमं रामं वयमिच्छामहे पितुः। आनृणत्वाच्च कैकेय्या: स्वर्गम् दशरथो गतः।।2.112.6।।
189.e: We always desire that Rama should discharge his debt to his father. Dasaratha, who by redeeming himself of his obligation to Kaikeyi, had ascended heaven.

189.sa: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं गन्धर्वा: स‌महर्षयः। राजर्षयश्चैव तदा सर्वे स्वां स्वां गतिं गताः।।2.112.7।।
189.e: Then the great rishis, gandharvas and royal sages having said this, returned to their respective abodes.

189.sa: ह्लादितस्तेन वाक्येन शुभेन शुभदर्शनः। राम स्संहृष्टवदनस्तानृषीनभ्यपूजयत्।।2.112.8।।
189.e: Of pleasing appearance, Rama, gladdened by the auspicious statements (of the sages),  paid them homage with a cheerful countenance.

189.sa: त्रस्तगात्रस्तु भरतस्स वाचा सज्जमानया। कृताञ्जलिरिदं वाक्यं राघवं पुनरब्रवीत्।।2.112.9।।
189.e: Before Bharata, with his limbs trembling and with palms folded (in reverence) was   ready to depart, he said to Rama:

189.sa: राजधर्ममनुप्रेक्ष्य कुलधर्मानुसन्ततिम्। कर्तुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ मम मातुश्च याचनाम्।।2.112.10।।
189.e: O Rama, keeping in view the code of kings and tradition of our family, it behoves you to consider my supplication and that of my mother.

189.sa: रक्षितुं सुमहद्राज्यमहमेकस्तु नोत्सहे। पौरजानपदांश्चापि रक्तान्रञ्जयितुं तथा।।2.112.11।।
189.e: I do not venture to protect this kingdom all by myself and keep the inhabitants of the towns and villages who are loyal to you pleased.

189.sa: ज्ञातयश्च हि योधाश्च मित्राणि सुहृदश्च नः। त्वामेव प्रतिवीक्षन्ते पर्जन्यमिव कर्षकाः।।2.112.12।।
189.e: All our relatives, warriors, friends and wellwishers long to see you like farmers yearn for the raincloud.

189.sa: इदं राज्यं महाप्राज्ञ स्थापय प्रतिपद्य हि। शक्तिमानसि काकुत्स्थ लोकस्य परिपालने।।2.112.13।।
189.e: O sagacious Rama, accept this kingdom and ensure its stability. You are powerful enough to govern this world. So accept this kingdom and restore its stability.

189.sa: इत्युक्त्वा न्यपतद्भ्रातुः पादयोर्भरतस्तदा। भृशं सम्प्रार्थयामास राममेव प्रियंवदः।।2.112.14।।
189.e: Having said this, Bharata, fell at the feet of his brother, and speaking sweetly, he profusely  entreated  Rama.

189.sa: तमङ्के भरतं कृत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्। श्यामं नलिनपत्राक्षं मत्तहंसस्वरं स्वयम्।।2.112.15।।
189.e: Rama took his in his arms Bharata who had a darkblue complexion, whose eyes were like petals of lotus and whose voice was the voice of an amorous swan.

189.sa: आगता त्वामियं बुद्धिस्स्वजा वैनयिकी च या। भृशमुत्सहसे तात रक्षितुं पृथिवीमपि।।2.112.16।।
189.e: O child, this wisdom of yours is both inborn and imbibed through training. With this, you are perfectly capable of protecting the earth.

189.sa: अमात्यैश्च सुहृद्भिश्च बुद्धिमद्भिश्च मन्त्रिभिः। सर्वकार्याणि सम्मन्त्र्य सुमहन्त्यपि कारय।।2.112.17।।
189.e: After due consultation with ministers, friends, counsellors and prudent persons,   accomplish all tasks, however formidable they may appear.

189.sa: लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रादपेयाद्वा हिमवान्वा हिमं त्यजेत्। अतीयात्सागरो वेलां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितुः।।2.112.18।।
189.e: The Moon might lose its splendour, snow might abandon the Himavat mountain, the ocean might overstep its shores, but I shall not forsake the promise made to my father.

189.sa: कामाद्वा तात लोभाद्वा मात्रातुभ्यमिदं कृतम्। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्।।2.112.19।।
189.e: Dear brother, whether out of affection or greed, your mother has done this for your sake. It should not agitate your mind. You should conduct yourself as one should towards one's mother.

189.sa: एवं ब्रुवाणं भरतः कौसल्यासुतमब्रवीत्। तेजसाऽऽदित्यसङ्काशं प्रतिपच्चन्द्रदर्शनम्।।2.112.20।।
189.e: On hearing this, Bharata replied to the son of  Kausalya who looked like the Sun or the new Moon in brilliance:

189.sa: आधिरोहाऽर्य पादाभ्यां पादुके हेमभूषिते। एतेहि सर्वलोकस्य योगक्षेमं विधास्यतः।।2.112.21।।
189.e: O noble one, place your feet on these sandals decorated with gold. They will secure the prosperity and safety of the entire world.

189.sa: सोऽधिरुह्य नरव्याघ्रः पादुके ह्यवरुह्य च। प्रायच्छत्सुमहातेजा भरताय महात्मने।।2.112.22।।
189.e: Rama, the best of men, one with great brilliance, put on and then put off the sandals  and presented them to the magnanimous Bharata.

189.sa: स पादुके सम्प्रणम्य रामं वचनमब्रवीत् चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि जटाचीरधरो ह्याहम्।।2.112.23।। फलमूलाशनो वीर भवेयं रघुनन्दन। तवाऽगमनमाकाङ्क्षान्वसन्वै नगराद्बहिः।।2.112.24।। तव पादुकयोर्न्यस्तराज्यतन्त्रः परन्तप।
189.e: Bharata bowed before the sandals and said to Rama, 'O tormentorr of enemies, O hero, wearing matted locks and bark garments, living on fruits and roots, placing the responsibility of ruling the kingdom on your sandals and looking forward to your arrival, I shall reside outside the city for fourteen years.'

189.sa: स पादुके सम्प्रणम्य रामं वचनमब्रवीत् चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि जटाचीरधरो ह्याहम्।।2.112.23।। फलमूलाशनो वीर भवेयं रघुनन्दन। तवाऽगमनमाकाङ्क्षान्वसन्वै नगराद्बहिः।।2.112.24।। तव पादुकयोर्न्यस्तराज्यतन्त्रः परन्तप।
189.e: Bharata bowed before the sandals and said to Rama, 'O tormentorr of enemies, O hero, wearing matted locks and bark garments, living on fruits and roots, placing the responsibility of ruling the kingdom on your sandals and looking forward to your arrival, I shall reside outside the city for fourteen years.'

189.sa: चतुर्दशे तु संपूर्णे वर्षेऽहनि रघूत्तम।।2.112.25।। न द्रक्ष्यामि यदि त्वां तु प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्।
189.e: O best of the Raghus, if I do not behold you on the day after completion of fourteen years I shall enter the blazing fire.

189.sa: तथेति च प्रतिज्ञाय तं परिष्वज्य सादरम्।।2.112.26।। शत्रुघ्नं च परिष्वज्य भरतं चेदमब्रवीत्।
189.e: 'Be it so', assured Rama and then affectionately embracing both Bharata and Satrughna, said to Bharata:

189.sa: मातरं रक्ष कैकेयीं मा रोषं कुरु तां प्रति।।2.112.27।। मया च सीतया चैव शप्तोऽसि रघुसत्तम। इत्युक्त्वाऽश्रुपरीताक्षो भ्रातरं विससर्ज ह।।2.112.28।।
189.e: Look after your mother, O chief of the Raghus Do not be angry with her. Swear in my name and in the name of Sita. So saying, eyes filled with tears, Rama took leave of his brother.

189.sa: मातरं रक्ष कैकेयीं मा रोषं कुरु तां प्रति।।2.112.27।। मया च सीतया चैव शप्तोऽसि रघुसत्तम। इत्युक्त्वाऽश्रुपरीताक्षो भ्रातरं विससर्ज ह।।2.112.28।।
189.e: Look after your mother, O chief of the Raghus Do not be angry with her. Swear in my name and in the name of Sita. So saying, eyes filled with tears, Rama took leave of his brother.

189.sa: स पादुके ते भरतः प्रतापवान् स्वलङ्कृते सम्परिपूज्य धर्मवित्। प्रदक्षिणं चैव चकार राघवम् चकार ते चोत्तमनागमूर्धनि।।2.112.29।।
189.e: The valiant and righteous Bharata, worshipped the welldecorated sandals and after circumambulating Rama reverentially placed them atop the best of elephants.

189.sa: अथाऽनुपूर्व्यात्प्रतिनन्द्य तं जनं गुरूंश्च मन्त्रिप्रकृतीस्तथाऽनुजौ। व्यसर्जयद्राघववंशवर्धनस्थिरः स्वधर्मे हिमवानिवाचलः।।2.112.30।।
189.e: Inflexibly fixed in his own code of righteouness, like the Himavat mountain, Rama, the enhancer of the progeny of the Raghu dynasty, paid respect due to the preceptors, ministers and subjects in accordance with their rank, blessed his younger brothers, Bharata and Satrughna and sent them forth.

189.sa: तं मातरो बाष्पगृहीतकण्ठ्यो दुःखेन नामन्त्रयितुं हि शेकुः। स त्वेव मात्रृ़रभिवाद्य सर्वारुदन्कुटीं स्वां प्रविवेश राघवः।।2.112.31।।
189.e: His mothers were unable to bid him farewell their throats were choked with tears of sorrow but Rama himself paid obeisance to them and entered his hut in tears. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्वादशोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredtwelfth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

190.sa: तत श्शिरसि कृत्वा तु पादुके भरतस्तदा। आरुरोह रथं हृष्टः शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः।।2.113.1।।
190.e: Then Bharata accompanied by Satrughna, placing the sandals on his head in delight, boarded the chariot.

190.sa: वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिश्च दृढव्रतः। अग्रतः प्रययु स्सर्वे मन्त्रिणो मन्त्रपूजिताः।।2.113.2।।
190.e: Vasishta, Vamadeva, Jabali of rigorous penance and all the ministers honoured for their counsel proceeded ahead.

190.sa: मन्दाकिनीं नदीं रम्यां प्राङ्मुखास्ते ययुस्तदा। प्रदक्षिणं च कुर्वाणाश्चित्रकूटं महागिरिम्।।2.113.3।।
190.e: All of them circumambulated the mighty mountain Chitrakuta and proceeded east towards the charming river Mandakini.

190.sa: पश्यन्धातुसहस्राणि रम्याणि विविधानि च। प्रययौ तस्य पार्श्वेन ससैन्यो भरतस्तदा।।2.113.4।।
190.e: Beholding a thousand varieties of beautiful minerals, Bharata with his army proceeded  alongside the mountain.

190.sa: अदूराच्चित्रकूटस्य ददर्श भरतस्तदा। आश्रमं यत्र स मुनिर्भरद्वाजः कृतालयः।।2.113.5।।
190.e: Not far from Chitrakuta mountain, Bharata beheld a hermitage where sage Bharadwaja resided.

190.sa: स तमाश्रममागम्य भरद्वाजस्य बुद्धिमान्। अवतीर्य रथात्पादौ ववन्दे भरतस्तदा।।2.113.6।।
190.e: On approaching the hermitage of sage Bharadwaja, Bharata  alighted from the chariot, and prostrated at his feet.

190.sa: ततो हृष्टो भरद्वाजो भरतं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। अपि कृत्यं कृतं तात रामेण च समागतम्।।2.113.7।।
190.e: Then Bhardwaja asked Bharata in delight, My son, have you accomplished your task?  Did you meet  Rama?

190.sa: एवमुक्त स्स तु ततो भरद्वाजेन धीमता। प्रत्युवाच भरद्वाजं भरतो धर्मवत्सलः।।2.113.8।।
190.e: Having been thus addressed by wise Bharadwaja, Bharata, devoted to righteousness, replied:

190.sa: स याच्यमानो गुरुणा मया च दृढविक्रमः। राघवः परमप्रीतो वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.113.9।।
190.e: Entreated by me and by preceptor (Vasistha), the highly pleased Rama with his  firmness of mind replied  to Vasistha:

190.sa: पितुः प्रतिज्ञां तामेव पालयिष्यामि तत्त्वतः। चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि या प्रतिज्ञा पितुर्मम।।2.113.10।।
190.e: In sooth, I shall honour the words of promise given by my father and live in the forest for fourteen years, as promised.

190.sa: एवमुक्तो महाप्राज्ञो वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह। वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं राघवं वचनं महत्।।2.113.11।।
190.e: On hearing him, Vasistha a great intellectual and highly eloquent one replied to Rama, skilled in words of deep significance.

190.sa: एते प्रयच्छ संहृष्टः पादुके हेमभूषिते। अयोध्यायां महाप्राज्ञ योगक्षेमकरे तव।।2.113.12।।
190.e: O extremely sagacious one, bestow with pleasure your sandals decked with gold for security and safety of Ayodhya.

190.sa: एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन राघवः प्राङ्मुखः स्थितः। पादुके ह्यधिरुह्यैते मम राज्याय वै ददौ।।2.113.13।।
190.e: Thus addressed by Vasistha, Rama stood facing eastward wearing these sandals. and bestowed them on me for the sake of ruling the kingdom.

190.sa: निवृत्तोऽहमनुज्ञातो रामेण सुमहात्मना। अयोध्यामेव गच्छामि गृहीत्वा पादुके शुभे।।2.113.14।।
190.e: I am now returning to Ayodhya with these auspicious sandals permitted by the  magnanimous Rama.

190.sa: एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरतस्य महात्मनः। भरद्वाजश्शुभतरं मुनिर्वाक्यमुवाच तम्।।2.113.15।।
190.e: Hearing the auspicious words of  the magnanimous Bharata, sage Bharadwaja said to  him in words still more  auspicious.

190.sa: नैतच्चित्रं नरव्याघ्र शीलवृत्तवतां वर। यदार्यं त्वयि तिष्ठेत्तु निम्ने सृष्टमिवोदकम्।।2.113.16।।
190.e: O best of men, foremost among men of excellent character and dispositon, it is not surprising that all noble qualities come to reside in you naturally like water poured flowing downward.

190.sa: अमृत स्समहाबाहुः पिता दशरथस्तव। यस्य त्वमीदृश: पुत्रो धर्मज्ञो धर्मवत्सलः।।2.113.17।।
190.e: With you as his son, endowed with qualities of righteousness and devotion to duty, your mightyarmed father Dasaratha is not dead. (He lives through you).

190.sa: तमृषिं तु महात्मानमुक्तवाक्यं कृताञ्जलिः। आमन्त्रयितुमारेभे चरणावुपगृह्य च।।2.113.18।।
190.e: Hearing the words of the magnanimous Bharadwaja, Bharata paid his respect, folding his palms,  and clasping the feet of the sage and sought his permission to leave.

190.sa: ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा भरद्वाजं पुनः पुनः। भरतस्तु ययौ श्रीमानयोध्यां सह मन्त्रिभिः।।2.113.19।।
190.e: Then illustrious Bharata circumambulated the sage several times in homage  before he set out for Ayodhya with his counsellors.

190.sa: यानैश्च शकटैश्चैव हयैर्नागैश्च सा चमूः। पुनर्निवृत्ता विस्तीर्णा भरतस्यानुयायिनी।।2.113.20 ।।
190.e: The vast army of Bharata with all its carriages, carts, horses and elephants following   him again turned  back towards Ayodhya.

190.sa: ततस्ते यमुनां दिव्यां नदीं तीर्त्वोर्मिमालिनीम्। ददृशुस्तां पुन स्सर्वे गङ्गां शुभजलां नदीम्।।2.113.21।।
190.e: Thereafter, all of them crossed  the divine river Yamuna wreathed in waves and, beheld  the Ganga of sacred waters once again.

190.sa: तां रम्यजलसंपूर्णां सन्तीर्य सहबान्धवः शृङ्गिबेरपुरं रम्यं प्रविवेश ससैनिकः। शृङ्गिबेरपुराद्भूय स्त्वयोध्यां सन्ददर्श ह।।2.113.22।।
190.e: Bharata along with his kins and his army crossed the Ganga with its overflowing,  wonderful waters and entered the beautiful city of Sringiberapura and from there he proceeded until he beheld the city of Ayodhya.

190.sa: अयोध्यां च ततो दृष्ट्वा पित्रा भ्रात्रा विवर्जिताम्। भरतो दुःख सन्तप्त स्सारथिं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.113.23।।
190.e: On seeing the city of Ayodhya bereft of his father and brothers, Bharata, consumed with grief, said to the charioteer:

190.sa: सारथे पश्य विध्वस्ता साऽयोध्या न प्रकाशते। निराकारा निरानन्दा दीना प्रतिहतस्वरा।।2.113.24।।
190.e: O charioteer, look, Ayodhya is in shapeless shambles. It is silent and cheerless. It is dull and desolate. It shines no more. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रयोदशोरशततमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the hundredthirteenth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

191.sa: स्निग्धगम्भीरघोषेण स्यन्दनेनोपयान्प्रभुः। अयोध्यां भरतः क्षिप्रं प्रविवेश महायशाः।।2.114.1।।
191.e: Bharata, the renowned lord (of Ayodhya) travelled on the chariot that produced a deep, soothing, sound. And entered Ayodhya soon.

191.sa: बिडालोलूकचरितामालीननरवारणाम्। तिमिराभ्याहतां कालीमप्रकाशां निशामिव।।2.114.2।।
राहुशत्रोः प्रियां पत्नीं श्रिया प्रज्वलितप्रभाम्। ग्रहेणाभ्युत्थितेनैकां रोहिणीमिव पीडिताम्।।2.114.3।।
191.e: (The city looked) like Rohini, the beloved consort of the Moon, the star which was majesticlly radiating flaming brilliance and now, tormented by the exalted Rahu which has eclipsed the Moon, shines alone.

191.sa: अल्पोष्णक्षुब्धसलिलां घर्मोत्तप्तविहङ्गमाम्। लीनमीनझषग्राहां कृशां गिरिनदीमिव।।2.114.4।।
191.e: (It appeared) like a lean mountainstream with scant, hot and turbid waters, with scorched aquatic birds and with small and large fishes and crocodiles dead due to the heat of the Sun.

191.sa: विधूमामिव हेमाभामध्वराग्ने स्समुत्थिताम्। हविरभ्युक्षितां पश्चाच्छिखां विप्रलयं गताम्।।2.114.5।।
विध्वस्तकवचां रुग्णगजवाजिरथध्वजाम्। हतप्रवीरामापन्नां चमूमिव महाहवे।।2.114.6।।
191.e: warriors slain in the great battle (the city appeared desolate).

191.sa: सफेनां सस्वनां भूत्वा सागरस्य समुत्थिताम्। प्रशान्तमारुतोद्धूतां जलोर्मिमिव निस्स्वनाम्।।2.114.7।।
त्यक्तां यज्ञायुधैः सर्वैरभिरूपैश्च याजकैः। सुत्याकाले सुनिर्वृत्ते वेदिं गतरवामिव।।2.114.8।।
गोष्ठमध्ये स्थितामार्तामचरन्तीं तृणं नवम्। गोवृषेण परित्यक्तां गवां पक्तिमिवोत्सुकाम्।।2.114.9।।
191.e: the midst of the herd despairs and no longer grazes the new grass.

191.sa: प्रभाकराद्यै स्सुस्निग्धैः प्रज्वलद्भिरिवोत्तमैः। वियुक्तां मणिभिर्जात्यैर्नवां मुक्तावलीमिव।।2.114.10।।
सहसा चलितां स्थानान्महीं पुण्यक्षयाद्गताम्। संवृतद्युतिविस्तारां तारामिव दिवश्च्युताम्।।2.114.11।।
पुष्पनद्धां वसन्तान्ते मत्तभ्रमरनादिताम्। द्रुतदावाग्नि विप्लुष्टां क्लान्तां वनलतामिव।।2.114.12।।
191.e: with the melodious humming of intoxicated bees and suddenly shrivelling, ravaged by the fastspreading forest fire.

191.sa: सम्मूढनिगमांस्तब्धां संक्षिप्तविपणापणाम्। प्रच्छन्नशशिनक्षत्रां द्यामिवाम्बुधरैर्वृताम्।।2.114.13।।
191.e: Ayodhya with its markets and shops closed, and its merchants in a daze looked like the sky covered with clouds obscuring the Moon and stars.

191.sa: क्षीणपानोत्तमैर्भग्नैः शरावैरभिसंवृताम्। हतशौण्डामिव ध्वस्तांं पानभूमिमसंस्कृताम्।।2.114.14।।
191.e: (Ayodhya looked) like an uncleansed drinking place with broken pitchers emptied of excellent wine scattered around and with drunkards lying dead in the open.

191.sa: वृक्णभूमितलां निम्नां वृक्णपात्रैस्समावृताम्। उपयुक्तोदकां भग्नां प्रपां निपतितामिव।।2.114.15।।
191.e: (Ayodhya appeared) like a ruined well, its foundations broken and sunken into the earth, its water used up, with broken pots scattered around, its riven surface forming a dale.

191.sa: विपुलां विततां चैव युक्तपाशां तरस्विनाम्। भूमौ बाणैर्विनिष्कृत्तां पतितां ज्यामिवायुधात्।।2.114.16।।
सहसा युद्धशौण्डेन हयारोहेण वाहिताम्। निहतां प्रतिसैन्येन वडवामिव पातिताम्।।2.114.17।।
शुष्कतोयां महामत्स्यैः कूर्मैश्च बहुभिर्वृताम्। प्रभिन्नतटविस्तीर्णां वापीमिव हृतोत्पलाम्।।2.114.18।।
पुरुषस्याप्रहृष्टस्य प्रतिषिद्धानुलेपनाम्। सन्तप्तामिव शोकेन गात्रयष्टिमभूषणाम्।।2.114.19।।
प्रावृषि प्रविगाढायां प्रविष्टस्याभ्रमण्डलम्। प्रच्छन्नां नीलजीमूतैर्भास्करस्य प्रभामिव।।2.114.20।।
भरतस्तु रथस्थ स्सन् श्रीमान्दशरथात्मजः। वाहयन्तं रथश्रेष्ठं सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.114.21।।
191.e: Illustrious Bharata, son of Dasaratha, seated in his chariot, addressed the charioteer as he drove the most excellent of chariots saying:

191.sa: किं नु खल्वद्य गम्भीरो मूर्छितो न निशम्यते। यथापुरमयोध्यायां गीतवादित्रनिस्वनः।।2.114.22।।
191.e: How is it that in Ayodhya, the deep and allpervasive songs and sounds of musical instruments of the former days are not heard now?

191.sa: वारुणीमदगन्धश्च माल्यगन्धश्च मूर्छितः। धूपितागुरुगन्धश्च न प्रवाति समन्ततः।।2.114.23।।
191.e: The breeze no longer carries the intoxicating odour of spirituous liquor, the pervading fragrance of flower garlands and agaru (incense).

191.sa: यानप्रवरघोषश्च स्निग्धश्च हयनिस्वनः। प्रमत्तगजनादश्च महांश्च रथनिस्वनः।।2.114.24।। नेदानीं श्रूयते पुर्यामस्यां रामे विवासिते।
191.e: After Rama's the exile the clatter of excellent carriages, the pleasing neighing of horses and trumpeting of elephants in rut and the rattle of chariots are no longer heard now.

191.sa: चन्दनागरुगन्धांश्च महार्हाश्च नवस्रजः। गते हि रामे तरुणा स्संतप्ता नोपभुञ्जते।।2.114.25।।
191.e: Since Rama has departed, the young men in distress do not enjoy expensive incense of agaru and sandalwood paste and garlands of fresh flowers.

191.sa: चन्दनागरुगन्धांश्च महार्हाश्च नवस्रजः। गते हि रामे तरुणा स्संतप्ता नोपभुञ्जते।।2.114.25।।
191.e: Since Rama has departed, the young men in distress do not enjoy expensive incense of agaru and sandalwood paste and garlands of fresh flowers.

191.sa: बहिर्यात्रां न गच्छन्ति चित्रमाल्यधरा नराः। नोत्सवा स्सम्प्रवर्तन्ते रामशोकार्दिते पुरे।।2.114.27।।
191.e: This city is stricken with grief on account of Rama's departure. Men do not go out on pleasure jaunts wearing garlands of variegated flowers. Festivities are not celebrated.

191.sa: सह नूनं मम भ्रात्रा पुरस्यास्य द्युतिर्गता। न हि राजत्ययोध्येयं सासारेवार्जुनी क्षपा।।2.114.28।।
191.e: Certainly splendour has left along with my brother. Like the night when the rain pours down during the waning of the Moon, Ayodhya shines not.

191.sa: कदा नु खलु मे भ्राता महोत्सव इवाऽगतः। जनयिष्यत्ययोध्यायां हर्षं ग्रीष्म इवाम्बुदः।।2.114.29।।
191.e: When will my brother return to Ayodhya like a carnival and cause delight to every one  like summer clouds?

191.sa: तरुणैश्चारुवेषैश्च नरैरुन्नतगामिभिः। सम्पतद्भिरयोध्यायां नाभिभान्ति महापथाः।।2.114.30।।
191.e: The highways of Ayodhya thronged with groups of elegantly attired young men or adults with their majestic gait, do not shine.

191.sa: एवं बहुविधं जल्पन्विवेश वसतिं पितुः। तेन हीनां नरेन्द्रेण सिंहहीनां गुहामिव।।2.114.31।।
191.e: Thus mourning in several ways, Bharata entered his fathers' palace (now) bereft of the king like a cave without the lion.

192.sa: ततो निक्षिप्य मातृ़ स्स अयोध्यायां दृढ व्रतः। भरत श्शोकसन्तप्तो गुरूनिदमथाब्रवीत्।।2.115.1।।
192.e: After keeping his mothers in Ayodhya, the griefstricken Bharata who was firm in his vows, said to the elders:

192.sa: नन्दिग्रामं गमिष्यामि सर्वानामन्त्रयेऽद्य वः। तत्र दुःखमिदं सर्वं सहिष्ये राघवं विना।।2.115.2।।
192.e: I take leave of all of you. I am going to Nandigrama where I shall keep company with grief on account of Rama's absence.

192.sa: गतश्च वा दिवं राजा वनस्थश्च गुरुर्मम। रामं प्रतीक्षे राज्याय स हि राजा महायशाः।।2.115.3।।
192.e: King Dasaratha has gone to heaven. My elder brother and guru is in the forest. I shall await his return for ruling the kingdom since he alone is the illustrious king of Ayodhya.

192.sa: एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं भरतस्य महात्मनः। अब्रुवन्मन्त्रिणस्सर्वे वसिष्ठश्च पुरोहितः।।2.115.4।।
192.e: Hearing the auspicious words of the magnanimous Bharata the counsellors, priests including Vasistha replied:

192.sa: सुभृशं श्लाघनीयं च यदुक्तं भरत त्वया। वचनं भ्रातृवात्सल्यादनुरूपं तवैव तत्।।2.115.5।।
192.e: O Bharata, the words you have uttered out of devotion to your brother which befit you alone are highly praiseworthy.

192.sa: नित्यं ते बन्धुलुब्धस्य तिष्ठतो भ्रातृसौहृदे। आर्यमार्गं प्रपन्नस्य नानुमन्येत कः पुमान्।।2.115.6।।
192.e: You are always attached to your relations, firmly established in the welfare of your brothers and are pursuing a noble path. Who would not approve of this?

192.sa: मन्त्रिणां वचनं श्रुत्वा यथाभिलषितं प्रियम्। अब्रवीत्सारथिं वाक्यं रथो मे युज्यतामिति।।2.115.7।।
192.e: On hearing the pleasing words of the counsellors which were in conformity with his desire, Bharata said to his charioteer, 'Harness my chariot'.

192.sa: प्रहृष्टवदन स्सर्वा मातृ़ स्समभिवाद्य सः। आरुरोह रथं श्रीमान् शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः।।2.115.8।।
192.e: With a cheerful countenance illustrious Bharata paid obeisance to all his mothers and, acompanied by Satrughna, ascended the chariot.

192.sa: आरुह्य च रथं शीघ्रं शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ। ययतुः परमप्रीतौ वृतौ मन्त्रिपुरोहितैः।।2.115.9।।
192.e: Highly pleased, Bharata and Satrughna ascended the chariot and, surrounded by counsellors and priests, set out  speedily.

192.sa: अग्रतो गुरव: सर्वे वसिष्ठप्रमुखा द्विजाः। प्रययुः प्राङ्ग्मुखा स्सर्वे नन्दिग्रामो यतोऽभवत्।।2.115.10।।
192.e: Preceded by preceptors, like Vasistha and other brahmins, all of them proceeded eastward in the direction of Nandigrama.

192.sa: बलं च तदनाहूतं गजाश्वरथसङ्कुलम्। प्रययौ भरते याते सर्वे च पुरवासिनः।।2.115.11।।
192.e: When Bharata left, the army with hordes of elephants, horses and chariots and  inhabitants of Ayodhya  followed him unbidden.

192.sa: रथस्थः स तु धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। नन्दिग्रामं ययौ तूर्णं शिरस्यादाय पादुके।।2.115.12।।
192.e: Righteous Bharata who was deeply attached to his brother proceeded speedily towards Nandigrama on the chariot bearing the sandals of Rama on his head.

192.sa: ततस्तु भरतः क्षिप्रं नन्दिग्रामं प्रविश्य सः। अवतीर्य रथात्तूर्णं गुरूनिदमुवाच ह।।2.115.13।।
192.e: Bharata entered Nandigrama quickly, alighted from the chariot and then, addressing, the preceptors, said:

192.sa: एतद्राज्यं मम भ्रात्रा दत्तं सन्नयासवत्स्वयम्। योगक्षेमवहे चेमे पादुके हेमभूषिते।।2.115.14।।
192.e: My brother gave me this kingdom as a trust. He gave me the sandals decorated with gold for securing the prosperity and security (of the kingdom).

192.sa: भरत श्शिरसा कृत्वा सन्न्यासं पादुके ततः। अब्रवीद्धुःखसंतप्त स्सर्वं प्रकृतिमण्डलम्।।2.115.15।।
192.e: Then Bharata placed the sandals held in trust on his head and, overcome with grief, he addressed the concourse of subjects:

192.sa: छत्रं धारयत क्षिप्रमार्यपादाविमौ मतौ। आभ्यां राज्ये स्थितो धर्मः पादुकाभ्यां गुरोर्मम।।2.115.16।।
192.e: Hold the royal paresol now. This is the accepted symbol of the exalted feet of my brother. These sandals shall establish righteousness in the kingdom.

192.sa: भ्रात्रा हि मयि संन्यासो निक्षिप्त स्सौहृदादयम्। तमिमं पालयिष्यामि राघवागमनं प्रति।।2.115.17।।
192.e: This kingdom has been given me by my brother out of affection as a trust. I shall safeguard it until Rama's return.

192.sa: क्षिप्रं संयोजयित्वातु राघवस्य पुनस्स्वयम्। चरणौ तौ तु रामस्य द्रक्ष्यामि सहपादुकौ।।2.115.18।।
192.e: 'I myself shall see soon Rama's feet reunited with these sandals.

192.sa: ततो निक्षिप्तभारोऽहं राघवेण समागतः। निवेद्य गुरवे राज्यं भजिष्ये गुरुवृत्तिताम्।।2.115.19।।
192.e: The burden of this kingdom has been cast on me. On reunion with Rama, I shall hand it over to my brother, my guru and shall be engaged in his service.

192.sa: राघवाय च सन्यासं दत्त्वेमे वरपादुके। राज्यं चेदमयोध्यां च धूतपापो भवामि च।।2.115.20।।
192.e: Restoring the sacred sandals, the kingdom and this city of Ayodhya held as a trust by me, I shall be cleansed of the sin.

192.sa: अभिषिक्ते तु काकुत्स्थे प्रहृष्टमुदिते जने। प्रीतिर्मम यशश्चैव भवेद्राज्याच्चतुर्गुणम्।।2.115.21।।
192.e: After Rama is coronated and the people are delighted and pleased, the renown and pleasure for me will be fourfold (what is obtained from ruling the kingdom).

192.sa: एवं तु विलपन्दीनो भरत स्समहायशाः। नन्दिग्रामेऽकरोद्राज्यं दुःखितो मन्त्रिभिस्सह।।2.115.22।।
192.e: Thus lamenting in desolation and grief, the illustrious Bharata lived in Nandigrama along with his counsellors and started ruling the kingdom.

192.sa: स वल्कलजटाधारी मुनिवेषधरः प्रभुः। नन्दिग्रामेऽवसद्वीर स्ससैन्यो भरतस्तदा।।2.115.23।।
192.e: Bharata, the warrior and lord, wore bark garments and matted locks and lived the life of an ascetic in Nandigrama along with his army.

192.sa: रामागमनमाकाङ्क्षन्भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तथा।।2.115.24।। पादुके त्वभिषिच्याथ नन्दिग्रामेऽवसत्तदा।
192.e: Bharata who was attached to his brother and ever obedient to him, fulfilled his vow. He coronated the sandals and lived at Nandigrama longing for the return of Rama.

192.sa: स वालव्यजनं छत्रं धारयामास स स्वयं। भरत श्शासनं सर्वं पादुकाभ्यां निवेदयन्।।2.115.25।।
192.e: Bharata reported everything relating to the kingdom to the sandals first. Waving the chamaras (a fan made of yak tail) himself, he held the royal parasol over them.

192.sa: ततस्तु भरत शश्रीमानभिषिच्याऽऽर्यपादुके। तदधीनस्तदा राज्यं कारयामास सर्वदा।।2.115.26।।
192.e: After the coronation of the sandals of his esteemed brother Rama, illustrious Bharata ruled the kingdom, subordianating himself to them.

192.sa: तदा हि यत्कार्यमुपैति किञ्चिदुपायनं चोपहृतं महार्हम्। स पादुकाभ्यां प्रथमं निवेद्य चकार पश्चाद्भरतो यथावत्।।2.115.27।।
192.e: Whenever an issue, however small, arose, Bharata kept the sandals informed. Whenever a valuable gift was presented, he offered it to the sandals before he accepted it. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चदशोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredfifteenth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

193.sa: प्रतिप्रयाते भरते वसन्रामस्तपोवने। लक्षयामास सोद्वेगमथौत्सुक्यं तपस्विनाम्।।2.116.1।।
193.e: After Bharta, had departed, Rama who was living in the penancegrove of ascetics observed that the ascetics were filled with apprehensions, and were eager (to leave that forest).

193.sa: ये तत्र चित्रकूटस्य पुरस्तात्तापसाश्रमे। राममाश्रित्य निरतास्तानलक्षयदुत्सुकान्।।2.116.2।।
193.e: Rama observed that the sages who earlier sought to stay with him near his hermitage under his protection on chitrakuta were filled with anxiety (now).

193.sa: नयनैर्ब्रुकुटीभिश्च रामं निर्दिश्य शङ्किताः। अन्योन्यमुपजल्पन्त श्शनैश्चक्रुर्मिथः कथाः।।2.116.3।।
193.e: Those sages, glancing at Rama with suspicious eyes, knitting their eyebrows and murmering among themselves, conversed secretly.

193.sa: तेषामौत्सुक्यमालक्ष्य रामस्त्वात्मनि शङ्कितः। कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदमृषिं कुलपतिं ततः।।2.116.4।।
193.e: Having observed their anxiety, Rama apprehending somethig in his mind approached  the chief of the hermitage with folded palms and said:

193.sa: न कच्चिद्भगवन्किञ्चित्पूर्ववृत्तमिदं मयि। दृश्यते विकृतं येन विक्रियन्ते तपस्विनः।।2.116.5।।
193.e: O revered sire, have you seen any change in my conduct? For what reason are the sages looking perturbed?

193.sa: प्रमादाच्चरितं कच्चित्किञ्चिन्नावरजस्य मे। लक्ष्मणस्यर्षिभिदृष्टं नानुरूपमिवात्मनः।।2.116.6।।
193.e: Have the sages found my younger brother Lakshmana doing something unbecoming of him through inadvertence?

193.sa: कच्चिच्छुश्रूषमाणा व श्शुश्रूषणपरा मयि। प्रमदाऽभ्युचितां वृत्तिं सीता युक्तं न वर्तते।।2.116.7।।
193.e: Has Sita devoted in her service to me and engaged in serving you failed to follow the conduct befitting a woman?

193.sa: अथर्षिर्जरया वृद्धस्तपसा च जरां गतः। वेपमान इवोवाच रामं भूतदयापरम्।।2.116.8।।
193.e: Hearing those words, an ascetic old in age and austerities, as though trembling said  to Rama who is compassionate to all beings:

193.sa: कुतः कल्याणसत्त्वायाः कल्याणाभिरतेस्तथा। चलनं तात वैदेह्यास्तपस्विषु विशेषतः।।2.116.9।।
193.e: O dear child, how can goodnatured Sita who is always engaged in performing auspicious deeds, especially towards ascetics be associated with violation of duty?

193.sa: त्वन्निमित्तमिदं तावत्तापसान्प्रतिवर्तते। रक्षोभ्यस्तेन संविग्नाः कथयन्ति मिथः कथाः।।2.116.10।।
193.e: There is apprehension for ascetics from the demons on acount of your presence here. That is why they are conversing with one another about the likely fallout.

193.sa: रावणावरजः कश्चित् खरो नामेह राक्षसः। उत्पाट्य तापसान्सर्वाञ्जनस्थाननिकेतनान्।।2.116.11।। धृष्टश्च जितकाशी च नृशंसः पुरुषादकः। अवलिप्तश्च पापश्च त्वां च तात न मृष्यते।।2.116.12।।
193.e: O dear child, Khara, one of the brothers of Ravana is dwelling in nearby 'Janasthana'. He is impudent, reportedly winner of battles, cruel, sinful, a maneater and haughty. He has uprooted all the ascetics  from Janasthana. He will not tolerate even you.

193.sa: रावणावरजः कश्चित् खरो नामेह राक्षसः। उत्पाट्य तापसान्सर्वाञ्जनस्थाननिकेतनान्।।2.116.11।। धृष्टश्च जितकाशी च नृशंसः पुरुषादकः। अवलिप्तश्च पापश्च त्वां च तात न मृष्यते।।2.116.12।।
193.e: O dear child, Khara, one of the brothers of Ravana is dwelling in nearby 'Janasthana'. He is impudent, reportedly winner of battles, cruel, sinful, a maneater and haughty. He has uprooted all the ascetics  from Janasthana. He will not tolerate even you.

193.sa: त्वं यदाप्रभृति ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रमे तात वर्तसे। तदाप्रभृति रक्षांसि विप्रकुर्वन्ति तापसान्।।2.116.13।।
193.e: O dear child, ever since you started residing in this hermitage rakshasas have been  tormenting the ascetics.

193.sa: दर्शयन्ति हि बीभत्सैः क्रूरैर्भीषणकैरपि। नानारूपैर्विरूपैश्च रूपैर्विकृतदर्शनैः।।2.116.14।।
193.e: They appear in various distorted forms now rapacious, now fearful, now deformed.

193.sa: अप्रशस्तैशुचिभिस्सम्प्रयोज्य च तापसान्। प्रतिध्नन्त्यपरान्क्षिप्रमनार्याः पुरतः स्थिताः।।2.116.15।।
193.e: Those wicked rakshasas employ forbidden and dirty means against ascetics and kill them by suddenly appearing in front of them.

193.sa: तेषु तेष्वाश्रमस्थानेष्वबुद्धमवलीय च। रमन्ते तापसां स्तत्र नाशयन्तोऽल्पचेतसः।।2.116.16।।
193.e: These debased rakshasas, concealing themselves in various ashram sites take delight  in harassing and killing the ascetics.

193.sa: अपक्षिपन्ति स्रुग्भाण्डानग्नीस्निञ्चन्ति वारिणा। कलशांश्च प्रमध्नन्ति हवने समुपस्थिते।।2.116.17।।
193.e: When sacrifices are about to start, they throw away the sacrificial ladels and vessels containing sacrificial materials and sprinkle water on sacrificial fire. They also break down the earthen vessels used in the sacrifice.

193.sa: तैर्दुरात्मभिरामृष्टानाश्रमान्प्रजिहासवः। गमनायान्यदेशस्य चोदयन्त्यृषयोऽद्य माम्।।2.116.18।।
193.e: Now all these sages are urging me to abandon this hermitage infested by these wicked rakshasas and move to another region.

193.sa: तत्पुरा राम शारीरामुपहिंसां तपस्विषु। दर्शयन्ति हि दुष्टास्ते त्यक्ष्याम इममाश्रमम्।।2.116.19।।
193.e: O Rama, those vile creatures resort to physical violence against ascetics, we have therefore, resolved to quit this ashram.

193.sa: बहुमूलफलं चित्रमविदूरादितो वनम्। पुराणाश्रममेवाहं श्रयिष्ये सगणः पुनः।।2.116.20।।
193.e: Not very far from here stands an ancient ashram in a lovely forest abounding in roots and fruits and I with my companions will seek shelter there.

193.sa: खरस्त्वय्यपि चायुक्तं पुरा तात प्रवर्तते। सहास्माभिरितो गच्छ यदि बुद्धिः प्रवर्तते।।2.116.21।।
193.e: Dear child, Khara will also misbehave with you as usual. (Therefore), if you so decide you may come along with us.

193.sa: सकलत्रस्य सन्देहो नित्यं यत्तस्य राघव। समर्थस्यापि हि सतो वासो दुःखमिहाद्य ते।।2.116.22।।
193.e: O Rama, even though you are always vigilant and capable in all possible ways to defend youself, a doubt arises in our mind. It is perilous for you to live here with your wife.

193.sa: इत्युक्तवन्तं स्तंराम राजपुत्रस्तपस्विनम्। न शशाकोत्तरैर्वाक्यैरवरोद्धुं समुत्सुकम्।।2.116.23।।
193.e: It was not possible for prince Rama to hold back by mere words that ascetic who was saying like this and was anxious to quit the hermitage.

193.sa: अभिनन्द्य समापृच्छ्य समाधाय च राघवम्। स जगामाश्रमं त्यक्त्वा कुलैः कुलपतिस्सह।।2.116.24।।
193.e: The leader of the group quit the hermitage along with his companions after paying  respect to Rama, convincing him and taking leave of him.

193.sa: रामः संसाद्य ऋषिगणमनुगमनाद्देशात्तस्मात्कुलपतिमभिवाद्य ऋषिम्। सम्यक्प्रीतैस्तैरनुमत उपदिष्टार्थः पुण्यं वासाय स्वनिलयमुपसम्पेदे।।2.116.25।।
193.e: Rama, followed the sages for some distance to bid them farewell. He paid obeisance to the chief of the group and having grasped the instruction of the highly pleased  sages, he with their consent returned to his holy hermitage.

193.sa: आश्रममृषिविरहितं प्रभुः क्षणमपिन जहौ स राघवः। राघवं हि सततमनुगता स्तापसाश्चार्षचरित धृतगुणाः।।2.116.26।।
193.e: Lord Rama, did not leave that hermitage deserted by the sages even for a moment. Those who had adopted the traditions of the sages and  had acquired many virtues followed Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षोडशोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the hundredsixteenth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

194.sa: राघव स्त्वथ यातेषु तपस्विषु विचिन्तयन्। न तत्रारोचयद्वासं कारणैर्बहुभिस्तदा।।2.117.1।।
194.e: When the ascetics had departed, Rama thought over the matter well and did not like to reside there for many reasons.

194.sa: इह मे भरतो दृष्टो मातरश्च सनागराः। सा च मे स्मृतिरन्वेति तान्नित्यमनुशोचतः।।2.117.2।।
194.e: It is here that Bharata, mothers along with citizens of Ayodhya have visited me. That  memory soaked with grief is chasing me.

194.sa: स्कन्धावारनिवेशेन तेन तस्य महात्मनः। हयहस्तिकरीषैश्च उपमर्दः कृतो भृशम्।।2.117.3।।
194.e: Due to the encampment of the army of the magnanimous Bharata (here), this place has been filled with the dung of horses and elephants and made exceedingly dirty.

194.sa: तस्मादन्यत्र गच्छाम इति सञ्चिन्त्य राघवः। प्रातिष्ठत स वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च सङ्गतः।।2.117.4।।
194.e: We shall, therefore, go to some other place, having resolved thus, Rama accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana set forth.

194.sa: सोऽत्रेराश्रममासाद्य तं ववन्दे महायशाः। तं चापि भगवानत्रिः पुत्रवत्प्रत्यपद्यत।।2.117.5।।
194.e: Having reached the hermitage of the revered sage Atri, illustrious Rama prostrated before him and Atri also received him as his son.

194.sa: स्वयमातिथ्यमादिश्य सर्वमन्यत्सुसत्कृतम्। सौमित्रिं च महाभागां सीतां च समसान्त्वयत्।।2.117.6।।
194.e: That sage Atri himself extended to Rama the hospitality befitting him in all possible ways and treated Lakshmana and highly virtuous Sita with kind words.

194.sa: पत्नीं च समनुप्राप्तां वृद्धामामन्त्र्य सत्कृताम्। सान्त्वयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वभूतहिते रतः।।2.117.7।।
194.e: Conversant in the ways of righteousness and eagaged in the welfate of all beings, sage Atri called out his aged wife who is revered by all and spoke kind words to her.

194.sa: आनसूयां महाभागां तापसीं धर्मचारिणीम् प्रतिगृह्णीष्व वैदेहीमब्रवीदृषिसत्तमः। रामाय चाऽचचक्षे तां तापसीं धर्मचारिणीम्।।2.117.8।।
194.e: Atri, who was excellent among the sages said to his ascetic wife who was highly virtuous and an adherent of righteousness, Welcome Sita. Thereafter, he related to Rama a story about his asetic wife who follows the ways of righteousness.

194.sa: दश वर्षाण्यनावृष्ट्या दग्धे लोके निरन्तरम्।।2.117.9।। यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्तिता। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता नियमैश्चाप्यलङ्कृता।।2.117.10।। दश वर्ष सहास्राणि तया तप्तं महत्तपः। अनसूया व्रतै स्स्नाता प्रत्यूहाश्च निवर्तिताः।।2.117.11।। देवकार्यनिमित्तं च यया सन्त्वरमाणया। दशरात्रं कृता रात्रि स्सेयं मातेव तेऽनघ।।2.117.12।।
194.e: O blameless one (Rama), once this world was consecutively ravaged by drought for ten years. It was the virtuous Anasuya who created roots and fruits and caused Ganga to flow. She was engaged in severe mortifications and selfimposed religious observances. She practised severe asceticism for ten thousand years bathed in her vows. Solicited on behalf of the gods, she removed all impediments and converted ten nights into one. She is like a your mother to you.

194.sa: दश वर्षाण्यनावृष्ट्या दग्धे लोके निरन्तरम्।।2.117.9।। यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्तिता। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता नियमैश्चाप्यलङ्कृता।।2.117.10।। दश वर्ष सहास्राणि तया तप्तं महत्तपः। अनसूया व्रतै स्स्नाता प्रत्यूहाश्च निवर्तिताः।।2.117.11।। देवकार्यनिमित्तं च यया सन्त्वरमाणया। दशरात्रं कृता रात्रि स्सेयं मातेव तेऽनघ।।2.117.12।।
194.e: O blameless one (Rama), once this world was consecutively ravaged by drought for ten years. It was the virtuous Anasuya who created roots and fruits and caused Ganga to flow. She was engaged in severe mortifications and selfimposed religious observances. She practised severe asceticism for ten thousand years bathed in her vows. Solicited on behalf of the gods, she removed all impediments and converted ten nights into one. She is like a your mother to you.

194.sa: दश वर्षाण्यनावृष्ट्या दग्धे लोके निरन्तरम्।।2.117.9।। यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्तिता। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता नियमैश्चाप्यलङ्कृता।।2.117.10।। दश वर्षसहास्राणि यया तप्तं महत् तपः। अनसूया व्रतै स्स्नाता प्रत्यूहाश्च निवर्तिताः।।2.117.11।। देवकार्यनिमित्तं च यया सन्त्वरमाणया। दशरात्रं कृता रात्रि स्सेयं मातेव तेऽनघ।।2.117.12।।
194.e: O blameless one (Rama), once this world was consecutively ravaged by drought for ten years. It was the virtuous Anasuya who created roots and fruits and caused Ganga to flow. She was engaged in severe mortifications and selfimposed religious observances. She practised severe asceticism for ten thousand years bathed in her vows. Solicited on behalf of the gods, she removed all impediments and converted ten nights into one. She is like a your mother to you.

194.sa: दश वर्षाण्यनावृष्ट्या दग्धे लोके निरन्तरम्।।2.117.9।। यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्तिता। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता नियमैश्चाप्यलङ्कृता।।2.117.10।। दश वर्ष सहास्राणि तया तप्तं महत्तपः। अनसूया व्रतै स्स्नाता प्रत्यूहाश्च निवर्तिताः।।2.117.11।। देवकार्यनिमित्तं च यया सन्त्वरमाणया। दशरात्रं कृता रात्रि स्सेयं मातेव तेऽनघ।।2.117.12।।
194.e: O blameless one (Rama), once this world was consecutively ravaged by drought for ten years. It was the virtuous Anasuya who created roots and fruits and caused Ganga to flow. She was engaged in severe mortifications and selfimposed religious observances. She practised severe asceticism for ten thousand years bathed in her vows. Solicited on behalf of the gods, she removed all impediments and converted ten nights into one. She is like a your mother to you.

194.sa: तामिमां सर्वभूतानां नमस्कार्यां यशस्विनीम् अभिगच्छतु वैदेही वृद्धामक्रोधनां सदा। अनसूयेति या लोके कर्मभिः ख्यातिमागता।।2.117.13।।
194.e: 'She is renowned throughout this world for her deeds as Anasuya, (one who is free from anger). Aged, illustrious she is free frm anger, worthy of adoration by all beings. Let Sita approach her'.

194.sa: एवं ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं तथेत्युक्त्वा स राघवः। सीतामुवाच धर्मज्ञामिदं वचनमुत्तमम्।।2.117.14।।
194.e: Hearing those words of the sage, Rama said be it so and said to righteous Sita these choice words.

194.sa: राजपुत्रि श्रुतमिदं मुनेरस्य समीरितम्। श्रेयोऽर्थमात्मनश्शीघ्रमभिगच्छ तपस्विनीम्।।2.117.15।।
194.e: O princess, you have heard the message of the sage. Without delay approach the ascetic (Anasuya) for your welfare.

194.sa: सीता त्वेतद वचः श्रुत्वा राघवस्य हितैषिणः। तामत्रिपन्तीं धर्मज्ञामभिचक्राम मैथिली।।2.117.16।।
194.e: Having heard the words of Rama, intended for her welfare, Sita, daughter of the king of Mithila, approached the consort of Atri (Devi Anasuya), knower of righteousness, and reverently circumambulated her.

194.sa: शिथिलां वलितां वृद्धां जरापाण्डुरमूर्धजाम्। सततं वेपमानाङ्गीं प्रवाते कदलीं यथा।। 2.117.17।। तां तु सीता महाभागामनसूयां पतिव्रताम्। अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रा स्वं नाम समुदाहरत्।।2.117.18।।
